科学哲学：简明导论

Philosophy of Science: A Very Short Introduction

《极简入门》系列丛书旨在为希望以轻松有趣的方式了解新学科的读者提供帮助。该系列丛书由专家撰写，已被翻译成40多种语言。

VERY SHORT INTRODUCTIONS are for anyone wanting a stimulating and accessible way into a new subject. They are written by experts, and have been translated into more than 40 different languages.

该系列丛书始于1995年，如今已涵盖各个学科的众多主题。VSI丛书目前拥有超过450卷，从心理学和科学哲学到美国历史和相对论，无所不包，内容涵盖广泛，并且还在各个学科领域持续扩充。

The series began in 1995, and now covers a wide variety of topics in every discipline. The VSI library now contains over 450 volumes—a Very Short Introduction to everything from Psychology and Philosophy of Science to American History and Relativity—and continues to grow in every subject area.

第一章

Chapter 1

什么是科学？

What is science?

什么是科学？这个问题看似容易回答：人人都知道物理、化学和生物等学科属于科学，而艺术、音乐和神学等学科则不属于科学。但当我们作为哲学家追问“什么是科学”时，我们想要的答案并非如此。我们并非仅仅想要一份通常被称为“科学”的活动清单，而是想要探究清单上所有事物的共同特征，即是什么使它们成为科学。如此理解，我们的问题就远非那么简单了。

What is science? This question may seem easy to answer: everybody knows that subjects such as physics, chemistry, and biology constitute science, while subjects such as art, music, and theology do not. But when as philosophers we ask what science is, that is not the sort of answer we want. We are not asking for a mere list of the activities that are usually called ‘science’. Rather we are asking what common feature all the things on that list share, i.e. what it is that makes something a science. Understood this way, our question is not so trivial.

但你或许仍然认为这个问题相对简单明了。科学不就是试图理解、解释和预测我们所生活的世界吗？这当然是一个合理的答案。但这真的是全部真相吗？毕竟，各种宗教也试图理解和解释世界，但宗教通常不被视为科学的一个分支。同样，占星术和算命也是预测未来的尝试，但大多数人不会将这些活动描述为科学。再想想历史。历史学家试图理解和解释过去发生的事情，但历史通常被归类为人文学科，而非科学学科。正如许多哲学问题一样，“什么是科学？”这个问题远比乍看之下要复杂得多。

But you may still think the question is relatively straightforward. Surely science is just the attempt to understand, explain, and predict the world we live in? This is certainly a reasonable answer. But is it the whole story? After all, the various religions also attempt to understand and explain the world, but religion is not usually regarded as a branch of science. Similarly, astrology and fortune-telling are attempts to predict the future, but most people would not describe these activities as science. Or consider history. Historians try to understand and explain what happened in the past, but history is usually classified as a humanities subject not a science subject. As with many philosophical questions, the question ‘what is science?’ is trickier than it looks at first sight.

许多人认为，科学的显著特征在于科学家用来探索世界的独特方法。这种观点颇有道理。因为许多科学学科确实采用了非科学领域所不具备的独特研究方法。一个显而易见的例子就是实验的使用，它在历史上标志着现代科学发展的一个转折点。然而，并非所有科学都是实验性的——天文学家显然无法对天体进行实验，只能进行细致的观察。许多社会科学也是如此。科学的另一个重要特征是理论的构建。科学家并非仅仅将实验和观察的结果记录在日志中——他们通常希望用一个普遍的理论来解释这些结果。这并非易事，但也有一些令人瞩目的成功案例。科学哲学的主要任务之一，就是理解实验、观察和理论构建等技术是如何帮助科学家揭开自然界诸多奥秘的。

Many people believe that the distinguishing features of science lie in the particular methods scientists use to investigate the world. This suggestion is quite plausible. For many scientific disciplines do employ distinctive methods of enquiry that are not used in non-scientific enterprises. An obvious example is the use of experiments, which historically marks a turning-point in the development of modern science. Not all the sciences are experimental though—astronomers obviously cannot do experiments on the heavens, but have to content themselves with careful observation instead. The same is true of many social sciences. Another important feature of science is the construction of theories. Scientists do not simply record the results of experiment and observation in a log book—they usually want to explain those results in terms of a general theory. This is not always easy to do, but there have been some striking successes. One of the main tasks of philosophy of science is to understand how techniques such as experimentation, observation, and theory construction have enabled scientists to unravel so many of nature’s secrets.

现代科学的起源

The origins of modern science

在当今的中小学和大学里，科学教学很大程度上缺乏历史视角。教科书尽可能以最便捷的方式呈现某一科学学科的核心概念，却鲜少提及促成这些概念发现的漫长而曲折的历史进程。作为一种教学策略，这无可厚非。然而，对科学思想史有所了解，有助于理解科学哲学家们所关注的问题。事实上，正如我们将在第五章中看到的，有人认为，密切关注科学史对于做好科学哲学研究至关重要。

In today’s schools and universities, science is taught in a largely ahistorical way. Textbooks present the key ideas of a scientific discipline in as convenient a form as possible, with little mention of the lengthy and often tortuous historical process which led to their discovery. As a pedagogical strategy, this makes good sense. But some appreciation of the history of scientific ideas is helpful for understanding the issues that interest philosophers of science. Indeed as we shall see in Chapter 5, it has been argued that close attention to the history of science is indispensable for doing good philosophy of science.

现代科学的起源可以追溯到1500年至1750年间欧洲科学的快速发展时期，我们现在称之为科学革命。古代和中世纪也曾进行过科学研究——科学革命并非凭空而来。在这些早期时期，占主导地位的世界观是亚里士多德主义，它以古希腊哲学家亚里士多德的名字命名，亚里士多德提出了物理学、生物学、天文学和宇宙学方面的详尽理论。但亚里士多德的思想及其研究方法在现代科学家看来会非常怪异。举例来说，他认为所有物体都由四种元素组成：土、火、气和水。这种观点显然与现代化学的理论相悖。

The origins of modern science lie in a period of rapid scientific development that occurred in Europe between about 1500 and 1750, which we now refer to as the scientific revolution. Of course scientific investigations were pursued in ancient and medieval times too—the scientific revolution did not come from nowhere. In these earlier periods the dominant worldview was Aristotelianism, named after the ancient Greek philosopher Aristotle, who put forward detailed theories in physics, biology, astronomy, and cosmology. But Aristotle’s ideas would seem very strange to a modern scientist, as would his methods of enquiry. To pick just one example, he believed that all earthly bodies are composed of just four elements: earth, fire, air, and water. This view is obviously at odds with what modern chemistry tells us.

现代科学世界观发展的第一个关键步骤是哥白尼革命。1542年，波兰天文学家尼古拉·哥白尼（1473-1543）出版了一本书，抨击了地心宇宙模型。地心宇宙模型认为静止的地球位于宇宙中心，行星和太阳围绕地球运行。地心天文学，也称托勒密天文学（以古希腊天文学家托勒密的名字命名），是亚里士多德世界观的核心，并在1800年间几乎未受到挑战。但哥白尼提出了另一种方案：太阳是宇宙的固定中心，包括地球在内的行星围绕太阳运行（见图1）。在这种日心说模型中，地球被视为一颗普通的行星，因此失去了传统赋予它的独特地位。哥白尼的理论最初遭到了很多阻力，尤其是来自天主教会的阻力，他们认为这违背了圣经，并在1616年查禁了所有宣扬地球运动的书籍。但不到100年，哥白尼学派就成为了公认的科学正统观念。

The first crucial step in the development of the modern scientific worldview was the Copernican revolution. In 1542 the Polish astronomer Nicolas Copernicus (1473–1543) published a book attacking the geocentric model of the universe, which placed the stationary earth at the centre of the universe with the planets and the sun in orbit around it. Geocentric astronomy, also known as Ptolemaic astronomy after the ancient Greek astronomer Ptolemy, lay at the heart of the Aristotelian worldview, and had gone largely unchallenged for 1,800 years. But Copernicus suggested an alternative: the sun was the fixed centre of the universe, and the planets, including the earth, were in orbit around it (see Figure 1). On this heliocentric model the earth is regarded as just another planet, and so loses the unique status that tradition had accorded it. Copernicus’ theory initially met with much resistance, not least from the Catholic Church who regarded it as contravening the Scriptures, and in 1616 banned books advocating the earth’s motion. But within 100 years Copernicanism had become established scientific orthodoxy.

1.哥白尼的日心宇宙模型，显示包括地球在内的行星围绕太阳运行。

1. Copernicus’ heliocentric model of the universe, showing the planets, including the earth, orbiting the sun.

哥白尼的创新不仅促进了天文学的发展，也间接地推动了现代物理学的发展，这主要归功于约翰内斯·开普勒（1571-1630）和伽利略·伽利莱（1564-1642）的研究。开普勒发现，行星并非像哥白尼认为的那样绕太阳做圆形轨道运动，而是做椭圆轨道运动。这是他提出的行星运动“第一定律”；他的第二定律……第三定律规定了行星绕太阳公转的速度。开普勒定律共同构建了一套成功的行星理论，解决了困扰天文学家几个世纪的问题。伽利略终生拥护哥白尼宇宙论，也是望远镜的早期先驱之一。当他用望远镜观测星空时，他取得了一系列惊人的发现：月球上的山脉、浩瀚的星空、太阳黑子、木星的卫星等等。所有这些都与亚里士多德的宇宙论相悖，并在科学界转向哥白尼宇宙论的过程中发挥了关键作用。

Copernicus’ innovation did not merely lead to a better astronomy. Indirectly, it led to the development of modern physics, through the work of Johannes Kepler (1571–1630) and Galileo Galilei (1564–1642). Kepler discovered that the planets do not move in circular orbits around the sun, as Copernicus thought, but rather in ellipses. This was his ‘first law’ of planetary motion; his second and third laws specify the speeds at which the planets orbit the sun. Taken together, Kepler’s laws provided a successful planetary theory, solving problems that had confounded astronomers for centuries. Galileo was a lifelong supporter of Copernicanism and one of the early pioneers of the telescope. When he pointed his telescope at the heavens, he made a wealth of amazing discoveries: mountains on the moon, a vast array of stars, sun-spots, Jupiter’s moons, and more. All of these conflicted with Aristotelian cosmology, and played a pivotal role in converting the scientific community to Copernicanism.

然而，伽利略最持久的贡献并非在于天文学，而在于力学。他驳斥了亚里士多德关于重物比轻物下落速度更快的理论。伽利略提出了一个反直觉的观点来取代这一理论：所有物体的下落速度都相等。自由落体无论重量如何，都会以相同的速度落向地球。（当然，在实际中，如果你从同一高度同时扔下一根羽毛和一个炮弹，炮弹会先落地，但伽利略认为这仅仅是由于空气阻力造成的——在真空中，它们会同时落地。）此外，他还认为自由落体做匀加速运动，即在相等的时间内速度增加量相等；这就是著名的伽利略自由落体定律。伽利略为这一定律提供了令人信服但并非决定性的证据，而这一定律也构成了他力学的核心。

Galileo’s most enduring contribution, however, lay not in astronomy but in mechanics, where he refuted the Aristotelian theory that heavier bodies fall faster than lighter ones. In place of this theory, Galileo made the counter-intuitive suggestion that all freely falling bodies will fall towards the earth at the same rate, irrespective of their weight. (Of course in practice, if you drop a feather and a cannonball from the same height the cannonball will land first, but Galileo argued that this is simply due to air resistance—in a vacuum, they would land together.) Furthermore, he argued that freely falling bodies accelerate uniformly, i.e. gain equal increments of speed in equal times; this is known as Galileo’s law of free fall. Galileo provided persuasive though not conclusive evidence for this law, which formed the centrepiece of his mechanics.

伽利略通常被认为是第一位现代物理学家。他是第一个证明数学语言可以用来描述物质对象（例如落体和抛射体）行为的人。对我们来说，这似乎显而易见——如今的科学理论通常用数学语言表达，不仅在物理学领域，在生物科学和社会科学领域也是如此。但在伽利略的时代，这并非显而易见：数学被广泛认为是处理纯粹抽象概念的，因此不适用于物理现实。伽利略的另一个创新之处在于他强调通过实验检验假设。对现代科学家来说，这或许也是理所当然的。但在伽利略的时代，实验并不被普遍认为是获取知识的可靠途径。伽利略对实验的重视标志着一种研究自然的经验方法的开端，这种方法一直延续至今。

Galileo is generally regarded as the first modern physicist. He was the first to show that the language of mathematics could be used to describe the behaviour of material objects, such as falling bodies and projectiles. To us this seems obvious—today’s scientific theories are routinely formulated in mathematical language, not only in physics but also in the biological and social sciences. But in Galileo’s day it was not obvious: mathematics was widely regarded as dealing with purely abstract entities, hence inapplicable to physical reality. Another innovative aspect was Galileo’s emphasis on testing hypotheses experimentally. To the modern scientist this may again seem obvious. But in Galileo’s day experimentation was not generally regarded as a reliable means of gaining knowledge. Galileo’s emphasis on experiment marks the beginning of an empirical approach to studying nature that continues to this day.

伽利略去世后的时期，科学革命迅速发展。法国哲学家兼科学家勒内·笛卡尔（1596-1650）发展出一种全新的“机械论哲学”，该哲学认为物理世界由相互作用和碰撞的惰性物质粒子构成。笛卡尔相信，支配这些粒子或“微粒”运动的规律是理解宇宙结构的关键。机械论哲学承诺用这些微粒的运动来解释所有可观测的现象，并迅速成为主流哲学。这是17世纪晚期的科学思想，在某种程度上，它至今仍然存在。惠更斯、伽桑狄、胡克和波义耳等人都曾拥护过机械论哲学；它的被接受标志着亚里士多德世界观的最终衰落。

The period following Galileo’s death saw the scientific revolution rapidly gain in momentum. The French philosopher-scientist René Descartes (1596–1650) developed a radical new ‘mechanical philosophy’, according to which the physical world consists of inert particles of matter interacting and colliding with one another. The laws governing the motion of these particles or ‘corpuscles’ held the key to understanding the structure of the universe, Descartes believed. The mechanical philosophy promised to explain all observable phenomena in terms of the motions of these corpuscles, and quickly became the dominant scientific vision of the late 17th century; to some extent it is still with us today. Versions of the mechanical philosophy were espoused by figures such as Huygens, Gassendi, Hooke, and Boyle; its acceptance marked the final downfall of the Aristotelian worldview.

科学革命在艾萨克·牛顿（1643-1727）的著作中达到顶峰，他的杰作《自然哲学的数学原理》于1687年出版。

The scientific revolution culminated in the work of Isaac Newton (1643–1727), whose masterpiece, Mathematical Principles of Natural Philosophy, was published in 1687.

牛顿认同机械哲学家的观点，认为宇宙仅仅由运动的粒子构成，并致力于改进笛卡尔的理论。最终，他建立了一套强大的动力学和力学理论，其核心是牛顿三大运动定律和著名的万有引力原理。根据这一原理，宇宙中任何物体都对其他物体施加引力；两个物体之间的引力大小取决于它们的质量乘积与它们之间距离的平方。运动定律则阐明了这种引力如何影响物体的运动。牛顿以惊人的精确性和严谨性完善了他的理论，并发明了我们现在称之为“微积分”的数学方法。值得注意的是，牛顿证明了开普勒的行星运动定律和伽利略的自由落体定律（经过一些细微的修正）都是他的运动定律和万有引力定律的逻辑推论。因此，一套单一的定律可以解释地球和天体中物体的运动，并且由牛顿以精确的定量形式表述出来。

Newton agreed with the mechanical philosophers that the universe consists simply of particles in motion, and sought to improve on Descartes’s theory. The result was a dynamical and mechanical theory of great power, based around Newton’s three laws of motion and his famous principle of universal gravitation. According to this principle, every body in the universe exerts a gravitational attraction on every other body; the strength of the attraction between two bodies depends on the product of their masses, and on the distance between them squared. The laws of motion then specify how this gravitational force affects the bodies’ motions. Newton elaborated his theory with remarkable precision and rigour, inventing the mathematical techniques we now call ‘calculus’. Strikingly, Newton was able to show that Kepler’s laws of planetary motion and Galileo’s law of free fall (both with certain minor modifications) were logical consequences of his laws of motion and gravitation. So a single set of laws could explain the motions of bodies in both terrestrial and celestial domains, and were formulated by Newton in a precise quantitative form.

牛顿物理学为接下来的两百年科学发展奠定了基础，迅速取代了笛卡尔物理学。在此期间，科学信心迅速增长，这主要归功于牛顿理论的成功。人们普遍认为牛顿理论揭示了自然界的真正运行规律，并且至少在原则上能够解释一切。人们进行了大量的尝试，试图将牛顿的解释模式扩展到越来越多的领域。现象。18世纪和19世纪都见证了显著的科学进步，尤其是在化学、光学、热力学和电磁学领域。但总的来说，这些发展被认为符合牛顿宇宙观的框架。科学家们普遍接受牛顿的宇宙观，认为其基本正确；剩下的工作就是完善细节。

Newtonian physics provided the framework for science for the next 200 years, quickly replacing Cartesian physics. Scientific confidence grew rapidly in this period, due largely to the success of Newton’s theory, which was widely believed to have revealed the true workings of nature, and to be capable of explaining everything, in principle at least. Detailed attempts were made to extend the Newtonian mode of explanation to more and more phenomena. The 18th and 19th centuries both saw notable scientific advances, particularly in chemistry, optics, thermodynamics, and electromagnetism. But for the most part, these developments were regarded as falling within a broadly Newtonian conception of the universe. Scientists accepted Newton’s conception as essentially correct; what remained to be done was to fill in the details.

20世纪初，物理学领域的两项革命性新进展——相对论和量子力学——动摇了人们对牛顿力学的信心。爱因斯坦发现的相对论表明，牛顿力学在应用于质量极大的物体或高速运动的物体时，无法给出正确的结果。相反，量子力学则表明，牛顿理论在应用于亚原子粒子等极小尺度时也失效了。相对论和量子力学，尤其是后者，都是奇异而激进的理论，它们对现实本质的论断与常识相悖，许多人难以接受甚至理解。它们的出现给物理学带来了巨大的概念性变革，这种变革至今仍在持续。

Confidence in the Newtonian picture was shattered in the early years of the 20th century, thanks to two revolutionary new developments in physics: relativity theory and quantum mechanics. Relativity theory, discovered by Einstein, showed that Newtonian mechanics does not give the right results when applied to very massive objects, or objects moving at very high velocities. Quantum mechanics, conversely, shows that the Newtonian theory does not work when applied on a very small scale, to subatomic particles. Both relativity theory and quantum mechanics, especially the latter, are strange and radical theories, making claims about the nature of reality which conflict with common sense, and which many people find hard to accept or even understand. Their emergence caused considerable conceptual upheaval in physics, which continues to this day.

到目前为止，我们对科学史的简要概述主要集中在物理学上。这并非偶然，因为物理学不仅在历史上举足轻重，而且在某种意义上也是最基础的科学学科。其他科学研究的对象本身也是由物理实体构成的，反之则不然。以植物学为例。植物学家研究植物，植物由细胞构成，细胞又由生物分子构成，生物分子最终由原子构成，而原子是物理粒子。因此，植物学研究的实体不如物理学那样“基础”——但这并不意味着它不重要。这一点我们将在第三章中再次讨论。但是，即使是对现代科学起源的简要描述，如果忽略了非物理科学，也是不完整的。

So far our brief account of the history of science has focused mainly on physics. This is no accident, as physics is both historically important and in a sense the most fundamental scientific discipline. For the objects that other sciences study are themselves made up of physical entities, but not vice versa. Consider botany, for example. Botanists study plants, which are composed of cells, which are themselves composed of bio-molecules, which are ultimately made up of atoms, which are physical particles. So botany deals with entities that are less ‘fundamental’ than does physics—though that is not to say it is less important. This is a point we shall return to in Chapter 3. But even a brief description of modern science’s origins would be incomplete if it omitted all mention of the non-physical sciences.

在生物学领域，最引人注目的事件莫过于查尔斯·达尔文于1859年发表的《物种起源》一书，书中阐述了自然选择进化论。在此之前，人们普遍认为不同的物种是上帝按照《创世记》的记载分别创造的。但达尔文认为，现存物种实际上是通过自然选择这一过程，从祖先物种进化而来。自然选择是指某些生物体因其生理特征而比其他生物体留下更多后代；如果这些特征被后代继承，随着时间的推移，种群就会越来越适应环境。达尔文指出，尽管这个过程看似简单，但经过无数代，它可以使一个物种进化成一个全新的物种。达尔文为他的理论提出的证据如此令人信服，以至于到20世纪初，尽管遭到了相当大的神学反对，它仍然被奉为科学正统。后来的研究为达尔文的理论提供了令人信服的佐证，该理论也构成了现代生物学世界观的核心。

In biology, the event that stands out is Charles Darwin’s discovery of the theory of evolution by natural selection, published in The Origin of Species in 1859. Until then it was widely believed that the different species had been separately created by God, as the Book of Genesis teaches. But Darwin argued that contemporary species have actually evolved from ancestral ones, through a process known as natural selection. Natural selection occurs when some organisms leave more offspring than others, depending on their physical characteristics; if these characteristics are then inherited by their offspring, over time the population will become better and better adapted to the environment. Simple though this process is, over a large number of generations it can cause one species to evolve into a wholly new one, Darwin argued. So persuasive was the evidence Darwin adduced for his theory that by the start of the 20th century it was accepted as scientific orthodoxy, despite considerable theological opposition. Subsequent work has provided striking confirmation of Darwin’s theory, which forms the centrepiece of the modern biological worldview.

20世纪见证了生物学领域另一场尚未完成的革命：分子生物学和遗传学的兴起。1953年，沃森和克里克发现了DNA的结构，DNA是构成生物细胞基因的遗传物质（见图2）。沃森和克里克的发现解释了遗传信息如何在细胞间复制，从而从亲代传递给子代，进而解释了为什么子代往往与父母相似。他们的发现开辟了一个令人兴奋的生物学研究新领域——分子生物学，该领域研究生物现象的分子基础。自沃森和克里克的研究以来的六十年间，分子生物学发展迅猛，彻底改变了我们对遗传、发育和其他核心生物过程的理解。2003年，历时十年、旨在提供人类全部基因组分子水平描述的人类基因组计划终于完成。虽然这项技术已经完成，但其对医学和生物技术的影响才刚刚开始被探索。21世纪，该领域很可能会出现更多令人振奋的发展。

The 20th century witnessed another revolution in biology that is not yet complete: the emergence of molecular biology and genetics. In 1953 Watson and Crick discovered the structure of DNA, the hereditary material that makes up the genes in the cells of living creatures (see Figure 2). Watson and Crick’s discovery explained how genetic information can be copied from one cell to another, and thus passed down from parent to offspring, thereby explaining why offspring tend to resemble their parents. Their discovery opened up an exciting new area of biological research known as molecular biology, which studies the molecular basis of biological phenomena. In the sixty years since Watson and Crick’s work, molecular biology has grown fast, transforming our understanding of heredity, development, and other core biological processes. In 2003, the decade-long attempt to provide a molecular-level description of the complete set of genes in a human being, known as the Human Genome Project, was finally completed; the implications for medicine and biotechnology have only begun to be explored. The 21st century will most likely see further exciting developments in this field.

2.詹姆斯·沃森和弗朗西斯·克里克发现了著名的“双螺旋”——这是他们于 1953 年发现的 DNA 结构的分子模型。

2. James Watson and Francis Crick with the famous ‘double helix’—their molecular model of the structure of DNA, discovered in 1953.

过去六十年间，投入科学研究的资源比以往任何时候都多。其成果之一是计算机科学、人工智能和神经科学等新兴学科的蓬勃发展。20世纪后期，认知科学兴起，它研究人类认知的各个方面，包括感知、记忆和推理，并彻底改变了传统心理学。认知科学的兴起很大程度上源于这样一种观点：人类的心智在某种程度上是不可预测的。人类的思维方式与计算机有相似之处，可以通过将其与计算机的运算进行比较来理解人类的思维过程。相比之下，神经科学则研究大脑本身的运作方式。得益于脑部扫描技术的进步，神经科学家们开始了解人类（以及动物）认知背后的神经基础。这项研究本身就具有巨大的意义，并且可能有助于改进精神疾病的治疗方法。

More resources have been devoted to scientific research in the last sixty years than ever before. One result has been an explosion of new scientific disciplines, such as computer science, artificial intelligence, and neuroscience. The late 20th century witnessed the rise of cognitive science, which studies aspects of human cognition including perception, memory, and reasoning, and has transformed traditional psychology. Much of the impetus for cognitive science comes from the idea that the human mind is in some respects similar to a computer, and that human mental processes can be understood by comparing them to the operations computers carry out. By contrast, the field of neuroscience studies how the brain itself works. Thanks to technological advances in brain scanning, neuroscientists are beginning to understand the underlying neural basis of human (and animal) cognition. This enterprise is of great intrinsic interest and may also lead to improved treatments for mental disorders.

经济学、人类学和社会学等社会科学在20世纪也蓬勃发展，尽管有人认为它们在复杂性和预测能力方面落后于自然科学。这就引出了一个有趣的方法论问题：社会科学家是否应该尝试使用与自然科学家相同的方法，还是说他们的研究对象需要不同的方法？我们将在第七章再次探讨这个问题。

The social sciences, such as economics, anthropology, and sociology, also flourished in the 20th century, though some believe they lag behind the natural sciences in terms of sophistication and predictive power. This raises an interesting methodological question. Should social scientists try to use the same methods as natural scientists, or does their subject matter call for a different approach? We return to this issue in Chapter 7.

什么是科学哲学？

What is philosophy of science?

科学哲学的主要任务是分析科学研究中使用的探究方法。你或许会疑惑，为什么这项任务应该由哲学家承担，而不是科学家自己？这是一个很好的问题。部分答案在于，哲学反思能够揭示科学探究中隐含的假设。举例来说，假设一位科学家做了一个实验，并得到了某个特定的结果。他重复实验几次，每次都得到相同的结果。之后，他很可能会停止实验，因为他确信，如果在完全相同的条件下再次重复实验，结果仍然会相同。这个假设看似显而易见，但作为哲学家，我们却想要质疑它。为什么会假设未来的实验重复会得到相同的结果？我们如何知道这是真的？科学家不太可能花太多时间思考这个问题：他们可能还有更重要的事情要做。这是一个典型的哲学问题。

The principal task of philosophy of science is to analyse the methods of enquiry used in the sciences. You may wonder why this task should fall to philosophers, rather than to the scientists themselves. This is a good question. Part of the answer is that philosophical reflection can uncover assumptions that are implicit in scientific enquiry. To illustrate, consider experimental practice. Suppose a scientist does an experiment and gets a particular result. They repeat the experiment a few times and keep getting the same result. After that they will probably stop, confident that were the experiment repeated again under exactly the same conditions, the same result would obtain. This assumption may seem obvious, but as philosophers we want to question it. Why assume that future repetitions of the experiment will yield the same result? How do we know this is true? The scientist is unlikely to spend much time puzzling over this: they probably have better things to do. It is a quintessentially philosophical question.

因此，科学哲学的部分工作在于质疑科学家们习以为常的假设。但如果就此断言科学家从不讨论哲学问题，那就错了。事实上，从历史上看，科学家在科学哲学的发展中扮演了关键角色。笛卡尔、牛顿和爱因斯坦就是杰出的例证。他们都对科学应该如何发展、应该采用何种研究方法以及科学知识是否存在局限性等问题抱有浓厚的兴趣。这些问题至今仍是当代科学哲学的核心。因此，科学哲学家所关注的问题也吸引了一些最伟大的科学家的目光。话虽如此，我们必须承认，如今许多科学家对科学哲学兴趣寥寥，知之甚少。这固然令人遗憾，但这并不意味着哲学问题不再重要。相反，这是科学日益专业化以及现代教育中科学与人文学科日益分化的结果。

So part of the job of philosophy of science is to question assumptions that scientists take for granted. But it would be wrong to imply that scientists never discuss philosophical issues themselves. Indeed historically, scientists have played a key role in the development of philosophy of science. Descartes, Newton, and Einstein are prominent examples. Each was deeply interested in questions about how science should proceed, what methods of enquiry it should use, and whether there are limits to scientific knowledge. These questions still lie at the heart of contemporary philosophy of science. So the issues that concern philosophers of science have engaged the attention of some of the greatest scientists. That being said, it must be admitted that many scientists today take little interest in philosophy of science, and know little about it. While this is unfortunate, it is not an indication that philosophical issues are no longer relevant. Rather it is a consequence of the increasingly specialized nature of science, and of the polarization between the sciences and the humanities that characterizes much modern education.

你或许仍然不明白科学哲学究竟是什么。仅仅说它“研究科学方法”其实并不全面。与其试图给出一个更详尽的定义，我们不如探讨一下科学哲学中的一个经典问题。

You may still be wondering exactly what philosophy of science is all about. For to say that it ‘studies the methods of science’ is not really to say very much. Rather than try to provide a more informative definition, we will instead examine a classic issue in the philosophy of science.

科学与伪科学

Science and pseudo-science

回想一下我们一开始提出的问题：什么是科学？20世纪极具影响力的科学哲学家卡尔·波普尔认为，科学理论的基本特征是可证伪性。称一个理论可证伪，并非意味着它是错误的。而是指该理论能够做出一些明确的预测，这些预测可以通过经验进行检验。如果这些预测最终被证明是错误的，那么该理论就被证伪了。因此，可证伪的理论是指……可能会被证明是错误的——它并非与所有可能的经验相符。波普尔认为，一些所谓的科学理论并不符合这一条件，因此根本不配被称为科学；它们仅仅是伪科学。

Recall the question with which we began: what is science? Karl Popper, an influential 20th-century philosopher of science, thought that the fundamental feature of a scientific theory is that it should be falsifiable. To call a theory falsifiable is not to say that it is false. Rather, it means that the theory makes some definite predictions which are capable of being tested against experience. If these predictions turn out to be wrong, then the theory has been falsified, or disproved. So a falsifiable theory is one which we might discover to be false—it is not compatible with every possible course of experience. Popper thought that some supposedly scientific theories did not satisfy this condition and thus did not deserve to be called science at all; they were merely pseudo-science.

弗洛伊德的精神分析理论是波普尔最喜欢的伪科学例子之一。波普尔认为，弗洛伊德的理论可以与任何经验发现相吻合。无论病人的行为如何，弗洛伊德主义者都能用他们的理论找到解释——他们永远不会承认自己的理论是错误的。波普尔用以下例子来说明他的观点。想象一下，一个人把一个孩子推进河里，意图谋杀他；另一个人为了救孩子而牺牲了自己的生命。弗洛伊德主义者可以同样轻松地解释这两个人的行为：前者是压抑，后者是升华。波普尔认为，通过使用压抑、升华和无意识欲望等概念，弗洛伊德的理论可以与任何临床数据相兼容；因此，它是无法证伪的。

Freud’s psychoanalytic theory was one of Popper’s favourite examples of pseudo-science. According to Popper, Freud’s theory could be reconciled with any empirical findings whatsoever. Whatever a patient’s behaviour, Freudians could find an explanation of it in terms of their theory—they would never admit that their theory was wrong. Popper illustrated his point with the following example. Imagine a man who pushes a child into a river with the intention of murdering him, and another man who sacrifices his life in order to save the child. Freudians can explain both men’s behaviour with equal ease: the first was repressed, and the second had achieved sublimation. Popper argued that through the use of such concepts as repression, sublimation, and unconscious desires, Freud’s theory could be rendered compatible with any clinical data whatever; it was thus unfalsifiable.

波普尔认为，马克思的历史理论也存在同样的问题。马克思声称，在世界各地的工业化社会中，资本主义终将让位于社会主义，最终走向共产主义。但当这种情况没有发生时，马克思主义者非但不承认马克思的理论是错误的，反而会编造出一套临时性的解释，来证明实际发生的情况与他们的理论完全吻合。例如，他们可能会说，福利国家的兴起暂时延缓了通往共产主义的必然进程，福利国家“软化”了无产阶级，削弱了他们的革命热情。如此一来，马克思的理论就像弗洛伊德的理论一样，可以与任何可能的历史进程相兼容。因此，按照波普尔的标准，这两种理论都不能算是真正科学的。

The same was true of Marx’s theory of history, Popper maintained. Marx claimed that in industrialized societies around the world, capitalism would give way to socialism and ultimately to communism. But when this didn’t happen, instead of admitting that Marx’s theory was wrong, Marxists would invent an ad hoc explanation for why what had happened was actually perfectly consistent with their theory. For example, they might say that the inevitable progress to communism had been temporarily slowed by the rise of the welfare state, which ‘softened’ the proletariat and weakened their revolutionary zeal. In this way, Marx’s theory could be made compatible with any possible course of events, just like Freud’s. Therefore neither theory qualifies as genuinely scientific, according to Popper’s criterion.

波普尔将弗洛伊德和马克思的理论与爱因斯坦的引力理论（即广义相对论）进行了对比。与弗洛伊德不同的是……与马克思的理论相比，爱因斯坦的理论做出了一个非常明确的预言：来自遥远恒星的光线会被太阳的引力场偏转。通常情况下，这种效应是无法观测到的——除非是在日食期间。1919年，英国天体物理学家亚瑟·爱丁顿爵士组织了两次考察，分别前往巴西和位于非洲大西洋沿岸的普林西比岛，以观测当年的日食，目的是为了验证爱因斯坦的预言。考察队发现，星光确实被太阳偏转，偏转的程度几乎与爱因斯坦的预言完全一致。波普尔对此印象深刻。爱因斯坦的理论做出了一个明确而精确的预言，并得到了观测的证实。如果观测结果表明星光并没有被太阳偏转，那就证明爱因斯坦的理论是错误的。因此，爱因斯坦的理论符合可证伪性的标准。

Popper contrasted Freud’s and Marx’s theories with Einstein’s theory of gravitation, known as general relativity. Unlike Freud’s and Marx’s theories, Einstein’s theory made a very definite prediction: that light rays from distant stars would be deflected by the gravitational field of the sun. Normally this effect would be impossible to observe—except during a solar eclipse. In 1919 the English astrophysicist Sir Arthur Eddington organized two expeditions to observe the solar eclipse of that year, one to Brazil and one to the island of Principe off the Atlantic coast of Africa, with the aim of testing Einstein’s prediction. The expeditions found that starlight was indeed deflected by the sun, by almost exactly the amount Einstein had predicted. Popper was very impressed by this. Einstein’s theory had made a definite, precise prediction, which was confirmed by observations. Had it turned out that starlight was not deflected by the sun, this would have shown that Einstein was wrong. So Einstein’s theory satisfies the criterion of falsifiability.

波普尔试图区分科学与伪科学，这在直觉上是相当合理的。一个理论如果能够随意拟合任何经验数据，那它肯定存在一些可疑之处。但许多哲学家认为波普尔的标准过于简单化。波普尔批评弗洛伊德主义者和马克思主义者，认为他们不愿承认自己的理论已被驳斥，而是试图用各种解释来掩盖任何看似与其理论相悖的数据。这看起来确实是一种可疑的做法。然而，有证据表明，一些“受人尊敬”的科学家——波普尔不会想指责他们从事伪科学——也经常使用这种方法，而且这种方法还促成了一些重要的科学发现。

Popper’s attempt to demarcate science from pseudo-science is intuitively quite plausible. There is surely something suspicious about a theory that can be made to fit any empirical data whatsoever. But many philosophers regard Popper’s criterion as overly simplistic. Popper criticized Freudians and Marxists for explaining away any data which appeared to conflict with their theories, rather than accepting that the theories had been refuted. This certainly looks like a dubious procedure. However there is some evidence that this very procedure is routinely used by ‘respectable’ scientists—whom Popper would not want to accuse of engaging in pseudo-science—and has led to important scientific discoveries.

另一个天文例子可以说明这一点。我们之前提到的牛顿万有引力理论预测了行星绕太阳运行的轨道。这些预测大多与观测结果相符。然而，天王星的观测轨道却始终与牛顿理论的预测存在偏差。这个谜题最终在1846年由两位科学家——英国的亚当斯和美国的勒维耶——解开。在法国，亚当斯和勒维耶独立开展研究。他们提出，可能存在另一颗尚未被发现的行星，对天王星施加着额外的引力。亚当斯和勒维耶计算出了这颗行星的质量和位置，以证明其引力确实是造成天王星异常行为的原因。不久之后，海王星被发现，其位置几乎与亚当斯和勒维耶的预测完全吻合。

Another astronomical example can illustrate this. Newton’s gravitational theory, which we encountered earlier, made predictions about the paths the planets should follow as they orbit the sun. For the most part these predictions were borne out by observation. However, the observed orbit of Uranus consistently differed from what Newton’s theory predicted. This puzzle was solved in 1846 by two scientists, Adams in England and Leverrier in France, working independently. They suggested that there was another planet, as yet undiscovered, exerting an additional gravitational force on Uranus. Adams and Leverrier were able to calculate the mass and position that this planet would have to have if its gravitational pull was indeed responsible for Uranus’ strange behaviour. Shortly afterwards the planet Neptune was discovered, almost exactly where Adams and Leverrier predicted.

显然，我们不应该批评亚当斯和勒维耶的行为是“不科学的”——毕竟，他们的行为最终发现了一颗新行星。但他们的做法恰恰与波普尔批评马克思主义者的做法如出一辙。他们从一个理论——牛顿的万有引力理论——出发，而该理论对天王星的轨道做出了错误的预测。他们并没有得出结论认为牛顿的理论一定是错误的，而是坚持己见，试图通过假设存在一颗新行星来解释相互矛盾的观测结果。同样地，当资本主义没有表现出向共产主义过渡的迹象时，马克思主义者也没有得出结论认为马克思的理论一定是错误的，而是坚持己见，试图用其他方式来解释相互矛盾的观测结果。那么，如果我们承认亚当斯和勒维耶的行为是优秀的、甚至是堪称典范的科学，那么指责马克思主义者从事伪科学岂不是有失偏颇吗？

Now clearly we should not criticize Adams’s and Leverrier’s behaviour as ‘unscientific’—after all, it led to the discovery of a new planet. But they did precisely what Popper criticized the Marxists for doing. They began with a theory—Newton’s theory of gravity—which made an incorrect prediction about Uranus’ orbit. Rather than concluding that Newton’s theory must be wrong, they stuck by the theory and attempted to explain away the conflicting observations by postulating a new planet. Similarly, when capitalism showed no signs of giving way to communism, Marxists did not conclude that Marx’s theory must be wrong, but stuck by the theory and tried to explain away the conflicting observations in other ways. So surely it is unfair to accuse Marxists of engaging in pseudo-science if we allow that what Adams and Leverrier did counted as good, indeed exemplary, science?

这表明，尽管波普尔试图区分科学与伪科学的做法乍看之下似乎合情合理，但实际上可能并不完全正确。因为亚当斯/勒维耶的例子绝非个例。一般来说，科学家不会仅仅因为理论与观测数据相冲突就放弃它们。通常，他们会寻找在不放弃理论的前提下消除冲突的方法；参见第五章。此外，值得注意的是，几乎所有科学理论都与某些观测结果相冲突——找到一个能够完美契合所有数据的理论极其困难。显然，如果一个理论持续与越来越多的数据相冲突，并且找不到任何合理的解释来消除这种冲突，那么它最终必然会被否定。但即便如此，也难以取得多少进展。如果科学家们一遇到困难就放弃自己的理论，就会造成这样的结果。

This suggests that Popper’s attempt to demarcate science from pseudo-science cannot be quite right, despite its initial plausibility. For the Adams/Leverrier example is by no means atypical. In general, scientists do not just abandon their theories whenever they conflict with the observational data. Usually they look for ways of eliminating the conflict without having to give up their theory; see Chapter 5. Also, it is worth remembering that virtually every scientific theory conflicts with some observations—finding a theory that fits all the data perfectly is extremely difficult. Obviously if a theory persistently conflicts with more and more data, and no plausible way of explaining away the conflict is found, it will eventually have to be rejected. But little progress would be made if scientists simply abandoned their theories at the first sign of trouble.

波普尔划界标准的失败引出了一个重要问题：我们是否真的能够找到某种共同特征，这种特征只存在于我们称之为“科学”的事物之中？波普尔认为答案是肯定的。他认为弗洛伊德和马克思的理论显然是不科学的，因此必然存在某种它们所缺乏而真正的科学理论所具备的特征。但是，无论我们是否接受波普尔对弗洛伊德和马克思的否定评价，他关于科学具有“本质”的假设都值得商榷。毕竟，科学是一种异质性活动，涵盖了广泛的学科和理论。它们或许共享一些定义科学本质的固定特征，但也未必如此。哲学家路德维希·维特根斯坦认为，并不存在一套固定的特征来定义“游戏”的本质。相反，大多数游戏都具备一系列松散的特征。但任何一款游戏都可能缺少集群中的某些特征，却仍然是一款游戏。科学也可能如此。如果真是如此，那么恐怕很难找到一个简单的标准来区分科学和伪科学。

The failure of Popper’s demarcation criterion throws up an important question. Is it actually possible to find some common feature shared by all and only the things we call ‘science’? Popper assumed that the answer was yes. He felt that Freud’s and Marx’s theories were clearly unscientific, so there must be some feature which they lack and which genuine scientific theories possess. But whether or not we accept Popper’s negative assessment of Freud and Marx, his assumption that science has an ‘essential nature’ is questionable. After all, science is a heterogeneous activity, encompassing a wide range of disciplines and theories. It may be that they share some fixed set of features which define what it is to be a science, but it may not. The philosopher Ludwig Wittgenstein argued that there is no fixed set of features that define what it is to be a ‘game’. Rather there is a loose cluster of features most of which are possessed by most games. But any particular game may lack any of the features in the cluster and still be a game. The same may be true of science. If so, a simple criterion for demarcating science from pseudo-science is unlikely to be found.

第二章

Chapter 2

科学推断

Scientific inference

科学家常常告诉我们一些我们原本不会相信的世界真相。例如，生物学家告诉我们，我们与黑猩猩有着密切的亲缘关系；地质学家告诉我们，非洲和南美洲曾经连在一起；宇宙学家告诉我们，宇宙正在膨胀。但是，科学家们是如何得出这些听起来匪夷所思的结论的呢？毕竟，没有人亲眼见过一个物种从另一个物种进化而来，也没有人亲眼见过一块大陆分裂成两块，更没有人亲眼见过宇宙变大。答案当然是，科学家们是通过推理或推断的过程得出这些结论的。但是，如果我们能更深入地了解这个过程，那就太好了。科学推断的本质究竟是什么呢？

Scientists often tell us things about the world that we would not otherwise have believed. For example, biologists tell us that we are closely related to chimpanzees, geologists tell us that Africa and South America used to be joined together, and cosmologists tell us that the universe is expanding. But how did scientists reach these unlikely sounding conclusions? After all, no one has ever seen one species evolve from other, or a single continent split into two, or the universe getting bigger. The answer, of course, is that scientists arrived at these beliefs by a process of reasoning or inference. But it would be nice to know more about this process. What exactly is the nature of scientific inference?

演绎推理与归纳推理

Deduction and induction

逻辑学家对演绎推理和归纳推理（简称演绎和归纳）做出了重要的区分。以下是一个演绎推理的例子：

Logicians make an important distinction between deductive and inductive inference, or deduction and induction for short. An example of a deductive inference is the following:

所有法国人都喜欢红酒

All Frenchmen like red wine

皮埃尔是法国人

Pierre is a Frenchman

_______________________

_______________________

因此，皮埃尔喜欢红酒。

Therefore, Pierre likes red wine

横线以上的两个陈述称为推理的前提，横线以下的陈述称为结论。这是一个演绎推理，因为它具有以下性质：如果前提为真，那么结论也必然为真。如果所有法国人都喜欢红酒，且皮埃尔是法国人，那么结论就是皮埃尔确实喜欢红酒。这有时被表述为推理的前提蕴含结论。当然，这个推理的前提几乎肯定不为真——肯定会有不喜欢红酒的法国人。但这并非重点。使推理成为演绎推理的关键在于前提和结论之间存在适当的关系，即前提为真保证了结论为真。

The two statements above the line are called the premises of the inference, while the statement below the line is called the conclusion. This is a deductive inference because it has the following property: if the premises are true, then the conclusion must be true too. If it’s true that all Frenchmen like red wine, and that Pierre is a Frenchman, it follows that Pierre does indeed like red wine. This is sometimes expressed by saying that the premises of the inference entail the conclusion. Of course the premises of this inference are almost certainly not true—there are bound to be Frenchmen who do not like red wine. But that is not the point. What makes the inference deductive is the existence of an appropriate relation between premises and conclusion, namely that the truth of the premises guarantees the truth of the conclusion.

并非所有推论都是演绎推理。请看以下示例：

Not all inferences are deductive. Consider the following example:

盒子里前五个鸡蛋都很好。

The first five eggs in the box were good.

所有鸡蛋上都印有相同的最佳食用日期。

All the eggs have the same best-before date stamped on them.

_______________________

_______________________

因此，第六个鸡蛋也很好。

Therefore, the sixth egg will be good too.

这看起来似乎是一个完全合理的推理。然而，它并非演绎推理，因为前提并不蕴含结论。即使前五个鸡蛋都是好的，而且所有鸡蛋的日期戳都相同，第六个鸡蛋仍然很可能已经腐烂。也就是说，这个推理的前提可能为真，但结论却为假，因此它不是演绎推理。相反，它被称为归纳推理。在典型的归纳推理中，我们从关于已检验对象的前提出发，推导出关于我们尚未检验的同类对象（在本例中为鸡蛋）的结论。

This looks like a perfectly sensible piece of reasoning. But nonetheless it is not deductive, for the premises do not entail the conclusion. Even if the first five eggs were good, and all the eggs do have the same date stamp, it is quite conceivable that the sixth egg will be rotten. That is, it is logically possible for the premises of this inference to be true and yet the conclusion false, so the inference is not deductive. Instead it is known as an inductive inference. In a typical inductive inference, we move from premises about objects that we have examined to conclusions about objects of the same sort that we haven’t examined—in this example, eggs.

演绎推理比归纳推理更安全。当我们进行演绎推理时，我们可以确信，如果我们从正确的前提出发，最终会得出正确的结论。相比之下，归纳推理完全有可能从正确的前提得出错误的结论。尽管存在这个缺陷，我们似乎在生活中仍然依赖归纳推理。例如，你早上打开电脑时，你会确信它不会在你面前爆炸。为什么？因为你每天早上都打开电脑，而且到目前为止它从未爆炸过。但是，从“到目前为止，我的电脑每次开机都没有爆炸”到“我的电脑这次不会爆炸”的推理是归纳推理，而不是演绎推理。你的电脑这次爆炸的可能性是存在的，即使它以前从未爆炸过。

Deductive inference is safer than its inductive cousin. When we reason deductively, we can be certain that if we start with true premises we will end up with a true conclusion. By contrast, inductive reasoning is quite capable of taking us from true premises to a false conclusion. Despite this defect, we seem to rely on inductive reasoning throughout our lives. For example, when you turn on your computer in the morning, you are confident it will not explode in your face. Why? Because you turn on your computer every morning, and it has never exploded up to now. But the inference from ‘up until now, my computer has not exploded when I turned it on’ to ‘my computer will not explode this time’ is inductive, not deductive. It is logically possible that your computer will explode this time, even though it has never done so before.

科学家也会运用归纳推理吗？答案似乎是肯定的。以唐氏综合征（DS）为例。遗传学家告诉我们，唐氏综合征患者拥有三条21号染色体，而不是通常的两条。他们是如何得出这个结论的呢？答案当然是，他们检查了大量唐氏综合征患者，发现每个人都多一条21号染色体。然后，他们运用归纳推理得出结论：所有唐氏综合征患者，包括那些他们没有检查过的个体，都多一条21号染色体。这种推论是归纳推理，而非演绎推理。因为虽然可能性不大，但所检查的样本可能并不具有代表性。这个例子并非个例。实际上，每当科学家从有限的数据推导出更普遍的结论时，他们都会运用归纳推理，而他们也一直在这样做。

Do scientists use inductive reasoning too? The answer seems to be yes. Consider the condition known as Down’s syndrome (DS). Geneticists tell us that people with DS have three copies of chromosome 21 instead of the usual two. How do they know this? The answer, of course, is that they examined a large number of people with DS and found that each had an additional copy of chromosome 21. They then reasoned inductively to the conclusion that all people with DS, including those they hadn’t examined, have an additional copy. This inference is inductive not deductive. For it is possible, though unlikely, that the sample examined was unrepresentative. This example is not an isolated one. In effect, scientists reason inductively whenever they move from limited data to a more general conclusion, which they do all the time.

归纳法在科学中的核心作用有时会被我们的表达方式所掩盖。例如，你可能会读到一篇报纸报道，称科学家们找到了“实验证据”，证明转基因玉米可以安全食用。这意味着科学家们在大量人群中测试了这种玉米，没有人受到任何伤害。但严格来说，这并不能证明这种玉米是安全的，至少在数学家所理解的意义上是如此。例如，可以证明毕达哥拉斯定理。因为从“玉米没有伤害任何接受测试的人”到“玉米不会伤害任何人”的推论是归纳推理，而非演绎推理。报纸报道真正应该说的是，科学家们已经找到了充分的证据，证明这种玉米对人类是安全的。“证明”一词严格来说只能用于演绎推理。在这个严格的意义上，科学假设几乎不可能被数据证明为真。

The central role of induction in science is sometimes obscured by how we talk. For example, you might read a newspaper report which says that scientists have found ‘experimental proof’ that genetically modified maize is safe to eat. What this means is that the scientists have tested the maize on a large number of people and none have come to any harm. But strictly speaking this doesn’t prove that the maize is safe, in the sense in which mathematicians can prove Pythagoras’ theorem, say. For the inference from ‘the maize didn’t harm any of the people on whom it was tested’ to ‘the maize will not harm anyone’ is inductive, not deductive. The newspaper report should really have said that scientists have found good evidence that the maize is safe for humans. The word ‘proof’ should strictly only be used when we are dealing with deductive inferences. In this strict sense of the word, scientific hypotheses can rarely if ever be proved true by the data.

大多数哲学家认为，科学严重依赖归纳法是显而易见的，甚至无需赘述。但令人惊讶的是，我们在上一章中提到的哲学家卡尔·波普尔却否认了这一点。波普尔声称，科学家只需要使用演绎推理。如果这是真的，那就太好了，因为正如我们所见，演绎推理比归纳推理更安全。

Most philosophers think it’s obvious that science relies heavily on induction, indeed so obvious that it hardly needs arguing for. But remarkably, this was denied by the philosopher Karl Popper, whom we met in the last chapter. Popper claimed that scientists only need to use deductive inferences. This would be nice if it were true, for deductive inferences are safer than inductive ones, as we have seen.

波普尔的基本论点是这样的：虽然科学理论（或假设）永远无法仅凭有限的数据就被证明是正确的，但它可以被证明是错误的，或者说被反驳。假设一位科学家正在检验“所有金属都导电”这一假设。即使他检验的每一块金属都导电，这也不能证明该假设是正确的，原因我们已经讨论过了。但是，如果这位科学家发现哪怕只有一块金属不导电，这就彻底驳斥了该理论。因为从“这块金属不导电”到“所有金属都导电”的推论是演绎推理——前提蕴含结论。所以，如果一位科学家试图反驳他的理论，而不是证明它的正确性，那么他无需使用归纳法也能达到目的。

Popper’s basic argument was this. Although a scientific theory (or hypothesis) can never be proved true by a finite amount of data, it can be proved false, or refuted. Suppose a scientist is testing the hypothesis that all pieces of metal conduct electricity. Even if every piece of metal they examine conducts electricity, this doesn’t prove that the hypothesis is true, for reasons that we’ve seen. But if the scientist finds even one piece of metal that fails to conduct electricity, this conclusively refutes the theory. For the inference from ‘this piece of metal does not conduct electricity’ to ‘it is false that all pieces of metal conduct electricity’ is a deductive inference—the premise entails the conclusion. So if a scientist were trying to refute their theory, rather than establish its truth, their goal could be accomplished without the use of induction.

波普尔论证的缺陷显而易见。因为科学的目标不仅仅是反驳理论，还要确定哪些理论是正确的（或可能是正确的）。当科学家收集实验数据时，他们的目标可能是为了证明某个特定现象。他们的理论——或许是他们宿敌的理论——是错误的。但更有可能的是，他们试图说服人们相信自己的理论是正确的。为了达到这个目的，他们必须诉诸某种归纳推理。因此，波普尔试图证明科学可以脱离归纳推理而行的努力并未成功。

The weakness of Popper’s argument is obvious. For the goal of science is not solely to refute theories, but also to determine which theories are true (or probably true). When a scientist collects experimental data, their aim might be to show that a particular theory—their arch-rival’s theory perhaps—is false. But much more likely, they are trying to convince people that their own theory is true. And in order to do that, they will have to resort to inductive reasoning of some sort. So Popper’s attempt to show that science can get by without induction does not succeed.

休谟的问题

Hume’s problem

虽然归纳推理在逻辑上并非滴水不漏，但它似乎是一种形成对世界认知的合理方式。太阳过去每天都升起，这难道不足以让我们相信它明天也会升起吗？如果你遇到有人声称自己对太阳明天是否会升起完全持不可知论的态度，你一定会觉得他非常奇怪，甚至可以说是不理智的。

Although inductive reasoning is not logically watertight, it seems like a sensible way of forming beliefs about the world. Surely the fact that the sun has risen every day in the past gives us good reason to believe that it will rise tomorrow? If you came across someone who professed to be entirely agnostic about whether the sun will rise tomorrow or not, you would regard them as very strange indeed, if not irrational.

但我们为何如此信赖归纳法呢？我们又该如何说服那些拒绝归纳推理的人承认他们的错误呢？18世纪苏格兰哲学家大卫·休谟（1711-1776）对此给出了一个简洁却激进的答案。他认为，归纳法的使用根本无法用理性来证明其合理性。休谟承认，我们在日常生活和科学研究中无时无刻不在运用归纳法，但他坚持认为这仅仅是一种本能的动物本能。他认为，如果我们被要求为运用归纳法提供充分的理由，我们将无法给出令人满意的答案。

But what justifies this faith we place in induction? How should we go about persuading someone who refuses to reason inductively that they are wrong? The 18th-century Scottish philosopher David Hume (1711–76) gave a simple but radical answer to this question. He argued that the use of induction cannot be rationally justified at all. Hume admitted that we use induction all the time, in everyday life and in science, but insisted that this was a matter of brute animal habit. If challenged to provide a good reason for using induction, we can give no satisfactory answer, he thought.

休谟是如何得出这个惊人的结论的呢？他首先指出，每当我们进行归纳推理时，似乎都会预设他所谓的“自然界的一致性”。为了理解休谟的意思，让我们回顾一下之前的例子。例如，从“盒子里的前五个鸡蛋是好的”推断出“第六个鸡蛋也会是好的”；从“接受检查的唐氏综合征患者多了一条染色体”推断出“所有唐氏综合征患者都多了一条染色体”；以及从“我的电脑以前从未爆炸过”推断出“我的电脑以后不会爆炸”。今天”。在每一种情况下，我们的推理似乎都依赖于这样一个假设：我们尚未考察的对象，在相关方面，会与我们已经考察过的同类对象相似。休谟所说的自然界的统一性，指的就是这种假设。

How did Hume arrive at this startling conclusion? He began by noting that whenever we make inductive inferences, we seem to presuppose what he called the ‘uniformity of nature’. To see what Hume meant by this, recall our examples. We had the inference from ‘the first five eggs in the box were good’ to ‘the sixth egg will be good’; from ‘the Down’s syndrome patients examined had an extra chromosome’ to ‘all those with Down’s syndrome have an extra chromosome’; and from ‘my computer has never exploded until now’ to ‘my computer will not explode today’. In each case, our reasoning seems to depend on the assumption that objects we haven’t examined will be similar, in relevant respects, to objects of the same sort that we have examined. That assumption is what Hume means by the uniformity of nature.

但是，我们如何知道均匀性假设是正确的呢？我们能否以某种方式证明它的正确性？休谟认为，我们无法证明。因为我们很容易想象这样一个世界：自然并非均匀一致，而是每天都在随机变化。在这样的世界里，电脑有时会无缘无故地爆炸，水有时会毫无预兆地使我们中毒，台球有时会在碰撞时突然停止。既然这样一个非均匀的世界是可以想象的，那么我们就无法证明均匀性假设是正确的。因为如果我们能够证明，那么非均匀宇宙在逻辑上就是不可能的。

But how do we know that the uniformity assumption is true? Can we perhaps prove its truth somehow? No, says Hume, we cannot. For it is easy to imagine a world where nature is not uniform but changes its course randomly from day to day. In such a world, computers might sometimes explode for no reason, water might sometimes intoxicate us without warning, and billiard balls might sometimes stop dead on colliding. Since such a non-uniform world is conceivable, it follows that we cannot prove that the uniformity assumption is true. For if we could, then the non-uniform universe would be a logical impossibility.

即使我们无法证明自然规律的统一性假设，我们或许仍希望找到充分的经验证据来支持其正确性。毕竟，这一假设迄今为止一直成立，这难道不正是它正确的证据吗？但休谟指出，这其实是循环论证！假设自然界迄今为止的运行方式基本统一，休谟认为，我们不能以此为依据来论证自然界将继续保持统一，因为这假设过去发生的事情能够可靠地预测未来——而这正是自然规律统一性假设的前提。如果我们试图从经验的角度来论证自然规律统一性假设，最终只会陷入循环论证。

Even if we cannot prove the uniformity assumption, we might nonetheless hope to find good empirical evidence for its truth. After all, the assumption has always held good up to now, so surely this is evidence that it is true? But this begs the question, says Hume! Grant that nature has behaved largely uniformly up to now. We cannot appeal to this fact to argue that nature will continue to be uniform, says Hume, because this assumes that what has happened in the past is a reliable guide to what will happen in the future—which is the uniformity of nature assumption. If we try to argue for the uniformity assumption on empirical grounds, we end up reasoning in a circle.

要体会休谟观点的力度，不妨想象一下，你会如何说服一个不相信归纳推理的人相信它。你可能会说：“你看，归纳推理到目前为止都非常有效。科学家们正是通过归纳推理分裂了原子，登上了月球，发明了激光。而那些没有运用归纳推理的人则死于非命。他们误以为砷能滋养身体，结果误食了砷。”他们从高楼跳下，以为自己会飞。因此，归纳推理显然是有益的。但这并不能说服怀疑者。因为仅仅因为归纳推理迄今为止行之有效就认为它值得信赖，这本身就是一种归纳推理。对于原本就不信任归纳推理的人来说，这样的论证毫无说服力。这正是休谟的核心观点。

The force of Hume’s point can be appreciated by imagining how you would persuade someone who doesn’t trust inductive reasoning that they should. You might say: ‘look, inductive reasoning has worked pretty well up until now. By using induction scientists have split the atom, landed on the moon, and invented lasers. Whereas people who haven’t used induction have died nasty deaths. They have eaten arsenic believing it would nourish them, and jumped off tall buildings believing they would fly. Therefore it will clearly pay you to reason inductively.’ But this wouldn’t convince the doubter. For to argue that induction is trustworthy because it has worked well up to now is to reason inductively. Such an argument would carry no weight with someone who doesn’t already trust induction. That is Hume’s fundamental point.

这一引人入胜的论证对科学哲学产生了深远的影响。（波普尔试图证明科学只需运用演绎推理，其动机源于他认为休谟已经证明了归纳推理的不合理性。）休谟论证的影响不难理解。因为我们通常认为科学是理性探究的典范。我们对科学家告诉我们的关于世界的信息深信不疑。然而，科学依赖于归纳推理，而休谟的论证似乎表明归纳推理无法得到理性的论证。如果休谟的观点是正确的，那么科学赖以建立的基础似乎并不像我们希望的那样稳固。这种令人困惑的局面被称为休谟归纳问题。

This intriguing argument has exerted a powerful influence on the philosophy of science. (Popper’s attempt to show that science need only use deduction was motivated by his belief that Hume had shown the unjustifiability of induction.) The influence of Hume’s argument is not hard to understand. For normally we think of science as the very paradigm of rational enquiry. We place great faith in what scientists tell us about the world. But science relies on induction, and Hume’s argument seems to show that induction cannot be rationally justified. If Hume is right, the foundations on which science is built do not look as solid as we might have hoped. This puzzling state of affairs is known as Hume’s problem of induction.

哲学家们对休谟的问题做出了数十种回应；时至今日，这仍然是一个活跃的研究领域。一种回应认为，寻求“归纳法的正当性”，或者哀叹归纳法缺乏正当性，最终都是自相矛盾的。20世纪50年代牛津大学哲学家彼得·斯特劳森用以下类比来捍卫这一观点。如果有人担心某个特定行为是否合法，他们可以查阅法律条文，看看条文是如何规定的。但假设有人担心法律本身是否合法，这确实是一个奇怪的担忧。因为法律是评判其他事物合法性的标准，去探究标准本身是否合法毫无意义。斯特劳森认为，归纳法也是如此。归纳法是我们用来判断某人关于世界的信念是否合理的标准之一。因此，去探究归纳法本身是否合理也毫无意义。

Philosophers have responded to Hume’s problem in literally dozens of ways; this is still an active area of research today. One response says that to seek a ‘justification of induction’, or to bemoan the lack of one, is ultimately incoherent. Peter Strawson, an Oxford philosopher from the 1950s, defended this view with the following analogy. If someone worried whether a particular action was legal, they could consult the lawbooks and see what they say. But suppose someone worried about whether the law itself was legal. This is an odd worry indeed. For the law is the standard against which the legality of other things is judged, and it makes little sense to enquire whether the standard itself is legal. The same applies to induction, Strawson argued. Induction is one of the standards we use to decide whether someone’s beliefs about the world are justified. So it makes little sense to ask whether induction itself is justified.

斯特劳森真的成功化解了休谟的问题吗？一些哲学家认为是，另一些则认为不是。但大多数人一致认为，很难找到一个令人满意的归纳法辩护理由。（剑桥大学著名哲学家弗兰克·拉姆齐在1919年写道，要求对归纳法进行辩护无异于“痴人说梦”。）这是否应该让我们担忧，或者动摇我们对科学的信念，是一个值得你深思的难题。

Has Strawson really succeeded in defusing Hume’s problem? Some philosophers say yes, others say no. But most agree that it is very hard to see how there could be a satisfactory justification of induction. (Frank Ramsey, a famous Cambridge philosopher, wrote in 1919 that to ask for a justification of induction was ‘to cry for the moon’.) Whether this is something that should worry us, or shake our faith in science, is a difficult question that you should ponder for yourself.

最佳解释推理

Inference to the best explanation

我们目前考察的归纳推理本质上都具有相同的结构。在每一种情况下，前提的形式都是“所有被考察的F都是G ”，结论的形式都是“其他F也是G ”。简而言之，这些推理将我们从已考察的某一类实例推导出未考察的同类实例。

The inductive inferences we’ve examined so far have all had essentially the same structure. In each case, the premise has had the form ‘all examined Fs have been G’, and the conclusion the form ‘other Fs are also G’. In short, these inferences take us from examined to unexamined instances of a given kind.

正如我们所见，这类推理在日常生活和科学领域中被广泛应用。然而，还有另一种常见的非演绎推理类型，它并不符合这种简单的模式。请看以下示例：

Such inferences are widely used in everyday life and in science, as we have seen. However, there is another common type of non-deductive inference which doesn’t fit this simple pattern. Consider the following example:

食品储藏室里的奶酪都不见了，只剩下一些碎屑。

The cheese in the larder has disappeared, apart from a few crumbs.

昨晚有人听到食品储藏室里传来抓挠声。

Scratching noises were heard coming from the larder last night.

_________________________________________________

_________________________________________________

因此，奶酪被老鼠吃掉了。

Therefore, the cheese was eaten by a mouse.

显然，这种推论并非演绎推理：前提并不蕴含结论。因为奶酪可能是女佣偷的，她巧妙地留下了一些碎屑，伪装成老鼠的杰作；而抓挠声也可能是锅炉过热造成的。尽管如此，这种推论显然是合理的。因为“老鼠吃了奶酪”的假设似乎比“女佣和锅炉”的假设更能解释数据。毕竟，女佣通常不会偷奶酪，现代锅炉也很少过热。而老鼠却会吃奶酪。它们有机会就会吃奶酪，而且确实会发出抓挠的声音。所以，虽然我们不能确定老鼠的假设是否正确，但总的来说，它看起来合情合理。

It is obvious that this inference is non-deductive: the premises do not entail the conclusion. For the cheese could have been stolen by the maid, who cleverly left a few crumbs to make it look like the handiwork of a mouse; and the scratching noises could have been caused by the boiler overheating. Nonetheless, the inference is clearly a reasonable one. For the hypothesis that a mouse ate the cheese seems to provide a better explanation of the data than the ‘maid and boiler’ hypothesis. After all, maids do not normally steal cheese, and modern boilers rarely overheat. Whereas mice do eat cheese when they get the chance, and do make scratching sounds. So although we cannot be certain that the mouse hypothesis is true, on balance it looks plausible.

这种推理被称为“最佳解释推理”（简称IBE）。关于IBE和归纳之间的关系，存在一些术语上的混淆。一些哲学家将IBE描述为一种归纳推理；实际上，他们用“归纳推理”来指代“任何非演绎推理”。另一些哲学家则像我们一样，将IBE与归纳进行对比。按照这种划分方式，“归纳”专指从已检验的同类实例推导出未检验的同类实例；IBE和归纳则是两种不同的非演绎推理。只要我们始终如一地坚持使用同一种术语，选择哪种术语并不重要。

Reasoning of this sort is known as ‘inference to the best explanation’, or IBE for short. Certain terminological confusions surround the relation between IBE and induction. Some philosophers describe IBE as a type of inductive inference; in effect, they use ‘inductive inference’ to mean ‘any inference which is not deductive’. Others contrast IBE with induction, as we have done. On this way of cutting the pie, ‘induction’ is reserved for inferences from examined to unexamined instances of a given kind; IBE and induction are then two different types of non-deductive inference. Nothing hangs on which choice of terminology we favour, so long as we stick to it consistently.

科学家经常运用证据基础（IBE）。例如，达尔文在论证他的进化论时，列举了生物界的一些事实：如果假设现存物种是分别创造的，这些事实就难以解释；但如果假设现存物种如他的理论所认为的那样，起源于共同祖先，那么这些事实就完全说得通了。例如，马和斑马的腿部在解剖结构上非常相似。如果上帝分别创造了马和斑马，我们该如何解释这种相似性呢？他完全可以随心所欲地创造它们不同的腿部结构。但如果马和斑马起源于共同祖先，那么它们腿部解剖结构的相似性就显而易见了。达尔文认为，他的理论能够解释这些事实，这本身就是其真理的有力证据。他写道：“很难想象，一个错误的理论能够像自然选择理论那样，如此令人满意地解释上述几大类事实。”

Scientists frequently use IBE. For example, Darwin argued for his theory of evolution by calling attention to various facts about the living world which are hard to explain if we assume that current species have been separately created, but which make perfect sense if current species have descended from common ancestors, as his theory held. For example, there are close anatomical similarities between the legs of horses and zebras. How do we explain this, if God created horses and zebras separately? Presumably he could have made their legs as different as he pleased. But if horses and zebras have descended from a common ancestor, this provides an obvious explanation of their anatomical similarity. Darwin argued that the ability of his theory to explain such facts constituted strong evidence for its truth. ‘It can hardly be supposed’, he wrote, ‘that a false theory would explain, in so satisfactory a manner as does the theory of natural selection, the several large classes of fact above specified.’

另一个IBE的例子是爱因斯坦关于布朗运动的著名研究——悬浮在水中的微观粒子的锯齿形运动液体或气体。19世纪曾有人尝试解释布朗运动。一种理论认为布朗运动是由粒子间的电吸引力造成的，另一种理论认为是由外部环境的扰动造成的，还有一种理论认为是由流体中的对流造成的。正确的解释基于物质的动理论，该理论认为液体和气体是由运动的原子或分子构成的。悬浮的粒子与周围的分子碰撞，导致它们产生不规则的运动。这一理论在19世纪末提出，但并未被广泛接受，这主要是因为许多科学家不相信原子和分子是真实存在的实体。但在1905年，爱因斯坦对布朗运动进行了巧妙的数学处理，并做出了一些后来被实验证实的预测。爱因斯坦的研究之后，人们很快一致认为动理论比其他理论更能解释布朗运动，对原子和分子存在的怀疑也随之消散。

Another example of IBE is Einstein’s famous work on Brownian motion—the zig-zag motion of microscopic particles suspended in a liquid or gas. A number of attempted explanations of Brownian motion were advanced in the 19th century. One theory attributed the motion to electrical attraction between particles, another to agitation from external surroundings, and another to convection currents in the fluid. The correct explanation is based on the kinetic theory of matter, which says that liquids and gases are made up of atoms or molecules in motion. The suspended particles collide with the surrounding molecules, causing their erratic movements. This theory was proposed in the late 19th century but not widely accepted, not least because many scientists didn’t believe that atoms and molecules were real entities. But in 1905, Einstein provided an ingenious mathematical treatment of Brownian motion, making a number of predictions that were later confirmed experimentally. After Einstein’s work, the kinetic theory was quickly agreed to provide a better explanation of Brownian motion than the alternatives, and scepticism about the existence of atoms and molecules subsided.

IBE（基于数据的推理）的基本思想——从数据出发，推导出能够解释数据的理论或假设——非常简单明了。但是，我们如何判断哪个相互竞争的假设能够提供对数据的“最佳解释”呢？判断标准是什么？一个常见的答案是，好的解释应该简洁明了。再以“食品储藏室里的奶酪”为例。有两个数据需要解释：奶酪不见了，以及刮擦声。老鼠假说只假设了一个原因——一只老鼠——就能解释这两个数据。但女佣和锅炉假说必须假设两个原因——一个不诚实的女佣和一个过热的锅炉——才能解释同样的数据。因此，老鼠假说更加简洁，因而更好。达尔文的例子与之类似。达尔文的理论可以解释生物世界的各种事实，而不仅仅是物种之间的解剖学相似性。原则上，这些事实都可以用其他方式解释，但进化论一次性地解释了所有事实——这使它成为对数据的最佳解释。

The basic idea behind IBE—reasoning from one’s data to a theory or hypothesis that explains the data—is straightforward. But how do we decide which of the competing hypotheses provides the ‘best explanation’ of the data? What criteria determine this? One popular answer is that a good explanation should be simple, or parsimonious. Consider again the cheese-in-the-larder example. There are two pieces of data that need explaining: the missing cheese and the scratching noises. The mouse hypothesis postulates just one cause—a mouse—to explain both pieces of data. But the maid-and-boiler hypothesis must postulate two causes—a dishonest maid and an overheating boiler—to explain the same data. So the mouse hypothesis is more parsimonious, hence better. The Darwin example is similar. Darwin’s theory could explain a diverse range of facts about the living world, not just anatomical similarities between species. Each of these facts could in principle be explained in other ways, but the theory of evolution explained all the facts in one go—that is what made it the best explanation of the data.

认为简洁性或简约性是良好解释的标志，这种观点颇具吸引力，并有助于具体化解释推理（IBE）的抽象概念。但如果科学家以简洁性作为推理的指导，这就引出了一个深刻的问题：我们是否有理由认为宇宙是简单的而非复杂的？倾向于选择能够用最少原因解释数据的理论似乎合情合理。但是，是否存在任何客观依据表明，这样的理论比其他不那么简单的理论更有可能是正确的？或者，科学家之所以重视简洁性，仅仅是因为它使他们的理论更容易构建和理解？科学哲学家们对于这个难题的答案尚未达成共识。

The idea that simplicity or parsimony is the mark of a good explanation is quite appealing, and helps flesh out the abstract idea of IBE. But if scientists use simplicity as a guide to inference, this raises a deep question. Do we have reason to think that the universe is simple rather than complex? Preferring a theory which explains the data in terms of the fewest number of causes seems sensible. But are there any objective grounds for thinking that such a theory is more likely to be true than a less simple rival? Or is simplicity something that scientists value because it makes their theories easier to formulate and to understand? Philosophers of science do not agree on the answer to this difficult question.

因果推断

Causal inference

科学的一个关键目标是发现自然现象的成因。通常，这一探索能够成功。例如，气候变化科学家知道燃烧化石燃料会导致全球变暖；化学家知道加热液体会使其变成气体；流行病学家知道麻疹、腮腺炎、风疹疫苗不会导致自闭症。由于因果关系无法直接观察（正如大卫·休谟的著名论断），这类科学知识必然是推理的结果。但因果推理究竟是如何进行的呢？

A key goal of science is to discover the causes of natural phenomena. Often this quest is successful. For example, climate change scientists know that burning fossil fuels causes global warming; chemists know that heating a liquid causes it to become a gas; and epidemiologists know that the MMR vaccine does not cause autism. Since causal connections are not directly observable (as David Hume famously argued), scientific knowledge of this sort must be the result of inference. But how exactly does causal inference work?

区分两种情况很有帮助：推断特定事件的原因和推断普遍的因果原则。为了说明这种区别，我们可以对比“陨石撞击导致恐龙灭绝”和“吸烟导致肺癌”这两个说法。前者是对特定历史事件原因的陈述，后者是对某种事件（例如罹患肺癌）原因的普遍陈述。在这两种情况下，科学家都通过推理过程得出了这些结论，但推理的方式略有不同。本文重点讨论第二种推理，即推断普遍的因果原则。

It is helpful to distinguish two cases: inferring the cause of a particular event versus inferring a general causal principle. To illustrate the distinction, consider the contrast between ‘a meteorite strike caused the extinction of the dinosaurs’ and ‘smoking causes lung cancer’. The former is a singular statement about the cause of a particular historical event, the latter a general statement about the cause of a certain sort of event (getting lung cancer). In both cases a process of inference has led scientists to believe the statements in question, but the inferences work in somewhat different ways. Here we focus on inferences of the second sort, i.e. to general causal principles.

假设一位医学研究人员想要检验肥胖是否会导致抑郁症这一假设。他们应该如何着手呢？一个自然的第一步是考察这两个特征是否相关。为了评估这一点，他们可以研究一个包含大量肥胖人群的样本，并观察该人群中抑郁症的发病率是否高于普通人群。如果发病率确实高于普通人群，那么除非有理由认为该样本不具有代表性，否则就可以合理地推断（通过普通归纳法）肥胖和抑郁症在普通人群中是相关的。

Suppose a medical researcher wishes to test the hypothesis that obesity causes depression. How should they proceed? A natural first step is to see whether the two attributes are correlated. To assess this, they could examine a large sample of obese people, and see whether the incidence of depression is higher in this group than in the general population. If it is, then unless there is some reason to think the sample unrepresentative, it is reasonable to infer (by ordinary induction) that obesity and depression are correlated in the overall population.

这种相关性是否表明肥胖会导致抑郁？未必如此。理科一年级学生通常会被教导，相关性并不意味着因果关系，这并非没有道理。因为这种相关性还有其他可能的解释。因果关系的方向可能恰恰相反，也就是说，抑郁可能会导致人们吃得更多，从而变得肥胖。或者，肥胖对抑郁可能没有因果影响，反之亦然，而这两种情况是同一原因共同作用的结果。例如，低收入可能通过另一条因果路径增加肥胖和抑郁的概率（见图3）。如果是这样，我们预期肥胖和抑郁在人群中会呈现相关性。这种“共同原因”的情况是，因果关系并非总能从相关性数据中可靠推断出来的主要原因。

Would such a correlation show that obesity causes depression? Not necessarily. First-year science students are routinely taught that correlation does not imply causation, and with good reason. For there are other possible explanations of the correlation. The direction of causation could be the other way round, i.e. being depressed might cause people to eat more, hence to become obese. Or there might be no causal influence of obesity on depression nor vice versa, but the two conditions are joint effects of a common cause. For example, perhaps low income raises the chance of obesity and also raises the chance of depression via a separate causal pathway (see Figure 3). If so, we would expect obesity and depression to be correlated in the population. This ‘common cause’ scenario is a major reason why causation cannot always be reliably inferred from correlational data.

3.因果图描绘了低收入是肥胖和抑郁症共同原因的假设。

3. Causal graph depicting the hypothesis that low income is a common cause of both obesity and depression.

我们如何检验低收入会导致肥胖和抑郁的假设呢？最直接的方法是找到一个收入水平相同的个体样本，然后进行考察。样本中肥胖与抑郁症是否存在相关性。如果我们针对不同的收入水平进行分析，发现每个收入水平相同的样本中，肥胖与抑郁症的相关性都消失了，这便是支持共同原因假说的有力证据。因为这表明，一旦将收入因素考虑在内，肥胖就不再与抑郁症相关。相反，如果即使在收入水平相同的人群中，肥胖与抑郁症之间也存在很强的相关性，这便是反对共同原因假说的证据。在统计学中，这个过程被称为“控制”收入变量。

How could we test the hypothesis that low income causes both obesity and depression? The obvious thing to do is to find a sample of individuals all with the same income level, and examine whether obesity and depression are correlated within the sample. If we do this for a number of different income levels, and find that within each income-homogeneous sample the correlation disappears, this is strong evidence in favour of the common cause hypothesis. For it shows that once income is taken into account, obesity is no longer associated with depression. Conversely, if a strong obesity–depression correlation exists even among individuals with the same income level, this is evidence against the common cause hypothesis. In statistical jargon, this procedure is known as ‘controlling for’ the variable income.

这里的基本逻辑与现代科学的支柱——对照实验类似。假设一位昆虫学家想要检验“在较高温度下饲养昆虫幼虫会导致成虫体型减小”这一假设。为了验证这一假设，昆虫学家会获取大量的昆虫幼虫，一部分在低温下饲养，另一部分在高温下饲养，然后测量最终成虫的体型。为了有效地检验这一因果假设，除了温度之外，两组幼虫之间所有其他因素都必须尽可能保持一致。例如，所有幼虫都应该来自同一物种，性别相同，并且喂食相同的食物。因此，昆虫学家必须精心设计实验，控制所有可能影响成虫体型的变量。只有这样，才能将两组成虫体型的差异可靠地归因于温度差异。

The underlying logic here is similar to that of the controlled experiment, a mainstay of modern science. Suppose an entomologist wishes to test the hypothesis that rearing insect larvae at higher temperatures leads to reduced adult body size. To test this, the entomologist gets a large number of insect larvae, rears some at a cool and others at a warm temperature, then measures the size of the resulting adults. For this to be an effective test of the causal hypothesis, it is important that all factors other than temperature be held constant between the two groups, so far as possible. For example, the larvae should all be from the same species, the same sex, and be fed the same food. So the entomologist must design their experiment carefully, controlling for all variables that could potentially affect adult body size. Only then can a difference in adult body size between the two groups safely be attributed to the temperature difference.

有时有人认为，控制实验是科学中进行因果推断的唯一可靠方法。持这种观点的人认为，纯粹的观察数据，没有任何实验干预，无法让我们了解因果关系。然而，这是一个颇具争议的论点。因为尽管控制实验无疑是探索自然奥秘的好方法，但统计控制技术通常也能达到类似的效果。近年来，统计学家和计算机科学家已经开发出强大的统计控制技术。从观察数据中进行因果推断。实验数据和观察数据在方法论上是否存在根本差异，以及这种差异是否会影响从中得出的因果推断的可靠性，这是一个持续争论的问题。

It is sometimes argued that controlled experiments are the only reliable way of making causal inferences in science. Proponents of this view argue that purely observational data, without any experimental intervention, cannot give us knowledge of causality. However this is a controversial thesis. For while controlled experimentation is certainly a good way of probing nature’s secrets, the technique of statistical control can often accomplish something quite similar. In recent years, statisticians and computer scientists have developed powerful techniques for making causal inferences from observational data. Whether there is a fundamental methodological difference between experimental and observational data, vis-à-vis the reliability of the causal inferences that can be drawn from them, is a matter of continuing debate.

在现代生物医学中，一种特殊的对照实验常常备受重视。这就是随机对照试验（RCT），它最初由R.A. Fisher在20世纪30年代提出，常用于检验新药的疗效。在典型的RCT中，患有特定疾病（例如严重偏头痛）的患者被分为两组。治疗组接受药物治疗，而对照组则不接受。研究人员随后比较两组患者在特定结局指标（例如偏头痛症状缓解情况）上的差异。如果治疗组患者的疗效显著优于对照组，则可初步证明该药物有效。RCT的关键在于，患者最初的分组必须是随机的。Fisher及其现代追随者认为，这是维持有效因果推断的必要条件。

In modern biomedical science, a particular sort of controlled experiment is often given particular prominence. This is the randomized controlled trial (RCT), originally devised by R. A. Fisher in the 1930s, and often used to test the effectiveness of a new drug. In a typical RCT, patients with a particular medical condition, e.g. severe migraine, are divided into two groups. Those in the treatment group receive the drug, while those in the control group do not. The researchers then compare the two groups on the outcome of interest, e.g. relief of migraine symptoms. If those in the treatment group do significantly better than the control group, this is presumptive evidence that the drug works. The key feature of an RCT is that the initial division of the patients into two groups must be done at random. Fisher and his modern followers argue that this is necessary to sustain a valid causal inference.

为什么随机化如此重要？因为它有助于消除混杂因素对目标结果的影响。通常，结果会受到多种因素的影响，例如年龄、饮食和运动。除非所有这些因素都已知，否则研究人员无法对其进行明确控制。然而，通过将患者随机分配到治疗组和对照组，可以很大程度上规避这个问题。即使药物以外的其他因素确实会影响结果，随机化也能确保这些因素不太可能在治疗组或对照组中过度代表。因此，如果治疗组和对照组的结果存在显著差异，则很可能是由药物引起的。当然，这并不能严格证明药物是因果关系，但它构成了强有力的证据。

Why is randomization so important? Because it helps to eliminate the effect of confounding factors on the outcome of interest. Typically the outcome will be affected by many factors, e.g. age, diet, and exercise. Unless all of these factors are known, the researcher cannot explicitly control for them. However by randomly allocating patients to the treatment and control groups, this problem can be largely circumvented. Even if factors other than the drug do affect the outcome, randomization ensures that any such factors are unlikely to be over-represented in either the treatment or the control group. So if there is a significant difference in outcome between treatment and control groups, this is very likely due to the drug. Of course this does not strictly prove that the drug was causally responsible, but it constitutes strong evidence.

在医学领域，随机对照试验（RCT）通常被视为评估因果关系的“黄金标准”。事实上，“循证医学”运动的支持者常常认为，只有RCT才能告诉我们某种特定疗法是否具有因果效力。然而，这种观点或许过于绝对（而且将“证据”一词仅用于指代RCT也具有误导性）。在许多科学领域，由于实际或伦理方面的原因，RCT难以实施，但人们仍然经常进行因果推断。此外，我们日常生活中许多关于因果关系的知识并非来自RCT。例如，幼儿知道把手伸进火里会感到灼痛；这无需任何随机试验就能证实。虽然RCT固然重要，并且在可行的情况下应该进行，但这并不意味着它是发现因果关系的唯一途径。

In medicine, the RCT is usually regarded as the ‘gold standard’ for assessing causality. Indeed proponents of the movement known as ‘evidence-based medicine’ often argue that only an RCT can tell us when a particular treatment is causally effective. However this position is arguably too strong (and the appropriation of the word ‘evidence’ to refer only to RCTs is misleading). In many areas of science, RCTs are not feasible, for either practical or ethical reasons, and yet causal inferences are routinely made. Furthermore, much of the causal knowledge we have in everyday life we gained without RCTs. Young children know that putting their hand in the fire causes a painful burning sensation; no randomized trial was needed to establish this. While RCTs are certainly important, and should be done when feasible, it is not true that they are the only way of discovering causality.

概率与科学推断

Probability and scientific inference

鉴于归纳推理无法提供确定性，我们自然会希望概率的概念能够帮助我们理解其运作方式。即使科学家的证据不能证明其假设是正确的，难道就不能使其具有很高的可能性吗？在探讨这一观点之前，我们需要简要了解一下概率的概念本身。

Given that inductive reasoning cannot give us certainty, it is natural to hope that the concept of probability will help us understand how it works. Even if a scientist’s evidence does not prove that their hypothesis is true, surely it can render it highly probable? Before exploring this idea we need to attend briefly to the concept of probability itself.

概率既有客观层面，也有主观层面。客观而言，概率指的是世界上事物发生的频率，或者说事物发生的倾向。例如，如果有人告诉你，一位英国女性活到90岁的概率是十分之一，你会理解为十分之一的英国女性能活到90岁。同样，对于“抛硬币正面朝上的概率是二分之一”这句话，自然的理解是，在一系列抛硬币中，正面朝上的比例非常接近二分之一。从这个角度理解，关于概率的陈述是客观的真或假，与个人的主观感受无关。

Probability has both an objective and a subjective guise. In its objective guise, probability refers to how often things in the world happen, or tend to happen. For example, if you are told that the probability of an Englishwoman living to age 90 is one in ten, you would understand this as meaning that one-tenth of all Englishwomen attain that age. Similarly, a natural understanding of the statement ‘the probability that the coin will land heads is a half’ is that in a long sequence of coin flips, the proportion of heads would be very close to a half. Understood this way, statements about probability are objectively true or false, independently of what anyone believes.

从主观角度来看，概率是理性信念程度的衡量标准。假设一位科学家告诉你，在火星上发现生命的概率极低。这是否意味着只有极少数天体存在生命？当然不是。首先，没有人知道天体的数量，也不知道其中有多少天体存在生命。因此，这里涉及的是另一种概率概念。既然火星上要么存在生命，要么不存在生命，那么在这种情况下谈论概率，必然反映的是我们对世界现状的无知，而不是对世界本身客观特征的描述。所以，很自然地，我们可以将这位科学家的说法理解为：根据所有证据，人们对“火星上存在生命”这一假设的理性信念程度非常低。

In its subjective guise, probability is a measure of rational degree of belief. Suppose a scientist tells you that the probability of finding life on Mars is extremely low. Does this mean that life is found on only a small proportion of all the celestial bodies? Surely not. For one thing, no one knows how many celestial bodies there are, nor how many of them contain life. So a different notion of probability is at work here. Now since there either is life on Mars or there isn’t, talk of probability in this context must presumably reflect our ignorance of the state of the world, rather than describing an objective feature of the world itself. So it is natural to take the scientist’s statement to mean that in the light of all the evidence, the rational degree of belief to have in the hypothesis that there is life on Mars is very low.

在现有证据的基础上，对某个科学假设的理性信念程度可以被视为一种概率，这种观点为科学推理的运作方式提供了一种自然的解释。假设一位科学家正在考虑一个特定的假设H。根据目前的证据，这位科学家对H有一定的信念程度，记为P ( H)，这是一个介于 0 和 1 之间的数值。（P ( H ) 的另一个名称是科学家对H的“信心” 。）随后出现了一些新的证据，例如来自实验或观察的证据。根据这些新证据，科学家将他们对H的信心更新为Pnew ( H )。如果新证据支持该理论，那么Pnew ( H ) 将大于P ( H )，也就是说，科学家将更加确信H是正确的。

The idea that the rational degree of belief to have in a scientific hypothesis, given the evidence, may be viewed as a type of probability suggests a natural picture of how scientific inference works. Suppose a scientist is considering a particular hypothesis H. In the light of the evidence to date, the scientist has a certain degree of belief in H, denoted P(H), which is a number between zero and one. (Another name for P(H) is the scientist’s ‘credence’ in H.) Some new evidence then comes to light, e.g. from experiment or observation. In the light of this new evidence, the scientist updates their credence in H to Pnew(H). If the new evidence supports the theory, then Pnew(H) will be greater than P(H), i.e. the scientist will have become more confident that H is true.

一个简单的例子可以帮助我们理解这一点。假设从一副洗好的扑克牌中抽出一张牌，并且这张牌被隐藏起来，你看不到。设H 为假设：这张牌是红桃皇后。P( H ) 的值是多少？也就是你最初对H 的理性信念。假设它是 1/52，因为一副牌中有 52 张牌，每张牌被抽中的概率均等。假设你随后得知抽到的牌确实是红桃。把这部分信息称为……已知信息e。根据e ， Pnew ( H )的值是多少？也就是说，根据新证据，你对H的置信度更新后是多少？显然， Pnew ( H ) 应该等于 1/13——因为牌组中有 13 张红桃，而你知道隐藏的牌是其中之一。因此，得知e后，你对H的置信度从 1/52 增加到了 1/13。

A toy example will help flesh this out. Suppose a playing card has been drawn from a well-shuffled pack and is concealed from your view. Let H be the hypothesis that the card is the queen of hearts. What is the value of P(H), i.e. your initial rational credence in H? Presumably it is 1/52. For there are fifty-two cards in the pack and they are all equally likely to be chosen. Suppose you then learn that the chosen card is definitely a heart. Call this piece of information e. In the light of e, what is the value of Pnew(H), i.e. your updated credence in H given the new evidence? Clearly, Pnew(H) should equal 1/13—for there are thirteen hearts in the pack and you know that the concealed card is one of them. So learning e has increased your credence in H from 1/52 to 1/13.

这一切显而易见，但根据新信息更新信念的一般规则是什么呢？答案是“条件化”。要理解这条规则，我们需要条件概率的概念。在抽牌的例子中，P ( H ) 是你对假设H 的初始信念。在假设e为真的条件下，你对假设H的初始信念记为P ( H / e )。（可以理解为“在e为真的情况下，假设H成立的概率”。） P ( H / e )的值是多少？答案是 1/13。因为在假设e为真（即抽到的牌是红桃）的情况下，你对假设H的信念等于 1/13。当你得知e 实际上为真时，根据条件化规则，你对假设H的新信念，即Pnew ( H )，应该等于你在e为真条件下对假设H 的初始信念。

This is all fairly obvious, but what is the general rule for updating your credence in the light of new information? The answer is called ‘conditionalization’. To grasp this rule we need the concept of conditional probability. In the card example, P(H) is your initial credence in hypothesis H. Your initial credence in H conditional on the assumption that e is true is denoted P(H/e). (Read this as ‘the probability of H given e’.) What is the value of P(H/e)? The answer is 1/13. For on the assumption that e is true, i.e. that the card drawn is a heart, your credence in the hypothesis H equals 1/13. When you learn that e is actually true, your new credence in H, i.e. Pnew(H), should then be set equal to your initial credence in H conditional on e, according to the rule of conditionalization.

条件化规则

Rule of conditionalization

得知证据e 后，P new ( H )应等于P ( H / e )。

Upon learning evidence e, Pnew(H) should equal P(H/e).

为了更好地理解条件化规则，请注意，条件概率P ( H / e ) 根据定义等于P ( H且e )/ P ( e )。在纸牌示例中，P ( H且e ) 表示你最初认为H和e都为真的概率。但由于在这种情况下H逻辑蕴含e——因为如果这张牌是红桃皇后，那么它一定是红桃——因此P ( H且e ) 等于P ( H )，即 1/52。那么P ( e ) 呢？这是你最初认为所选牌是红桃的概率。由于牌组中恰好有四分之一的牌是红桃，并且你认为所有牌成为所选牌的概率均等，因此P ( e ) 等于 1/4。应用P ( H / e )的定义，这告诉我们P ( H / e ) 等于 1/52 除以 1/4，即 1/13——与我们之前计算的答案相同。

To better understand the rule of conditionalization, note that the conditional probability P(H/e) is by definition equal to the ratio P(H and e)/P(e). In the card example, P(H and e) denotes your initial credence that both H and e are true. But since in this case H logically entails e—for if the card is the queen of hearts then it must be a heart—it follows that P(H and e) is simply equal to P(H), i.e. 1/52. What about P(e)? This is your initial credence that the chosen card is a heart. Since exactly one quarter of the cards in the deck are hearts, and you regard all the cards as equally likely to be the chosen one, it follows that P(e) is ¼. Applying the definition of P(H/e), this tells us that P(H/e) equals 1/52 divided by ¼, which is 1/13—the same answer as we computed previously.

条件化规则听起来可能很复杂，但就像许多逻辑规则一样，我们常常不假思索地遵循它。在卡片例子中，直觉上很明显，学习e应该会将你对H的理性信念从1/52提高到1/13，而实际上，大多数人也正是这样做的。这样做，即使他们从未听说过条件化规则，也无意识地遵循了它。除了这些隐性应用之外，条件化规则也经常被科学家显式地使用，例如在某些统计推理中。贝叶斯统计学这一统计学分支广泛运用条件化更新。（“贝叶斯”这个名称源于17世纪英国牧师托马斯·贝叶斯，他是概率论的早期先驱，也是条件化规则的发现者。）

The rule of conditionalization may sound complicated, but like many logical rules we often obey it without thinking. In the card example, it is intuitively obvious that learning e should increase your rational credence in H from 1/52 to 1/13, and in practice this is exactly what most people would do. In doing so, they are implicitly obeying the rule of conditionalization even if they have never heard of it. In addition to its implicit uses, the conditionalization rule is often used explicitly by scientists, for example in certain sorts of statistical reasoning. The branch of statistics known as Bayesian statistics makes extensive use of updating by conditionalization. (The name ‘Bayesian’ refers to the 17th-century English clergyman Thomas Bayes, an early pioneer of probability theory, who discovered the conditionalization rule.)
