一些科学哲学家希望将条件化更新作为科学推理的通用模型，甚至适用于那些并非明确基于概率的推理。其核心思想是，任何理性科学家都可以被认为对其理论或假设抱有一定的初始信念，然后根据新的证据，遵循条件化规则对其进行更新。即便科学家的实际推理过程与此截然不同，这些哲学家认为这仍然是一种有用的理想化模型。

Some philosophers of science wish to use updating by conditionalization as a general model for scientific inference, applicable even to inferences that are not explicitly probabilistic. The idea is that any rational scientist can be thought of as having an initial credence in their theory or hypothesis, which they then update in the light of new evidence by following the rule of conditionalization. Even if the scientist’s conscious reasoning process looks nothing like this, it is a useful idealization according to these philosophers.

这种“贝叶斯式”的科学推理观点颇具吸引力，因为它阐明了科学方法的某些方面。试想一下，当一个科学理论做出可检验的预测，并且最终被证实为真时，这通常被视为支持该理论的证据。在第一章中，我们举了爱因斯坦广义相对论的例子：该理论预测星光会受到太阳引力场的偏转；当这一预测得到证实后，科学家们对爱因斯坦理论的信心增强了。但是，既然总会有其他无法排除的可能解释，为什么一个成功的预测会增强科学家对某个理论的信心呢？这仅仅是科学家推理方式的一个简单事实，还是背后有着更深层次的解释？

This ‘Bayesian’ view of scientific inference is quite attractive, as it sheds light on certain aspects of the scientific method. Consider the fact that when a scientific theory makes a testable prediction that turns out to be true, this is usually taken as evidence in favour of the theory. In Chapter 1 we had the example of Einstein’s theory of general relativity predicting that starlight would be deflected by the sun’s gravitational field; when this prediction was confirmed it increased scientists’ confidence in Einstein’s theory. But why should a successful prediction enhance a scientist’s confidence in a theory, given that there will always be other possible explanations that can’t be ruled out? Is this simply a brute fact about how scientists reason, or does it have a deeper explanation?

贝叶斯主义者认为这确实有更深层次的解释。假设一个理论T蕴含一个可检验的命题e。科学家最初对T为真和e为真分别抱有P ( T )和P ( e )的置信度。我们假设P ( T ) 和P ( e ) 都取非极端值，即不为零或一。假设科学家随后得知e确为真。如果他们遵循条件化规则，那么根据逻辑，他们对理论T 的新置信度，即Pnew ( T )，必然大于P ( T )。换句话说，只要科学家遵循条件化规则，当他们得知自己的理论做出了正确的预测时，他们必然会增强对该理论的信心。因此，在贝叶斯科学推理的观点下，成功预测通常会使科学家对自己的理论更有信心这一事实可以得到一个简洁的解释。

Bayesians argue that it does indeed have a deeper explanation. Suppose that a theory T entails a testable statement e. The scientist initially has credence P(T) that T is true and P(e) that e is true. We assume that both P(T) and P(e) take non-extreme values, i.e. are not zero or one. Suppose the scientist then learns that e is definitely true. If they follow the rule of conditionalization, their new credence in theory T, i.e. Pnew(T), must then be greater than P(T) as a matter of logic. In other words, upon learning that their theory has made a true prediction, a scientist will necessarily increase their confidence in the theory so long as they obey the conditionalization rule. So the fact that successful predictions typically lead scientists to become more confident of their theories has a neat explanation, on the Bayesian view of scientific inference.

然而，贝叶斯观点也有其局限性。许多有趣的科学推论都涉及提出前所未有的理论或假设。哥白尼、牛顿和达尔文的伟大科学成就都属于此类。他们各自提出了前人从未考虑过的新理论。引导他们得出这些理论的推理过程显然不能被视为贝叶斯推理。因为条件化描述的是，当科学家获得新的证据时，他们对某个理论的理性信念应该如何改变；这预设了该理论此前已被提出。因此，从数据推导出全新理论的科学推论不能用条件化来理解。

However the Bayesian view has its limitations. Much interesting scientific inference involves inventing theories or hypotheses that have never been thought of before. The great scientific advances made by Copernicus, Newton, and Darwin were all of this sort. Each of these scientists came up with a new theory which their predecessors had never entertained. The reasoning that led them to these theories cannot plausibly be regarded as Bayesian. For conditionalization describes how a scientist’s rational credence in a theory should change when they get new evidence; this presumes that the theory has already been thought of. So scientific inferences that go from data to completely new theory cannot be understood in terms of conditionalization.

贝叶斯观点的另一个局限性在于，在获得新证据之前，初始信念的来源是什么。在扑克牌的例子中，你最初理性地认为选中的牌是红桃皇后，这很容易确定，因为一副牌有52张，每张牌被选中的概率均等。但许多科学假设并非如此。例如，假设到2100年全球变暖将超过4摄氏度。在获得任何相关证据之前，科学家对这个假设的初始信念应该是什么？这个问题的答案显而易见。一些贝叶斯科学哲学家认为，初始信念完全是主观的，也就是说，它们仅仅代表科学家对假设的“最佳猜测”，因此任何初始信念都与其他信念一样好。在这种贝叶斯观点下，科学家可以通过客观理性的方式，在获得新证据时改变他们的信念（即条件化），但对他们的初始信念应该是什么并没有客观的限制。

Another limitation of the Bayesian view concerns the source of the initial credences, prior to updating on the new evidence. In the card example, your initial rational credence that the chosen card was the queen of hearts was easy to determine, because there are fifty-two cards in a deck each with an equal chance of being chosen. But many scientific hypotheses are not like this. Consider the hypothesis that global warming will exceed four degrees by the year 2100. What should a scientist’s initial credence in this hypothesis, before getting any relevant evidence, be? There is no obvious answer to this question. Some Bayesian philosophers of science reply that initial credences are purely subjective, i.e. they simply represent a scientist’s ‘best guess’ about the hypothesis, so any initial credence is as good as any other. On this version of the Bayesian view, there is an objectively rational way for a scientist to change their credences when they get new evidence, i.e. conditionalization, but no objective constraint on what their initial credences should be.

许多哲学家认为这种主观维度的介入是不受欢迎的，因此他们得出结论：贝叶斯观点并非科学推理的全部。这也表明，休谟的归纳问题无法找到贝叶斯式的“解决方案”。认为我们可以借助概率来摆脱休谟问题的想法由来已久。即便太阳过去每天都升起并不能证明它明天也会升起，但这难道不意味着它明天升起的概率很高吗？这种对休谟问题的回应最终是否有效是一个复杂的问题，但我们可以得出以下结论：如果唯一的客观约束在于我们应该如何改变我们的信念，而我们最初的信念应该是什么则完全是主观的，那么那些对世界持有非常怪异观点的人也会被视为完全理性。因此，通过概率来摆脱休谟问题并不能从贝叶斯科学推理的观点中得出。

This intrusion of a subjective dimension is regarded as unwelcome by many philosophers, leading them to conclude that the Bayesian view cannot be the whole story about scientific inference. Also, it shows that there cannot be a Bayesian ‘solution’ to Hume’s problem of induction. The idea that we can somehow escape Hume’s problem by invoking probability is an old one. Even if the sun’s having risen every day in the past doesn’t prove that it will rise tomorrow, surely it makes it highly probable? Whether this response to Hume ultimately works is a complex matter, but we can say the following. If the only objective constraints concern how we should change our credences, but what our initial credences should be is entirely subjective, then individuals with very bizarre opinions about the world will count as perfectly rational. So a probabilistic escape from Hume’s problem will not fall out of the Bayesian view of scientific inference.

第三章

Chapter 3

科学解释

Explanation in science

科学的一个重要目标是尝试解释我们周围世界发生的一切。有时，我们寻求解释是为了实际目的。例如，我们可能想知道臭氧层为何损耗如此迅速，以便采取相应措施。而在其他情况下，我们寻求科学解释仅仅是为了满足我们的求知欲——我们想要更多地了解世界的运行方式。历史上，对科学解释的追求一直受到这两种目标的驱动。

One important aim of science is to try and explain what happens in the world around us. Sometimes we seek explanations for practical ends. For example, we might want to know why the ozone layer is being depleted so quickly in order to try and do something about it. In other cases we seek scientific explanations simply to satisfy our intellectual curiosity—we want to understand more about how the world works. Historically, the pursuit of scientific explanation has been motivated by both goals.

现代科学常常成功地提供解释。例如，化学家可以解释钠燃烧时为何会变成黄色；天文学家可以解释日食发生的时间；经济学家可以解释日元在20世纪80年代贬值的原因；遗传学家可以解释男性脱发为何具有家族遗传倾向；神经生理学家可以解释极度缺氧为何会导致脑损伤。你或许还能想到许多其他成功的科学解释的例子。

Quite often, modern science is successful in its aim of supplying explanations. For example, chemists can explain why sodium turns yellow when it burns. Astronomers can explain why solar eclipses occur when they do. Economists can explain why the yen declined in value in the 1980s. Geneticists can explain why male baldness tends to run in families. Neurophysiologists can explain why extreme oxygen deprivation leads to brain damage. You can probably think of many other examples of successful scientific explanations.

但究竟什么是科学解释？说某种现象可以用科学“解释”究竟意味着什么？自亚里士多德以来，这个问题就一直困扰着哲学家们，但我们的出发点将是德裔美籍哲学家在20世纪50年代提出的关于科学解释的著名论述。卡尔·亨佩尔。亨佩尔的解释被称为覆盖律模型，原因稍后会阐明。

But what exactly is a scientific explanation? What exactly does it mean to say that a phenomenon can be ‘explained’ by science? This is a question that has exercised philosophers since Aristotle, but our starting-point will be a famous account of scientific explanation put forward in the 1950s by the German-American philosopher Carl Hempel. Hempel’s account is known as the covering law model of explanation, for reasons that will become clear.

亨佩尔的覆盖定律解释模型

Hempel’s covering law model of explanation

覆盖律模型的基本思想很简单。亨​​佩尔指出，科学解释通常是为了回应他所谓的“寻求解释的为什么问题”而给出的。这些问题包括“为什么地球不是完美的球形？”或“为什么女性比男性寿命更长？”——它们都是对解释的需求。因此，给出科学解释就是对寻求解释的为什么问题提供一个令人满意的答案。如果我们能够确定这种答案必须具备的基本特征，我们就能知道什么是科学解释。

The basic idea behind the covering law model is straightforward. Hempel noted that scientific explanations are usually given in response to what he called ‘explanation-seeking why-questions’. These are questions such as ‘why is the earth not perfectly spherical?’ or ‘why do women live longer than men?’—they are demands for explanation. To give a scientific explanation is thus to provide a satisfactory answer to an explanation-seeking why-question. If we could determine the essential features that such an answer must have, we would know what scientific explanation is.

亨佩尔认为，科学解释通常具有论证的逻辑结构，即一组前提后跟一个结论。结论表明需要解释的现象确实存在，而前提则告诉我们为什么结论是正确的。例如，假设有人问为什么糖会溶于水。这是一个寻求解释的“为什么”问题。亨佩尔指出，为了回答这个问题，我们必须构建一个论证，其结论是“糖溶于水”，而前提则告诉我们为什么这个结论是正确的。因此，阐述科学解释的任务就变成了精确地刻画一组前提与结论之间必须存在的关系，只有这样，前提才能构成对结论的解释。这就是亨佩尔给自己设定的问题。

Hempel suggested that scientific explanations typically have the logical structure of an argument, i.e. a set of premises followed by a conclusion. The conclusion states that the phenomenon which needs explaining occurs, and the premises tell us why the conclusion is true. Thus suppose someone asks why sugar dissolves in water. This is an explanation-seeking why-question. To answer it, says Hempel, we must construct an argument whose conclusion is ‘sugar dissolves in water’ and whose premises tell us why this conclusion is true. The task of providing an account of scientific explanation then becomes the task of characterizing precisely the relation that must hold between a set of premises and a conclusion, in order for the former to count as an explanation of the latter. That was the problem Hempel set himself.

亨佩尔对这个问题的解答有三点。首先，前提必须蕴含结论，也就是说，论证必须是演绎式的。其次，所有前提都必须为真。第三，前提必须至少包含一条普遍规律。普遍规律包括“所有金属都能导电”、“物体的加速度与其质量成反比”以及“所有植物都含有……”等。例如“叶绿素”；它们与“这块金属能导电”和“我桌上的植物含有叶绿素”等具体事实形成对比。普遍规律有时也被称为自然规律。亨佩尔认为，科学解释可以诉诸具体事实，也可以诉诸普遍规律，但他认为至少一条普遍规律是必不可少的。因此，按照亨佩尔的理念，解释一种现象就是证明它的出现可以从一条普遍规律中演绎得出，或许还可以辅以其他规律和/或具体事实，而所有这些都必须为真。

Hempel’s answer to the problem was threefold. First, the premises should entail the conclusion, i.e. the argument should be a deductive one. Secondly, the premises should all be true. Thirdly, the premises should consist of at least one general law. General laws are things such as ‘all metals conduct electricity’, ‘a body’s acceleration varies inversely with its mass’, and ‘all plants contain chlorophyll’; they contrast with particular facts such as ‘this piece of metal conducts electricity’ and ‘the plant on my desk contains chlorophyll’. General laws are sometimes called laws of nature. Hempel allowed that a scientific explanation could appeal to particular facts as well as general laws, but he held that at least one general law was always essential. So to explain a phenomenon, on Hempel’s conception, is to show that its occurrence follows deductively from a general law, perhaps supplemented by other laws and/or particular facts, all of which must be true.

举例来说，假设我要解释为什么我桌上的植物死了。我可能会这样解释：由于书房光线昏暗，阳光无法照射到植物；但阳光是植物进行光合作用的必要条件；没有光合作用，植物就无法合成生存所需的碳水化合物，最终会死亡；因此，我的植物死了。这个解释完全符合亨佩尔的模型。它通过两个真理——阳光是光合作用的必要条件，以及光合作用是植物生存的必要条件——和一个具体事实——植物没有获得阳光——来解释植物的死亡。鉴于这两个真理和这个具体事实，植物的死亡是必然发生的；这就是为什么前者能够很好地解释后者。

To illustrate, suppose I am trying to explain why the plant on my desk has died. I might offer the following explanation. Owing to the poor light in my study, no sunlight has been reaching the plant; but sunlight is necessary for a plant to photosynthesize; and without photosynthesis a plant cannot make the carbohydrates it needs to survive, and so will die; therefore my plant died. This explanation fits Hempel’s model exactly. It explains the death of the plant by deducing it from two true laws—that sunlight is necessary for photosynthesis, and that photosynthesis is necessary for survival—and one particular fact—that the plant was not getting any sunlight. Given the truth of the two laws and the particular fact, the death of the plant had to occur; that is why the former constitute a good explanation of the latter.

从示意图上看，亨佩尔的解释模型可以写成如下形式：

Schematically, Hempel’s model of explanation can be written as follows:

普通法

General Laws

具体事实

Particular Facts

⇒

⇒

待解释的现象

Phenomenon to be explained

需要解释的现象称为被解释项（explanandum），而解释该现象的普遍规律和具体事实称为解释项（explanans）。被解释项可以是具体的，也可以是普遍的。在前面的例子中，它是一个具体事实——我的植物死了。但有时我们想要解释的事物是普遍性的。例如，我们可能想解释为什么日晒常常会导致皮肤癌。这本身就是一个普遍规律，而非具体事实。要解释它，我们需要从更基本的规律中推导出来——大概是关于辐射对皮肤细胞影响的规律，以及关于阳光中辐射量的具体事实。因此，无论被解释项（即我们试图解释的事物）是具体的还是普遍的，科学解释的结构本质上都是相同的。

The phenomenon to be explained is called the explanandum, and the general laws and particular facts that do the explaining are called the explanans. The explanandum may be either particular or general. In the previous example, it was a particular fact—the death of my plant. But sometimes the things we want to explain are general. For example, we might wish to explain why exposure to the sun often leads to skin cancer. This is itself a generality, not a particular fact. To explain it, we would need to deduce it from more fundamental laws—presumably, laws about the impact of radiation on skin cells, combined with particular facts about the amount of radiation in sunlight. So the structure of a scientific explanation is essentially the same whether the explanandum, i.e. thing we are trying to explain, is particular or general.

很容易理解“覆盖定律模型”名称的由来。根据该模型，解释的本质在于证明待解释的现象被某种普遍的自然定律所“覆盖”。这个想法确实很有吸引力。因为证明某种现象是普遍定律的结果，就能消除其神秘感，使其更容易理解。许多实际的科学解释也确实符合亨佩尔描述的模式。例如，牛顿解释了行星为何绕太阳做椭圆运动，他证明这可以从万有引力定律以及一些其他假设中推导出来。牛顿的解释与亨佩尔的模型完全吻合：通过证明在自然定律和一些其他事实的约束下，某种现象必然如此，就能解释该现象。牛顿之后，行星轨道为何是椭圆的这一问题就不再是谜了。

It is easy to see where the covering law model gets its name. For according to the model, the essence of explanation is to show that the phenomenon to be explained is ‘covered’ by some general law of nature. There is certainly something appealing about this idea. For showing that a phenomenon is a consequence of a general law takes the mystery out of it—it renders it more intelligible. And many actual scientific explanations do fit the pattern Hempel describes. For example, Newton explained why the planets move in ellipses around the sun by showing that this can be deduced from his law of universal gravitation, along with some minor additional assumptions. Newton’s explanation fits Hempel’s model exactly: a phenomenon is explained by showing that it had to be so, given the laws of nature plus some additional facts. After Newton, there was no longer any mystery about why planetary orbits are elliptical.

亨佩尔意识到并非所有科学解释都完全符合他的模型。例如，如果你问别人为什么雅典的雾霾近年来加剧，他们可能会回答“因为家庭燃木量增加”。这没错，而且是一个完全可以接受的科学解释，尽管它没有提及任何定律。但亨佩尔会说，如果解释得更详细一些，定律就会发挥作用。想必存在这样一条定律：如果一定区域内燃木烟雾排放量超过一定水平，且风力足够小，就会形成雾霾云。完整的解释……要解释雅典雾霾加剧的原因，可以引用这条法律，以及雅典燃木量增加和当地风力较弱的事实。实际上，除非我们过于吹毛求疵，否则不会如此详细地解释。但如果要解释，它与这条法律的适用模式非常吻合。

Hempel was aware that not all scientific explanations fit his model exactly. For example, if you ask someone why the smog in Athens has worsened in recent years they might reply ‘because of the increase in domestic wood-burning’. This is true, and is a perfectly acceptable scientific explanation, though it involves no mention of any laws. But Hempel would say that if the explanation were spelled out in full detail, laws would enter the picture. Presumably there is a law which says something like ‘if wood-smoke emissions exceed a certain level in an area of a given size, and if the wind is sufficiently light, smog clouds will form’. The full explanation of why the smog in Athens has worsened would cite this law, along with the fact that wood-burning in Athens has increased and that wind levels there are fairly low. In practice we wouldn’t spell out the explanation in this much detail unless we were being very pedantic. But if we were to spell it out, it would correspond quite well to the covering law pattern.

亨佩尔从他的模型中得出了一个关于解释和预测之间关系的有趣结论。他认为，这两者是同一枚硬币的两面。每当我们用一个涵盖性的定律来解释某种现象时，我们所引用的定律和具体事实，即便我们之前并不了解这种现象，也足以预测它的发生。举例来说，我们再次考虑牛顿对行星轨道为何是椭圆的解释。这个事实早在牛顿用万有引力理论解释它之前就已经为人所知——它是由开普勒发现的。但即便开普勒当时并不了解，牛顿也能够根据他的万有引力理论做出预测。亨佩尔用以下方式表达了这一点：每一个科学解释都可能是一种预测——即使我们之前并不了解这种现象，它也能用来预测它。亨佩尔认为，反过来也成立：每一个可靠的预测都可能是一种解释。举例来说，假设科学家根据栖息地破坏的信息预测山地大猩猩将在2030年灭绝。假设他们的预测最终被证实是正确的。亨佩尔认为，他们之前用来预测大猩猩灭绝的信息，在大猩猩灭绝之后也可以用来解释这一事实。解释和预测在结构上是对称的。

Hempel drew an interesting consequence from his model about the relation between explanation and prediction. He argued that these are two sides of the same coin. Whenever we give a covering law explanation of a phenomenon, the laws and particular facts we cite would have enabled us to predict the occurrence of the phenomenon, if we hadn’t already known about it. To illustrate, consider again Newton’s explanation of why planetary orbits are elliptical. This fact was known long before Newton explained it using his theory of gravity—it was discovered by Kepler. But had it not been known, Newton would have been able to predict it from his theory of gravity. Hempel expressed this by saying that every scientific explanation is potentially a prediction—it would have served to predict the phenomenon in question, had it not already been known. The converse is also true, Hempel thought: every reliable prediction is potentially an explanation. To illustrate, suppose scientists predict that mountain gorillas will be extinct by 2030, based on information about the destruction of their habitat. Suppose they turn out to be right. According to Hempel, the information they used to predict the gorillas’ extinction before it happened will serve to explain that same fact after it has happened. Explanation and prediction are structurally symmetric.

尽管覆盖律模型能够很好地捕捉许多实际科学解释的结构，但它也面临着一些棘手的反例。特别是，有些案例符合覆盖律模型，但直觉上却不能算作真正的科学解释。这些案例表明，亨佩尔的模型过于宽松——它允许纳入一些本应排除的因素。本文将重点讨论其中的两个案例。

Though the covering law model captures the structure of many actual scientific explanations quite well, it also faces a number of awkward counterexamples. In particular, there are cases that fit the covering law model but intuitively do not count as genuine scientific explanations. These cases suggest that Hempel’s model is too liberal—it allows in things that should be excluded. We focus on two such cases here.

情况（i）：对称性问题

Case (i): the problem of symmetry

假设你在一个阳光明媚的日子里躺在沙滩上，你注意到一根旗杆在沙滩上投下了 20 米长的影子（见图4）。

Suppose you are lying on the beach on a sunny day, and you notice that a flagpole is casting a shadow of 20 metres across the sand (see Figure 4).

4.当太阳位于头顶正上方 37° 时，15 米高的旗杆会投下 20 米长的影子。

4. A 15-metre flagpole casts a shadow of 20 metres when the sun is 37° overhead.

有人问你为什么影子长20米。这是一个寻求解释的“为什么”的问题。一个合理的答案可能是这样的：“太阳光线照射到旗杆上，旗杆高15米。太阳的仰角为37°。由于光沿直线传播，简单的三角函数计算（tan 37° = 15/20）表明，旗杆会投射出20米长的影子。”

Someone asks you to explain why the shadow is 20 metres long. This is an explanation-seeking why-question. A plausible answer might go as follows: ‘light rays from the sun are hitting the flagpole, which is exactly 15 metres high. The angle of elevation of the sun is 37°. Since light travels in straight lines, a simple trigonometric calculation (tan 37° = 15/20) shows that the flagpole will cast a shadow 20 metres long.’

这看起来是一个完全合理的科学解释。通过按照亨佩尔的模式重写它，我们可以看到它符合覆盖律模型：

This looks like a perfectly good scientific explanation. And by rewriting it in accordance with Hempel’s schema, we can see that it fits the covering law model:

一般法律 光沿直线传播
三角函数定律
具体事实 太阳仰角为37°
旗杆高15米
待解释的现象 影子长20米

影子的长度可以根据旗杆的高度、太阳的仰角、光沿直线传播的光学定律以及三角函数定律推导得出。由于这些定律成立，且旗杆的高度确实是 15 米，因此该解释完全满足亨佩尔的要求。到目前为止一切顺利。问题如下：假设我们将被解释项——影子的长度为 20 米——替换为旗杆的高度为 15 米。结果如下：

The length of the shadow is deduced from the height of the flagpole and the angle of elevation of the sun, along with the optical law that light travels in straight lines and the laws of trigonometry. Since these laws are true, and since the flagpole is indeed 15 metres high, the explanation satisfies Hempel’s requirements precisely. So far so good. The problem arises as follows. Suppose we swap the explanandum—that the shadow is 20 metres long—with the particular fact that the flagpole is 15 metres high. The result is this:

一般法律 光沿直线传播
三角函数定律
具体事实 太阳仰角为37°
影子长20米
待解释的现象 旗杆高15米

这种“解释”显然也符合遮蔽定律的模式。旗杆的高度是根据其投射的影子长度、太阳的仰角、光沿直线传播的光学定律以及三角函数定律推导出来的。但将此视为旗杆为何15米高的解释似乎非常奇怪。旗杆为何15米高的真正解释大概是木匠故意设计的——这与它投射的影子长度毫无关系。因此，亨佩尔的模型过于宽泛：它允许将一些显然并非科学解释的东西视为科学解释。

This ‘explanation’ clearly conforms to the covering law pattern too. The height of the flagpole is deduced from the length of the shadow it casts and the angle of elevation of the sun, along with the optical law that light travels in straight lines and the laws of trigonometry. But it seems very odd to regard this as an explanation of why the flagpole is 15 metres high. The real explanation of why the flagpole is 15 metres high is presumably that a carpenter deliberately made it so—it has nothing to do with the length of the shadow that it casts. So Hempel’s model is too liberal: it allows something to count as a scientific explanation which obviously is not.

旗杆的例子所蕴含的普遍寓意是，解释的概念本身就存在重要的不对称性。在给定相关规律和其他事实的情况下，旗杆的高度可以解释影子的长度，但反之则不然。一般来说，如果给定相关规律和其他事实， x可以解释y ，那么在相同的规律和事实下， y就不能解释x。这有时被表述为解释是一种不对称关系。亨佩尔的覆盖律模型并非如此。尊重这种不对称性。正如我们可以根据定律和其他事实，从旗杆的高度推导出影子的长度一样，我们也可以根据影子的长度推导出旗杆的高度。因此，亨佩尔的模型未能充分体现科学解释的本质，因为它暗示解释应该是一种对称关系，而实际上它是不对称的。

The general moral of the flagpole example is that the concept of explanation exhibits an important asymmetry. The height of the flagpole explains the length of the shadow, given the relevant laws and additional facts, but not vice versa. In general, if x explains y, given the relevant laws and additional facts, then it will not be true that y explains x, given the same laws and facts. This is sometimes expressed by saying that explanation is an asymmetric relation. Hempel’s covering law model does not respect this asymmetry. For just as we can deduce the length of the shadow from the height of the flagpole, given the laws and additional facts, so we can deduce the height of the flagpole from the length of the shadow. So Hempel’s model fails to capture fully what it is to be a scientific explanation, for it implies that explanation should be a symmetric relation when in fact it is asymmetric.

影子和旗杆的例子也反驳了亨佩尔关于解释和预测是同一枚硬币两面的论点。原因显而易见。假设你不知道旗杆有多高。如果有人告诉你旗杆的影子长20米，太阳位于头顶正上方37°，那么只要你掌握相关的光学和三角学定律，就能预测出旗杆的高度。但正如我们刚才看到的，这些信息显然无法解释旗杆为什么是这个高度。因此，在这个例子中，预测和解释分道扬镳。在我们知道某个事实之前可以用来预测它的信息，在我们知道这个事实之后却不能用来解释它，这与亨佩尔的论点相矛盾。

The shadow and flagpole case also provides a counterexample to Hempel’s thesis that explanation and prediction are two sides of the same coin. The reason is obvious. Suppose you didn’t know how high the flagpole was. If someone told you that it was casting a shadow of 20 metres and that the sun was 37° overhead, you would be able to predict the flagpole’s height, given that you knew the relevant optical and trigonometrical laws. But as we have just seen, this information clearly doesn’t explain why the flagpole has the height it does. So in this example prediction and explanation part ways. Information that serves to predict a fact before we know it does not serve to explain that same fact after we know it, which contradicts Hempel’s thesis.

案例（二）：无关性问题

Case (ii): the problem of irrelevance

假设一个小孩在医院的产科病房里。他注意到房间里有一个人——名叫约翰——没有怀孕，便问医生为什么。医生回答说：“约翰过去几年一直在定期服用避孕药。定期服用避孕药的人是不会怀孕的。所以，约翰没有怀孕。” 假设医生说的是真的——约翰患有精神疾病，确实在服用避孕药，而且他认为避孕药对他有帮助。即便如此，医生的回答显然对小孩没有帮助。约翰没有怀孕的正确解释显然是：他是男性，而男性不可能怀孕。

Suppose a young child is in a maternity ward in a hospital. The child notices that one person in the room—who is a man called John—is not pregnant, and asks the doctor why not. The doctor replies: ‘John has been taking birth control pills regularly for the last few years. People who take birth control pills regularly never become pregnant. Therefore, John has not become pregnant.’ Let us suppose that what the doctor says is true—John is mentally ill and does indeed take birth control pills, which he believes help him. Even so, the doctor’s reply to the child is clearly not helpful. The correct explanation of why John has not become pregnant, obviously, is that he is male and males cannot become pregnant.

然而，医生的解释完全符合覆盖律模型。医生从服用避孕药的人不会怀孕这一普遍规律以及约翰一直在服用避孕药这一特殊事实推断出需要解释的现象——约翰没有怀孕。由于普遍规律和特殊事实都为真，并且它们确实蕴含了被解释项，根据覆盖律模型，医生已经解释了约翰为什么没有怀孕。但实际上，他并没有解释清楚。

However, the explanation the doctor has given fits the covering law model exactly. The doctor deduces the phenomenon to be explained—that John is not pregnant—from the general law that people who take birth control pills do not become pregnant and the particular fact that John has been taking birth control pills. Since both the general law and the particular fact are true, and since they do entail the explanandum, according to the covering law model the doctor has given an explanation of why John is not pregnant. But of course he hasn’t.

总的来说，对某种现象的良好解释应该包含与该现象发生相关的信息。医生对孩子的回答恰恰错在这一点上。虽然医生告诉孩子的话完全正确，但约翰服用避孕药与他没有怀孕无关，因为即使他没有服用避孕药，他也不会怀孕。这就是为什么医生的回答不能算作对孩子问题的合理解答。亨佩尔的模型忽略了我们解释概念中这一关键特征。

The general moral is that a good explanation of a phenomenon should contain information that is relevant to the phenomenon’s occurrence. This is where the doctor’s reply to the child goes wrong. Although what the doctor tells the child is perfectly true, the fact that John has been taking birth control pills is irrelevant to his not being pregnant, because he wouldn’t have been pregnant even if he hadn’t taken been taking the pills. This is why the doctor’s reply does not constitute a good answer to the child’s question. Hempel’s model does not respect this crucial feature of our concept of explanation.

解释与因果关系

Explanation and causality

由于覆盖律模型存在问题，人们自然会寻求理解科学解释的替代方法。一些哲学家认为，关键在于因果关系的概念。这确实是一个颇具吸引力的观点。因为在许多情况下，解释一种现象实际上就是说明其原因。例如，如果事故调查员试图解释一起飞机坠毁事故，他们显然是在寻找事故的原因。事实上，“飞机为什么会坠毁？”和“飞机坠毁的原因是什么？”这两个问题几乎是同义的。同样，如果生态学家试图解释为什么热带雨林的生物多样性不如以往，他们也是在寻找生物多样性减少的原因。解释和因果关系这两个概念之间的联系非常紧密。

Since the covering law model encounters problems, it is natural to look for an alternative way of understanding scientific explanation. Some philosophers believe that the key lies in the concept of causality. This is quite an attractive suggestion. For in many cases to explain a phenomenon is indeed to say what caused it. For example, if an accident investigator is trying to explain an aeroplane crash, they are obviously looking for the cause of the crash. Indeed the questions ‘why did the plane crash?’ and ‘what was the cause of the plane crash?’ are practically synonymous. Similarly, if an ecologist is trying to explain why there is less biodiversity in the tropical rainforests than there used to be, they are looking for the cause of the reduction in biodiversity. The link between the concepts of explanation and causality is quite intimate.

受此联系的启发，许多哲学家放弃了覆盖律解释，转而采用基于因果关系的解释。具体细节各有不同，但这些解释背后的基本思想是：解释一个现象就是说明它的原因。在某些情况下，覆盖律解释和因果解释之间的区别其实并不大，因为从普遍规律推导出现象的发生通常就等于给出了它的原因。例如，我们不妨再回顾一下牛顿对行星轨道为何呈椭圆形的解释。我们看到，这种解释符合覆盖律模型——因为牛顿从万有引力定律以及一些其他事实推导出了行星轨道的形状。但牛顿的解释也是一种因果解释，因为行星的椭圆轨道是由行星和太阳之间的引力作用造成的。

Impressed by this link, a number of philosophers have abandoned the covering law account of explanation in favour of causality-based accounts. The details vary, but the basic idea behind these accounts is that to explain a phenomenon is simply to say what caused it. In some cases, the difference between the covering law and causal accounts is not actually very great, for to deduce the occurrence of a phenomenon from a general law often just is to give its cause. For example, recall again Newton’s explanation of why planetary orbits are elliptical. We saw that this explanation fits the covering law model—for Newton deduced the shape of the planetary orbits from his law of gravity, plus some additional facts. But Newton’s explanation was also a causal one, since elliptical planetary orbits are caused by the gravitational attraction between planets and the sun.

然而，覆盖律和因果解释并非完全等价——在某些情况下，它们甚至会相悖。事实上，许多哲学家之所以倾向于用因果解释，正是因为他们认为因果解释可以避免覆盖律模型面临的一些问题。回想一下旗杆问题。根据覆盖律，为什么我们的直觉告诉我们旗杆的高度可以解释影子的长度，而反之则不然？合理的解释是，旗杆的高度是影子长20米的原因，但影子长20米并不是旗杆高15米的原因。因此，与覆盖律模型不同，因果解释在旗杆问题上给出了“正确”的答案——它尊重了我们的直觉，即我们不能通过指出影子的长度来解释旗杆的高度。

However the covering law and causal accounts are not fully equivalent—in some cases they diverge. Indeed, many philosophers favour a causal account of explanation precisely because they think it can avoid some of the problems facing the covering law model. Recall the flagpole problem. Why do our intuitions tell us that the height of the flagpole explains the length of the shadow, given the laws, but not vice versa? Plausibly, because the height of the flagpole is the cause of the shadow being 20 metres long, but the shadow being 20 metres long is not the cause of the flagpole being 15 metres high. So unlike the covering law model, a causal account of explanation gives the ‘right’ answer in the flagpole case—it respects our intuition that we cannot explain the height of the flagpole by pointing to the length of the shadow it casts.

旗杆问题的总体寓意在于，覆盖律模型无法解释解释是一种不对称关系这一事实。显然，因果关系也是一种不对称关系：如果x是y的原因，那么y就不是x的原因。例如，如果短路导致了火灾，那么火灾显然不是短路的原因。因此，很自然地会认为，解释的不对称性源于因果关系的不对称性。因果关系。如果解释一个现象就是说明是什么导致了它，那么既然因果关系是不对称的，我们就应该预期解释也是不对称的——事实也的确如此。覆盖律模型之所以会遇到“旗杆问题”，正是因为它试图在不考虑因果关系的情况下分析科学解释的概念。

The general moral of the flagpole problem was that the covering law model cannot accommodate the fact that explanation is an asymmetric relation. Now causality is obviously an asymmetric relation too: if x is the cause of y, then y is not the cause of x. For example, if the short-circuit caused the fire, then the fire clearly did not cause the short-circuit. It is therefore natural to suggest that the asymmetry of explanation derives from the asymmetry of causality. If to explain a phenomenon is to say what caused it, then since causality is asymmetric we should expect explanation to be asymmetric too—as it is. The covering law model runs up against the flagpole problem precisely because it tries to analyse the concept of scientific explanation without reference to causality.

避孕药的例子也是如此。约翰服用避孕药并不能解释他为什么没有怀孕，因为避孕药并非他没有怀孕的原因。相反，约翰的性别才是他没有怀孕的原因。这就是为什么我们认为“为什么约翰没有怀孕？”这个问题的正确答案是“因为他是男性，而男性不可能怀孕”，而不是医生的答案。因此，覆盖律模型之所以会陷入无关性问题，正是因为它没有明确要求科学解释能够指出我们想要解释的现象的根本原因。

The same is true of the birth control pill case. That John takes birth control pills does not explain why he isn’t pregnant, because the birth control pills are not the cause of his not being pregnant. Rather, John’s sex is the cause of his not being pregnant. That is why we think that the correct answer to the question ‘why is John not pregnant?’ is ‘because he is male, and males can’t become pregnant’, rather than the doctor’s answer. So the covering law model runs into the problem of irrelevance precisely because it does not explicitly require that a scientific explanation identify the cause of the phenomenon that we wish to explain.

批评亨佩尔未能重视因果关系与解释之间的紧密联系，这一点很容易理解，许多哲学家也曾这样做过。但在某种程度上，这种批评并不公平。因为亨佩尔信奉经验主义哲学，而经验主义者历来对因果关系的概念持怀疑态度。经验主义认为，我们所有的知识都来源于经验。我们在第二章中提到的大卫·休谟是一位杰出的经验主义者，他认为我们不可能体验到因果关系。因此，他得出结论：因果关系并不存在——因果关系是我们人类“投射”到世界的东西！这是一个很难接受的结论。玻璃花瓶摔碎难道不是一个客观事实吗？休谟否认了这一点。他承认，大多数摔碎的玻璃花瓶确实都碎了，这是一个客观事实。但我们对因果关系的理解远不止于此。它包含一种观念，即掉落和破碎之间存在因果关系，前者导致后者。根据这种观点，世界上并不存在这样的联系。休谟：我们看到的只是一个花瓶被摔落，然后片刻后它就碎了。这让我们误以为两者之间存在因果关系，但实际上并非如此。

It is easy to criticize Hempel for failing to respect the close link between causality and explanation, as many philosophers have done. In some ways this criticism is a bit unfair. For Hempel subscribed to the philosophical doctrine called empiricism, and empiricists are traditionally suspicious of the concept of causality. Empiricism says that all our knowledge comes from experience. David Hume, whom we met in Chapter 2, was a leading empiricist, and he argued that it is impossible to experience causal relations. So he concluded that they don’t exist—causality is something that we humans ‘project’ onto the world! This is a very hard conclusion to accept. Surely it is an objective fact that dropping glass vases causes them to break? Hume denied this. He allowed that it is an objective fact that most glass vases which have been dropped have in fact broken. But our idea of causality includes more than this. It includes the idea of a causal connection between the dropping and the breaking, i.e. that the former brings about the latter. No such connections are to be found in the world, according to Hume: all we see is a vase being dropped, and then it breaking a moment later. This leads us to believe there is a causal connection between the two, but in reality there is not.

很少有经验主义者直接接受这一惊人的结论。但由于休谟的著作，他们倾向于将因果关系视为一个需要谨慎对待的概念。因此，对经验主义者而言，用因果关系来分析解释的想法似乎是荒谬的。如果一个人的目标是澄清科学解释的概念（正如亨佩尔的目标），那么使用本身也需要澄清的概念就毫无意义。因此，覆盖律模型没有提及因果关系并非亨佩尔的疏忽。近年来，经验主义的受欢迎程度有所下降。此外，许多哲学家得出结论：因果关系的概念虽然存在问题，但对于我们理解世界而言是不可或缺的。因此，基于因果关系的科学解释理论似乎比亨佩尔时代更容易被接受。

Few empiricists have accepted this startling conclusion outright. But as a result of Hume’s work, they have tended to regard causality as a concept to be treated with caution. So to an empiricist, the idea of analysing explanation in terms of causality would seem perverse. If one’s goal is to clarify the concept of scientific explanation, as Hempel’s was, there is little point in using notions which are equally in need of clarification themselves. So the fact that the covering law model makes no mention of causality was not a mere oversight on Hempel’s part. In recent years empiricism has declined somewhat in popularity. Furthermore, many philosophers have come to the conclusion that the concept of causality, although problematic, is indispensable to how we understand the world. So the idea of a causality-based account of scientific explanation seems more acceptable than it would have done in Hempel’s day.

基于因果关系的解释能够很好地捕捉许多实际科学解释的结构，但也存在一些不太适用的情况。例如，科学中所谓的“理论等同”，如“水是H₂O ”或“温度是平均分子动能”。在这两种情况下，一个熟悉的日常概念被等同于一个更深奥的科学概念。这种理论等同为我们提供了看似科学的解释。当化学家发现水是H₂O时，他们就解释了水是什么。同样，当物理学家发现物体的温度是其分子平均动能时，他们就解释了温度是什么。但这两种解释都不是因果关系。由H₂O构成并不意味着一种物质是水——它只是水而已。拥有特定的平均分子动能并不意味着一种液体具有特定的温度——它只是具有该温度而已。如果接受这些例子……他们认为，合理的科学解释表明，基于因果关系的解释并不能说明全部问题。

Causality-based accounts capture the structure of many actual scientific explanations quite well, but there are also cases they fit less well. Consider what are called ‘theoretical identifications’ in science, such as ‘water is H2O’ or ‘temperature is mean molecular kinetic energy’. In both cases, a familiar everyday concept is equated or identified with a more esoteric scientific concept. Such theoretical identifications furnish us with what appear to be scientific explanations. When chemists discovered that water is H2O, they thereby explained what water is. Similarly, when physicists discovered that an object’s temperature is the average kinetic energy of its molecules, they thereby explained what temperature is. But neither of these explanations is causal. Being made of H2O doesn’t cause a substance to be water—it just is being water. Having a particular mean molecular kinetic energy doesn’t cause a liquid to have the temperature it does—it just is having that temperature. If these examples are accepted as legitimate scientific explanations, they suggest that causality-based accounts of explanation cannot be the whole story.

科学能解释一切吗？

Can science explain everything?

现代科学可以解释我们所处世界的许多方面。但也有许多事实尚未被科学解释，或者至少尚未得到充分解释。生命的起源就是其中一个例子。我们知道，大约40亿年前，具有自我复制能力的分子出现在原始汤中，生命由此演化而来。但我们并不了解这些能够自我复制的分子最初是如何出现的（尽管一些可能的解释已被提出）。另一个例子是，患有阿斯伯格综合征的儿童通常拥有非常好的记忆力。大量研究证实了这一事实，但至今仍无人能够解释其原因。

Modern science can explain a great deal about the world we live in. But there are also numerous facts that have not been explained by science, or at least not explained fully. The origin of life is one such example. We know that about four billion years ago, molecules with the ability to make copies of themselves appeared in the primeval soup, and life evolved from there. But we do not understand how these self-replicating molecules got there in the first place (though some possible scenarios have been sketched). Another example is the fact that children with Asperger’s syndrome often have very good memories. Numerous studies have confirmed this fact, but as yet nobody has succeeded in explaining it.

许多人相信，最终科学能够解释这类事实。这种观点相当合理。分子生物学家正努力研究生命起源的问题，只有悲观主义者才会认为他们永远无法解决这个问题。诚然，这个问题并不容易，尤其因为我们很难了解40亿年前地球的状况。但即便如此，也没有理由认为生命的起源永远无法得到解释。阿斯伯格症儿童的超强记忆力也是如此。记忆科学仍处于起步阶段，关于阿斯伯格症等疾病的神经学基础，还有许多未知之处等待我们去发现。显然，我们无法保证最终一定能找到解释。但鉴于现代科学已经取得的众多解释性成就，我们有理由相信，许多当今无法解释的事实最终也会得到解释。

Many people believe that in the end, science will be able to explain facts of this sort. This is quite a plausible view. Molecular biologists are working hard on the problem of the origin of life, and only a pessimist would say they will never solve it. Admittedly the problem is not easy, not least because it is hard to know what conditions on earth four billion years ago were like. But nonetheless, there is no reason to think that the origin of life will never be explained. Similarly for the exceptional memories of children with Asperger’s. The science of memory is still fairly new, and much remains to be discovered about the neurological basis of conditions such as Asperger’s syndrome. Obviously we cannot guarantee that the explanation will eventually be found. But given the number of explanatory successes that modern science has already notched up, the smart money must be on many of today’s unexplained facts eventually being explained too.

但这是否意味着科学原则上可以解释一切？或者说，是否存在一些现象注定永远无法被科学解释？解释？这并非一个容易回答的问题。一方面，断言科学可以解释一切似乎有些狂妄；另一方面，断言任何特定现象都无法用科学解释又显得目光短浅。因为科学日新月异，从今天的科学视角来看完全无法解释的现象，明天或许就能轻易解释。

But does this mean that science can in principle explain everything? Or are there some phenomena that must forever elude scientific explanation? This is not an easy question to answer. On the one hand, it seems arrogant to assert that science can explain everything. On the other hand, it seems short-sighted to assert that any particular phenomenon can never be explained scientifically. For science changes and develops fast, and a phenomenon that looks completely inexplicable from the vantage-point of today’s science may be easily explained tomorrow.

许多哲学家认为，科学永远无法解释一切，这完全是出于逻辑原因。因为要解释任何事物，无论它是什么，我们都需要援引其他事物。但谁来解释这第二个事物呢？举例来说，牛顿用万有引力定律解释了各种各样的现象。但万有引力定律本身又该如何解释呢？如果有人问为什么所有物体之间都存在引力，我们应该如何回答？牛顿对此无能为力。在牛顿科学中，万有引力定律是一个基本原理：它解释了其他事物，但它自身却无法被解释。这个道理具有普遍性。无论未来的科学能够解释多少事物，它给出的解释都必须运用某些基本定律和原理。既然任何事物都无法自我解释，那么至少其中一些定律和原理本身也将无法被解释。

According to many philosophers, there is a purely logical reason why science will never be able to explain everything. For in order to explain something, whatever it is, we need to invoke something else. But what explains the second thing? To illustrate, recall that Newton explained a diverse range of phenomena using his law of gravity. But what explains the law of gravity itself? If someone asks why all bodies exert a gravitational attraction on each other, what should we tell them? Newton had no answer to this question. In Newtonian science the law of gravity was a fundamental principle: it explained other things, but could not itself be explained. The moral generalizes. However much the science of the future can explain, the explanations it gives will have to make use of certain fundamental laws and principles. Since nothing can explain itself, it follows that at least some of these laws and principles will themselves remain unexplained.

无论人们如何看待这种论点，它无疑都非常抽象。它试图表明有些事物永远无法解释，但却没有告诉我们这些事物究竟是什么。然而，一些哲学家对他们认为科学永远无法解释的现象提出了具体的见解。例如意识——它是像我们人类和其他高等动物这样有思想、有感觉的生物的显著特征。神经科学家、心理学家和其他领域的专家已经并将继续对意识的本质进行大量研究。但一些近期的哲学家声称，无论这些研究得出什么结论，都永远无法完全解释意识的本质。这种现象本身就蕴含着某种神秘的特质。他们认为，意识是任何科学研究都无法消除的。

Whatever one makes of this argument, it is undeniably very abstract. It purports to show that some things will never be explained, but does not tell us what they are. However, some philosophers have made concrete suggestions about phenomena which they think science can never explain. An example is consciousness—the distinguishing feature of thinking, feeling creatures such as ourselves and other higher animals. Much research into the nature of consciousness has been and continues to be done, by neuroscientists, psychologists, and others. But a number of recent philosophers claim that whatever this research throws up, it will never fully explain the nature of consciousness. There is something intrinsically mysterious about the phenomenon of consciousness, they maintain, that no amount of scientific investigation can eliminate.

这种观点的依据是什么？其基本论点是，意识体验与世间万物截然不同，因为它们具有“主观性”。例如，想想观看恐怖电影的体验。这种体验有一种非常独特的“感觉”；用现在的术语来说，就是这种体验“感觉很特别”。神经科学家或许有一天能够详细解释大脑中产生恐惧感的复杂过程。但这能解释为什么观看恐怖电影会给人这种感觉，而不是其他感觉吗？一些哲学家认为不能。在他们看来，对大脑的科学研究至多只能告诉我们哪些大脑过程与哪些意识体验相关。这当然是有趣且有价值的信息。然而，它并不能解释为什么具有独特主观“感觉”的体验会源于大脑中纯粹的物理活动。因此，意识，或者至少是意识的某个重要方面，在科学上是无法解释的。

What are the grounds for this view? The basic argument is that conscious experiences are fundamentally unlike anything else in the world, in that they have a ‘subjective aspect’. Consider for example the experience of watching a terrifying horror movie. This is an experience with a very distinctive ‘feel’ to it; in the current jargon, there is ‘something that it is like’ to have the experience. Neuroscientists may one day be able to give a detailed account of the complex goings-on in the brain which produce our feeling of terror. But will this explain why watching a horror movie feels the way it does, rather than feeling some other way? Some philosophers argue that it will not. On their view, the scientific study of the brain can at most tell us which brain processes are correlated with which conscious experiences. This is certainly interesting and valuable information. However it doesn’t tell us why experiences with distinctive subjective ‘feels’ should result from the purely physical goings-on in the brain. Hence consciousness, or at least one important aspect of it, is scientifically inexplicable.

尽管这个论点颇具说服力，但它也颇具争议，并非所有哲学家都认同，更遑论所有神经科学家。事实上，哲学家丹尼尔·丹尼特1991年出版的一本著名著作就以《意识的解释》为题，颇具挑战性。那些认为意识无法用科学解释的人有时会被指责缺乏想象力。即便目前脑科学确实无法解释意识体验的主观层面，我们难道不能想象一种不同的脑科学的出现，它拥有不同的解释方法，能够解释我们体验的感受方式吗？哲学家们一直试图告诉科学家什么是可能的，什么是不可能的，而后来的科学发展往往证明哲学家们的观点是错误的。最终结果如何，只有时间才能给出答案。那些认为意识必然永远无法用科学解释的人，也将面临同样的命运。

Though quite compelling, this argument is controversial and not endorsed by all philosophers, let alone all neuroscientists. Indeed a well-known 1991 book by the philosopher Daniel Dennett is defiantly entitled Consciousness Explained. Supporters of the view that consciousness is scientifically inexplicable are sometimes accused of having a lack of imagination. Even if it is true that brain science as currently practised cannot explain the subjective aspect of conscious experience, can we not imagine the emergence of a different type of brain science, with different explanatory techniques, that does explain why our experiences feel the way they do? There is a long tradition of philosophers trying to tell scientists what is and isn’t possible, and later scientific developments have often proved the philosophers wrong. Only time will tell whether the same fate awaits those who argue that consciousness must always elude scientific explanation.

解释与简化

Explanation and reduction

不同的科学学科旨在解释不同类型的现象。解释橡胶为何不导电是物理学的任务；解释乌龟为何寿命如此之长是生物学的任务；解释高利率为何能降低通货膨胀是经济学的任务，等等。简而言之，不同学科之间存在分工：每个学科都专注于解释其特定的现象。这就解释了为什么各学科之间通常不会相互竞争——例如，为什么生物学家并不担心物理学家和经济学家会侵占他们的研究领域。

The different scientific disciplines are designed for explaining different types of phenomena. To explain why rubber doesn’t conduct electricity is a task for physics. To explain why turtles have such long lives is a task for biology. To explain why higher interest rates reduce inflation is a task for economics, and so on. In short, there is a division of labour between the different sciences: each specializes in explaining its own particular set of phenomena. This explains why the sciences are not usually in competition with one another—why biologists, for example, do not worry that physicists and economists might encroach on their turf.

然而，人们普遍认为，各个科学分支并非完全平等：有些分支比其他分支更具基础性。物理学通常被认为是所有科学中最基础的。为什么呢？因为其他科学研究的对象最终都是由物理粒子构成的。以生物体为例。生物体由细胞构成，细胞本身又由水、核酸、蛋白质、糖类和脂质构成，而这些物质又都由分子或连接在一起的长链分子构成。但是，分子是由原子构成的，而原子是物理粒子。因此，生物学家研究的对象最终只是非常复杂的物理实体。这同样适用于其他科学，甚至包括社会科学。以经济学为例。经济学研究企业和消费者在市场中的行为及其后果。但是，消费者是人，企业也是由人组成的；而人是生物体，因此也是物理实体。

Nonetheless, it is widely held that the different branches of science are not all on a par: some are more fundamental than others. Physics is usually regarded as the most fundamental science of all. Why? Because the objects studied by the other sciences are ultimately composed of physical particles. Consider living organisms, for example. Living organisms are made up of cells, which are themselves made up of water, nucleic acids, proteins, sugars, and lipids, all of which consist of molecules or long chains of molecules joined together. But molecules are made up of atoms, which are physical particles. So the objects biologists study are ultimately just very complex physical entities. The same applies to the other sciences, even the social sciences. Take economics for example. Economics studies the behaviour of firms and consumers in the market place, and the consequences of this behaviour. But consumers are human beings and firms are made up of human beings; and human beings are living organisms, hence physical entities.

这是否意味着，原则上物理学可以涵盖所有更高层次的科学？因为一切都由物理量构成。如果物理学能够完美地预测宇宙中所有物理粒子的行为，那么其他所有科学岂不都变得多余了？大多数哲学家对此持反对意见。毕竟，认为物理学有朝一日能够解释生物学和经济学所解释的现象，这听起来似乎很疯狂。直接从物理定律推导出生物学和经济学定律的可能性微乎其微。无论未来的物理学发展成什么样子，它都极不可能预测经济衰退。生物学和经济学等科学不仅无法被物理学所取代，而且在很大程度上独立于物理学之外。

Does this mean that, in principle, physics can subsume all the higher-level sciences? Since everything is made up of physical particles, surely if we had a complete physics, which allowed us to predict perfectly the behaviour of every physical particle in the universe, all the other sciences would become superfluous? Most philosophers resist this line of thought. After all, it seems crazy to suggest that physics might one day be able to explain the things that biology and economics explain. The prospect of deducing the laws of biology and economics straight from the laws of physics looks very remote. Whatever the physics of the future looks like, it is most unlikely to be capable of predicting economic downturns. Far from being reducible to physics, sciences such as biology and economics seem largely autonomous of it.

这就引出了一个哲学难题：一门研究本质上是物质实体的科学，怎么可能不能被还原为物理学呢？假设高等科学实际上独立于物理学之外，这又如何可能呢？一些哲学家认为，答案在于高等科学研究的对象在物理层面上是多种实现的。为了说明多种实现的概念，不妨想象一堆烟灰缸。每个烟灰缸显然都是一个物理实体，就像宇宙中的一切事物一样。但是，这些烟灰缸的物理构成可能千差万别——有些可能是玻璃做的，有些是铝做的，有些是塑料做的，等等。它们的尺寸、形状和重量也可能各不相同。一个烟灰缸可以拥有的物理属性种类几乎是无限的。因此，我们不可能用纯粹的物理术语来定义“烟灰缸”这个概念。我们找不到形如“ x是烟灰缸当且仅当x是……”的真命题，其中空格处必须填入物理学术语。这意味着烟灰缸在物理层面上以多种形式存在。

This leads to a philosophical puzzle. How can a science which studies entities which are ultimately physical not be reducible to physics? Granted that the higher-level sciences are in fact autonomous of physics, how is this possible? According to some philosophers, the answer lies in the fact that the objects studied by the higher-level sciences are multiply realized at the physical level. To illustrate the idea of multiple realization, imagine a collection of ashtrays. Each individual ashtray is obviously a physical entity, like everything else in the universe. But the physical composition of the ashtrays could be very different—some might be made of glass, others of aluminium, others of plastic, and so on. And they will probably differ in size, shape, and weight. There is virtually no limit on the range of different physical properties that an ashtray can have. So it is impossible to define the concept ‘ashtray’ in purely physical terms. We cannot find a true statement of the form ‘x is an ashtray if and only if x is … ’ where the blank is filled by an expression taken from the language of physics. This means that ashtrays are multiply realized at the physical level.

哲学家们经常援引多重实现理论来解释为什么心理学不能被还原为物理学或化学，但原则上，这种解释适用于任何更高层次的科学。例如，考虑一下神经细胞比皮肤细胞寿命更长的生物学事实。细胞是物理实体，因此人们可能会……有人认为，这一事实终有一天会被物理学解释。然而，细胞在微观物理层面上几乎肯定是多种实现的。细胞最终由原子构成，但不同细胞中原子的精确排列方式却截然不同。因此，“细胞”的概念无法用基础物理学的术语来定义。不存在“ x是细胞当且仅当x是……”这种形式的真命题，其中空格处可以填入微观物理学的表达式。如果这是正确的，那就意味着基础物理学永远无法解释为什么神经细胞比皮肤细胞寿命更长，或者任何其他关于细胞的事实。细胞生物学的词汇和物理学的词汇无法以所需的方式相互对应。因此，我们就能解释为什么细胞生物学无法被还原为物理学，尽管细胞是物理实体。并非所有哲学家都认同多种实现的理论，但它确实为高等科学的自主性提供了一个简洁的解释，这种自主性既独立于物理学，也独立于其他科学。

Philosophers have often invoked multiple realization to explain why psychology cannot be reduced to physics or chemistry, but in principle the explanation works for any higher-level science. For example, consider the biological fact that nerve cells live longer than skin cells. Cells are physical entities, so one might think that this fact will one day be explained by physics. However, cells are almost certainly multiply realized at the microphysical level. Cells are ultimately made up of atoms, but the precise arrangement of atoms will be very different in different cells. So the concept ‘cell’ cannot be defined in terms drawn from fundamental physics. There is no true statement of the form ‘x is a cell if and only if x is … ’ where the blank is filled by an expression taken from the language of microphysics. If this is correct, it means that fundamental physics will never be able to explain why nerve cells live longer than skin cells, or indeed any other facts about cells. The vocabulary of cell biology and the vocabulary of physics do not map onto each other in the required way. Thus we have an explanation of why it is that cell biology cannot be reduced to physics, despite the fact that cells are physical entities. Not all philosophers are happy with the doctrine of multiple realization, but it does promise a neat explanation of the autonomy of the higher-level sciences, both from physics and from each other.

第四章

Chapter 4

现实主义与反现实主义

Realism and anti-realism

在哲学界，存在着一场古老的辩论，一方是实在论，另一方是唯心论。实在论认为，物质世界独立于人类的思想和感知而存在。唯心论则否定了这一点——它声称物质世界在某种程度上依赖于人类的意识活动。对大多数人来说，实在论似乎比唯心论更合情理。因为实在论与常识相符，即关于世界的真相“就在那里”，等待着人们去发现。的确，乍一看，唯心论似乎很荒谬。既然即使人类灭绝，岩石和树木依然存在，那么它们的存在又如何依赖于人类的思维呢？实际上，这个问题远比这复杂得多，至今仍是哲学家们探讨的话题。

There is an ancient debate in philosophy between two opposing schools of thought called realism and idealism. Realism holds that the physical world exists independently of human thought and perception. Idealism denies this—it claims that the physical world is in some way dependent on the conscious activity of humans. To most people, realism seems more plausible than idealism. For realism fits well with the commonsense view that the facts about the world are ‘out there’ waiting to be discovered. Indeed at first glance idealism can sound plain silly. Since rocks and trees would continue to exist even if the human race died out, in what sense is their existence dependent on human minds? In fact the issue is a bit more subtle than this, and continues to be discussed by philosophers today.

虽然传统的实在论/唯心论之争属于形而上学的范畴，但它与科学并无直接关联。本章关注的是一个当代的、专门针对科学的辩论，它在某些方面与传统的实在论/唯心论之争有相似之处。这场辩论的双方分别是被称为科学实在论的立场和它的对立面——反实在论或工具主义。从现在开始，我们将用“实在论”来指代科学实在论，“实在论者”来指代科学实在论者。

Though the traditional realism/idealism issue belongs to an area of philosophy called metaphysics, it has nothing in particular to do with science. Our concern in this chapter is with a contemporary debate that is specifically about science, and is in some ways analogous to the traditional issue. The debate is between a position known as scientific realism and its converse, known as anti-realism or instrumentalism. From now on we shall use the word ‘realism’ to mean scientific realism, and ‘realist’ to mean scientific realist.

科学现实主义与反现实主义

Scientific realism and anti-realism

科学实在论的基本思想很简单。实在论者认为，科学旨在提供对世界的真实描述，而且通常都能成功。因此，在实在论者看来，好的科学理论就是能够真实描述世界本来面目的理论。这听起来似乎是一个相当无害的理论。毕竟，肯定没有人会认为科学的目的是为了对世界做出错误的描述吧？但反实在论者却不这么认为。相反，反实在论者认为，科学的目标是找到经验上充分的理论，即能够正确预测实验和观察结果的理论。如果一个理论达到了完美的经验充分性，那么对于反实在论者来说，它是否真实地描述了世界这个问题就显得多余了；事实上，有些人甚至认为这个问题本身就毫无意义。

The basic idea of scientific realism is straightforward. Realists hold that science aims to provide a true description of the world, and that it often succeeds. So a good scientific theory, according to realists, is one that truly describes the way the world is. This may sound like a fairly innocuous doctrine. For surely no one thinks that science is aiming to produce a false description of the world? But that is not what anti-realists think. Rather, anti-realists hold that the aim of science is to find theories that are empirically adequate, i.e. which correctly predict the results of experiment and observation. If a theory achieves perfect empirical adequacy, the further question of whether it truly describes the world is redundant, for anti-realists; indeed some argue that this question does not even make sense.

现实主义与反现实主义之间的对比在那些对不可观测的现实领域做出论断的科学领域最为鲜明。物理学就是一个显而易见的例子。物理学家提出了关于原子、电子、夸克、轻子和其他奇异实体的理论，这些实体都无法以通常意义上的方式被观测到；此外，这些理论通常以高度数学化的语言表达。因此，物理理论与非科学家对世界的常识性描述截然不同。然而，现实主义者认为，这些理论是对世界——亚原子世界——的描述，而衡量其成功与否的标准在于它们对世界的描述是否正确。在这方面，科学理论与对世界的常识性描述是相等的。

The contrast between realism and anti-realism is starkest for sciences which make claims about the unobservable region of reality. Physics is the obvious example. Physicists advance theories about atoms, electrons, quarks, leptons, and other strange entities, none of which can be observed in the normal sense of the word; moreover these theories are typically couched in a highly mathematical language. So physical theories are rather different from the commonsense descriptions of the world that non-scientists give. Nonetheless, realists argue, these theories are attempts to describe the world—the subatomic world—and the measure of their success is whether what they say about the world is true. In this respect, scientific theories and commonsense descriptions of the world are on a par.

反实在论者认为，科学理论的真正目的在于经验上的充分性，而非真理。物理学家或许会谈论不可观测的实体，但它们仅仅是为了帮助预测可观测现象而引入的方便的虚构概念。举例来说，我们再次考虑气体动力学理论，该理论认为：任何体积的气体都包含大量运动的微小粒子。这些粒子——分子——是不可观测的。从分子动力学理论中，我们可以推导出气体可观测行为的各种结果，例如，在压力保持不变的情况下，加热气体样本会导致其膨胀，这可以通过实验验证。反实在论者认为，分子动力学理论中引入不可观测粒子的唯一目的就是推导出这类结果。气体是否真的包含运动的分子并不重要；分子动力学理论的目的并非在于真正描述隐藏的事实，而仅仅是为了提供一种便捷的预测观测结果的方法。我们可以看出，反实在论有时被称为“工具主义”——它将科学理论视为帮助我们预测可观测现象的工具，而不是试图描述现实的本质。

Anti-realists argue that empirical adequacy, not truth, is the real aim of scientific theorizing. Physicists may talk about unobservable entities, but they are merely convenient fictions introduced in order to help predict observable phenomena. To illustrate, consider again the kinetic theory of gases, which says that any volume of gas contains a large number of very small entities in motion. These entities—molecules—are unobservable. From the kinetic theory we can deduce various consequences about the observable behaviour of gases, for example that heating a sample of gas will cause it to expand if the pressure remains constant, which can be verified experimentally. Anti-realists argue that the only purpose of positing unobservable entities in the kinetic theory is to deduce consequences of this sort. Whether or not gases really do contain molecules in motion doesn’t matter; the point of the kinetic theory is not to truly describe the hidden facts, but just to provide a convenient way of predicting observations. We can see why anti-realism is sometimes called ‘instrumentalism’—it regards scientific theories as instruments for helping us predict observable phenomena, rather than as attempts to describe the underlying nature of reality.

由于实在论/反实在论之争关乎科学的目标，人们或许会认为只需询问科学家们就能解决。为什么不做个非正式的科学家调查，问问他们各自的目标呢？但这种建议却不得要领——它对“科学的目标”这一表述理解得过于字面化。当我们问科学的目标是什么时，我们并非在询问个别科学家的目标。相反，我们是在问如何才能最好地理解科学家的言行——如何诠释科学事业。虽然了解科学家们对实在论/反实在论之争的看法固然有趣，但归根结底，这仍然是一个哲学问题。

Since the realism/anti-realism debate concerns the aim of science, one might think it could be resolved by simply asking the scientists themselves. Why not do a straw poll of scientists asking them about their aims? But this suggestion misses the point—it takes the expression ‘the aim of science’ too literally. When we ask what the aim of science is, we are not asking about the aims of individual scientists. Rather, we are asking how best to make sense of what scientists say and do—how to interpret the scientific enterprise. While it would certainly be interesting to discover scientists’ own views on the realism/anti-realism debate, the issue is ultimately a philosophical one.

反实在论的一个动机源于这样一种信念：我们实际上无法获得关于现实中不可观察部分的知识——它超越了人类的认知范围。这种悲观的信念源于经验主义，经验主义是一种哲学学说，它认为人类的知识仅限于原则上可以经验到的事物。应用于科学领域，经验主义学说就变成了这样一种观点：科学知识的界限是由我们的观察能力决定的。因此，科学可以让我们了解化石，树木和糖晶体是存在的，但原子、电子和夸克却不存在。这种观点并非完全没有道理。因为没有人会认真怀疑化石和树木的存在，但原子和电子的存在却并非如此。正如我们在上一章中看到的，19世纪末，许多顶尖科学家确实对原子的存在表示怀疑。任何接受这种观点的人显然都必须解释，如果科学知识仅限于可观察的事物，那么为什么科学家还要提出假设不可观察实体的理论呢？反实在论者的解释是，这些理论是方便的虚构，旨在帮助预测可观察世界中事物的行为。

One motivation for anti-realism stems from the belief that we cannot actually attain knowledge of the unobservable part of reality—it lies beyond human ken. This pessimistic belief stems from empiricism, the philosophical doctrine according to which human knowledge is limited to what can in principle be experienced. Applied to science, the empiricist doctrine becomes the view that the limits to scientific knowledge are set by our powers of observation. So science can give us knowledge of fossils, trees, and sugar crystals, but not of atoms, electrons, and quarks. This view is not altogether implausible. For no one could seriously doubt the existence of fossils and trees, but the same is not true of atoms and electrons. As we saw in the last chapter, in the late 19th century many leading scientists did doubt the existence of atoms. Anyone who accepts such a view must obviously give some explanation of why scientists advance theories that posit unobservable entities, if scientific knowledge is limited to what can be observed. The explanation anti-realists give is that they are convenient fictions, designed to help predict the behaviour of things in the observable world.

现实主义者并不认为科学知识受限于我们的观察能力。相反，他们相信我们已经掌握了大量关于不可观察现实的知识。因为我们完全有理由相信我们最好的科学理论是正确的，而这些理论正是在描述不可观察的实体。例如，原子论认为所有物质都由原子构成。原子论能够解释世界上的诸多事实。现实主义者认为这是该理论正确的有力证据，也就是说，物质确实由原子构成，并且原子的行为符合该理论的描述。当然，尽管有明显的证据支持，但该理论也可能是错误的，任何理论都可能如此。仅仅因为原子不可观察，并不意味着我们就应该将原子论解释为对现实的一种描述之外的任何东西——而且很可能是一种非常成功的描述。

Realists do not agree that scientific knowledge is limited by our powers of observation. On the contrary, they believe that we already have substantial knowledge of unobservable reality. For there is every reason to believe that our best scientific theories are true, and those theories talk about unobservable entities. Consider for example the atomic theory of matter, which says that all matter is made up of atoms. The atomic theory is capable of explaining a great range of facts about the world. Realists regard this as good evidence that the theory is true, i.e. that matter really is made up of atoms which behave as the theory says. Of course the theory might be false, despite the apparent evidence in its favour, but so might any theory. Just because atoms are unobservable, that is no reason to interpret atomic theory as anything other than an attempted description of reality—and a very successful one, in all likelihood.

反实在论的另一种动机源于这样一个事实：科学理论具有一些普通世界描述所不具备的特殊性。许多科学理论构建都涉及模型的构建，这些模型通常用数学语言表达。这类模型通常会做出一些理想化的假设，这些假设在现实世界中是错误的，但为了保持模型的可操作性，这些假设又是必要的。例如，在经济学中，许多模型假设经济主体是完全理性的，并且拥有完美的……人们获取信息，并做出最大化自身效用的决策。经济学家们知道现实中的人们并非如此，但他们仍然希望自己的模型能够为现实世界的经济提供一些启示。同样，在进化生物学中，许多模型假设种群规模无限大，交配是随机的；这些假设极大地简化了数学计算。现实中没有任何种群能够满足这些假设，但生物学家们希望这些假设能够足够接近现实，从而使他们的模型具有解释力。反实在论者经常认为，科学中理想化模型的普遍存在恰恰支持了他们的观点。他们认为，将这类模型视为试图真实描述世界是毫无意义的，因为它们包含着已知为错误的假设。这类模型的目标是经验上的充分性，而非真理。

A different motivation for anti-realism stems from the fact that scientific theories have certain peculiarities which ordinary descriptions of the world do not. Much scientific theorizing involves the construction of models, often couched in mathematical language. Such models typically make idealizing assumptions that are known to be false of the real world, but are necessary to keep the model tractable. In economics, for example, many models assume that agents are perfectly rational, have perfect information, and make decisions that maximize their utility. Economists know that real people are not like this, but they hope that their models may nonetheless shed light on the real-world economy. Similarly, in evolutionary biology many models assume that the population size is infinite and that mating is random; these assumptions greatly simplify the mathematics. No real population satisfies these assumptions, but biologists hope that they are a good enough approximation to reality for their models to have explanatory power. Anti-realists often argue that the prevalence of idealized models in science supports their view. It makes no sense to regard such models as attempts to truly describe the world, they argue, since they contain assumptions known to be false. The aim of such models is empirical adequacy, not truth.

现实主义者并不认为这种论点具有决定性意义。理想化模型在科学理论中的作用并不意味着我们必须彻底否定科学追求真理的观点。相反，现实主义者认为，我们需要接受的是，这类模型的目标是近似真理，而非精确真理。例如，考虑一个气候变化的数学模型。这样的模型会包含许多简化的假设，而这些假设已知并非完全正确，例如化石燃料是二氧化碳的唯一来源。但这并不意味着该模型的目标仅仅是做出正确的预测。相反，该模型旨在对真正影响气候变化的潜在因果因素进行近似的真实描述。当然，一个好的气候变化模型应该在预测方面取得成功，但其真正的目标是设计一个尽可能准确地反映气候真实因果影响的模型。现实主义者认为，理想化模型永远无法完全真实地描述世界，但它仍然可以是一个很好的近似。

Realists do not regard this argument as decisive. The role of idealized models in scientific theorizing does not compel us to reject outright the idea that science aims at truth. Instead we need to accept that approximate truth, rather than exact truth, is the goal of such models, realists argue. Consider for example a mathematical model of climate change. Such a model will incorporate many simplifying assumptions that are known not to be exactly true, e.g. that fossil fuels are the sole source of carbon dioxide. But that does not mean that the model aims only at generating correct predictions. Rather, the model is aiming to provide an approximately true description of the hidden causal factors that actually affect climate change. Certainly a good climate change model should be predictively successful, but the real aim is to devise a model that accurately represents, as far as possible, the real causal influences on the climate. An idealized model will never be a literally true description of the world, but it may still be a good approximation, realists argue.

“没有奇迹”的论点

The ‘no miracles’ argument

许多假设存在不可观测实体的理论在经验上都取得了成功——它们对事物的预测非常准确。宏观物体的行为。气体动力学理论（详见“科学实在论与反实在论”一节）就是一个例子，类似的例子还有很多。此外，这类理论通常具有技术应用价值。例如，激光技术正是基于原子中电子从高能级跃迁到低能级时所发生现象的理论。而激光确实有效——它使我们能够矫正近视、打印高质量文本、用制导导弹攻击敌人等等。因此，支撑激光技术的理论在实践中得到了高度验证。

Many theories which posit unobservable entities are empirically successful—they make excellent predictions about the behaviour of macroscopic objects. The kinetic theory of gases, described in the section ‘Scientific realism and anti-realism’, is one example, and there are many others. Furthermore, such theories often have technological applications. For example, laser technology is based on a theory about what happens when electrons in an atom go from higher to lower energy states. And lasers work—they allow us to correct myopia, print high-quality text, attack our enemies with guided missiles, and more. The theory that underpins laser technology is therefore highly empirically successful.

假设存在不可观测实体的理论在经验上取得成功，是科学实在论的主要论据之一，即“无奇迹论证”。该论证最初由美国著名哲学家希拉里·普特南提出，它指出，如果电子和原子不存在，那么假设它们存在的理论能够做出准确的预测将是一个极其巧合的现象。如果原子和电子不存在，又该如何解释该理论与经验数据的紧密吻合呢？同样地，除非我们假设相关理论是正确的，否则又该如何解释这些理论所带来的技术进步呢？如果原子和电子仅仅是反实在论者所坚持的“方便的虚构”，那么激光又为何能够工作呢？在这种观点看来，成为反实在论者就等同于相信奇迹。既然存在非奇迹的替代方案，那么不相信奇迹就更好了，因此我们应该成为科学实在论者。

The empirical success of theories which posit unobservable entities is the basis of one of the main arguments for scientific realism, known as the ‘no miracles’ argument. Originally formulated by Hilary Putnam, a leading American philosopher, the no miracles argument says that it would be an extraordinary coincidence if a theory which posits electrons and atoms made accurate predictions unless these entities actually exist. If there are no atoms and electrons, what explains the theory’s close fit with the empirical data? Similarly, how do we explain the technological advances our theories have led to, unless by supposing that the theories in question are true? If atoms and electrons are just ‘convenient fictions’, as anti-realists maintain, then why do lasers work? On this view, being an anti-realist is akin to believing in miracles. Since it is better not to believe in miracles if a non-miraculous alternative is available, we should be scientific realists.

这种论证并非旨在证明实在论正确而反实在论错误，而是一种似是而非的论证——一种推论最佳解释的方法。需要解释的现象是，许多假设存在不可观测实体和过程的理论都获得了很高的经验成功率。无奇迹论的支持者认为，对此现象的最佳解释是这些理论是正确的——相关实体确实存在，并且其行为与理论的描述完全一致。

This argument is not intended to prove that realism is right and anti-realism wrong. Rather it is a plausibility argument—an inference to the best explanation. The phenomenon to be explained is the fact that many theories which postulate unobservable entities and processes enjoy a high level of empirical success. The best explanation of this fact, say advocates of the no miracles argument, is that the theories are true—the entities in question really exist, and behave just as the theories say.

除非我们接受这种解释，否则我们理论的实证成功就是一个无法解释的谜团。

Unless we accept this explanation, the empirical success of our theories is an unexplained mystery.

反实在论者对“没有奇迹”论点的一种回应诉诸科学史。历史上，许多科学理论在当时都取得了经验上的成功，但后来却被证明是错误的。在20世纪80年代一篇著名的文章中，美国科学哲学家拉里·劳丹列举了三十多个这样的理论，这些理论来自不同的科学领域和时代。燃素燃烧理论就是其中之一。该理论在18世纪末之前被广泛接受，它认为任何物体燃烧时都会向大气中释放一种名为“燃素”的物质。现代化学告诉我们，这是错误的：根本不存在燃素这种物质。燃烧实际上是物体与空气中的氧气发生反应的结果。尽管燃素并不存在，但燃素燃烧理论在当时却取得了相当不错的经验结果：它与当时可获得的数据吻合得相当好。

One anti-realist response to the no miracles argument appeals to the history of science. Historically, there are many examples of scientific theories which were empirically successful in their day but later turned out to be false. In a well-known article from the 1980s, the American philosopher of science Larry Laudan listed more than thirty such theories, drawn from a range of different scientific disciplines and eras. The phlogiston theory of combustion is one example. This theory, which was widely accepted until the end of the 18th century, held that when any object burns it releases a substance called ‘phlogiston’ into the atmosphere. Modern chemistry teaches us that this is false: there is no such substance as phlogiston. Rather, burning occurs when things react with oxygen in the air. But despite the non-existence of phlogiston, the phlogiston theory was empirically quite successful: it fitted the data available at the time reasonably well.

诸如此类的例子表明，支持科学实在论的“无奇迹论证”过于草率。该论证的支持者将当今科学理论的经验成功视为其真理的证据。但科学史表明，经验上成功的理论往往最终被证明是错误的。那么，我们如何确定今天的理论不会重蹈覆辙呢？例如，我们如何确定原子论不会像燃素论那样被证伪呢？反实在论者认为，一旦我们认真研究科学史，就会发现从经验成功推导出理论真理是相当站不住脚的。因此，对于原子论，理性的态度应该是不可知论——它可能是正确的，也可能是错误的。反实在论者说，我们对此一无所知。

Examples such as this suggest that the no miracles argument for scientific realism is too quick. Proponents of that argument regard the empirical success of today’s scientific theories as evidence of their truth. But the history of science shows that empirically successful theories have often turned out to be false. So how do we know that the same fate will not befall today’s theories? How do we know that the atomic theory of matter, for example, will not go the same way as the phlogiston theory? Once we pay due attention to the history of science, argue the anti-realists, we see that the inference from empirical success to theoretical truth is rather shaky. The rational attitude towards the atomic theory is thus one of agnosticism—it may be true or it may not. We just do not know, say the anti-realists.

这是对“没有奇迹”论点的有力反驳，但并非决定性的。现实主义者对此做出了回应，他们修改了这一论点。有两种修正方法。第一种修正认为，理论的经验成功表明它是近似正确的，而非精确正确的。这种较弱的论断不易被科学史上的反例所驳倒。它也更为谦逊：它允许现实主义者承认，当今的科学理论可能并非每个细节都完全正确，但仍然认为它们大体上是正确的。而且正如我们所见，现实主义者无论如何都需要近似真理的概念来解释理想化的模型。第二种修正方法涉及对“无奇迹论证”的完善，即细化经验成功的概念。一些现实主义者认为，经验成功不仅指拟合已知数据，还包括预测先前未知的新观测结果。相对于这种更为严格的经验成功标准，我们更难找到历史上那些经验上成功的理论最终被证明是错误的案例。

This is a powerful counter to the no miracles argument, but it is not decisive. Realists have responded by modifying the argument in two ways. The first modification is to claim that a theory’s empirical success is evidence that it is approximately true, rather than precisely true. This weaker claim is less vulnerable to counter examples from the history of science. It is also more modest: it allows the realist to admit that today’s scientific theories may not be correct down to every last detail, while still holding that they are broadly on the right lines. And as we have seen, the realist needs the notion of approximate truth anyway, to account for idealized models. The second modification of the no miracles argument involves refining the notion of empirical success. Some realists hold that empirical success is not just a matter of fitting the known data, but also allowing us to predict new observations that were previously unknown. Relative to this more stringent criterion of empirical success, it is less easy to find historical examples of empirically successful theories which later turned out to be false.

这些改进能否挽救“无奇迹论”尚存争议。它们确实减少了历史上的反例数量，但并未完全消除。其中一个反例是光的波动理论，该理论最初由克里斯蒂安·惠更斯于1690年提出。根据这一理论，光是由一种被称为以太的不可见介质中的波状振动构成的，而以太被认为遍布整个宇宙。（波动理论的竞争对手是牛顿所推崇的光的粒子理论，该理论认为光是由光源发射的极小粒子构成的。）直到1815年，法国物理学家奥古斯特·菲涅耳提出了该理论的数学版本，并用它来预测一些令人惊讶的新光学现象，波动理论才被广泛接受。光学实验证实了菲涅耳的预测，使许多19世纪的科学家相信光的波动理论一定是正确的。但现代物理学告诉我们，该理论是错误的：以太并不存在，因此光并非由以太中的振动构成。这又是一个错误但经验上成功的理论的例子。

Whether these refinements can save the no miracles argument is debatable. They certainly reduce the number of historical counterexamples, but not to zero. One that remains is the wave theory of light, first put forward by Christian Huygens in 1690. According to this theory, light consists of wave-like vibrations in an invisible medium called the ether, which was supposed to permeate the whole universe. (The rival to the wave theory was the particle theory of light, favoured by Newton, which held that light consists of very small particles emitted by the light source.) The wave theory was not widely accepted until the French physicist Auguste Fresnel formulated a mathematical version of the theory in 1815, and used it to predict some surprising new optical phenomena. Optical experiments confirmed Fresnel’s predictions, convincing many 19th-century scientists that the wave theory of light must be true. But modern physics tells us the theory is not true: there is no such thing as the ether, so light doesn’t consist of vibrations in it. Again, we have an example of a false but empirically successful theory.

这个例子的关键在于，它甚至反驳了修正后的“无奇迹论证”。因为菲涅耳的理论确实做出了新的预测，所以即使按照更严格的经验成功标准来看，它也算是经验上的成功。鉴于菲涅耳的理论是基于以太的概念（而以太并不存在），很难理解它如何能被称为“近似正确”。无论一个理论“近似正确”的确切含义是什么，其必要条件无疑是该理论所描述的实体确实存在。简而言之，即使按照对“近似正确”概念的严格理解，菲涅耳的理论也是经验上的成功，但它甚至连近似正确都算不上。反实在论者认为，这个故事的寓意在于，我们不应该仅仅因为现代科学理论在经验上取得了成功，就想当然地认为它们至少大致正确。

The important feature of this example is that it tells against even the modified version of the no miracles argument. For Fresnel’s theory did make novel predictions, so qualifies as empirically successful even relative to the stricter notion of empirical success. And it is hard to see how Fresnel’s theory can be called ‘approximately true’, given that it was based around the idea of the ether, which does not exist. Whatever exactly it means for a theory to be approximately true, a necessary condition is surely that the entities the theory talks about really do exist. In short, Fresnel’s theory was empirically successful even according to a strict understanding of this notion, but was not even approximately true. The moral of the story, say anti-realists, is that we should not assume that modern scientific theories are even roughly on the right lines, just because they are so empirically successful.

因此，“无奇迹论”的地位仍是一个悬而未决的问题。一方面，科学史对这一论断提出了严峻的挑战。另一方面，这一论断又具有某种直觉上的说服力。考虑到那些假设原子和电子存在的理论取得了惊人的成功，我们很难接受原子和电子可能并不存在的观点。但历史表明，无论我们当前的科学理论与数据多么吻合，我们都应该谨慎地假设它们是正确的。许多科学家过去都曾这样假设，但最终都被证明是错误的。

The status of the no miracles argument is thus an open question. On the one hand, the argument is open to serious challenge from the history of science. On the other hand, there is something intuitively compelling about the argument. It really is hard to accept that atoms and electrons might not exist when one considers the amazing success of theories which postulate these entities. But as history shows, we should be cautious about assuming that our current scientific theories are true, however well they fit our data. Many scientists have assumed that in the past and been proved wrong.

可观察/不可观察的区别

The observable/unobservable distinction

现实主义与反现实主义之争的核心在于区分可观察与不可观察之物。迄今为止，我们一直想当然地认为这种区分是理所当然的——桌椅是可观察的，原子和电子则不是。但事实上，这种区分在哲学上颇具争议。实际上，科学现实主义的主要论点之一就指出，这种区分根本无法从原则层面进行界定。

Central to the debate between realism and anti-realism is the distinction between what is observable and what is not. So far we have simply taken this distinction for granted—tables and chairs are observable, atoms and electrons are not. But in fact the distinction is quite philosophically problematic. Indeed, one of the main arguments for scientific realism says that it is not possible to draw the distinction in a principled way.

为什么这可以作为支持科学实在论的论据？因为反实在论者认为科学无法提供关于不可观测实在的知识，这预设了可观测与不可观测之间存在清晰的界限。如果事实证明这种界限无法令人满意地划分，那么反实在论显然就站不住脚了。这就是为什么科学实在论者常常热衷于强调与可观测/不可观测区分相关的种种问题。

Why should this be an argument for scientific realism? Because anti-realists hold that science cannot give us knowledge of unobservable reality, which presumes that there is a clear distinction between what can be observed and what cannot. If it turns out that this division cannot be drawn satisfactorily, then anti-realism is obviously in trouble. That is why scientific realists are often keen to emphasize the problems associated with the observable/unobservable distinction.

其中一个问题涉及观察与探测之间的关系。像电子这样的粒子在通常意义上是无法直接观测的，但我们可以使用称为粒子探测器的特殊装置来探测它们的存在。最简单的粒子探测器是云室，它由一个充满饱和水蒸气的空气的密闭容器组成（见图5）。当电子等带电粒子穿过云室时，它们会与空气中的中性原子碰撞，将原子转化为离子；水蒸气在这些离子周围凝结，形成肉眼可见的液滴。我们可以通过观察这些液滴的轨迹来追踪电子在云室中的运动路径。这是否意味着我们最终能够观测到电子呢？大多数哲学家会给出否定的答案：云室使我们能够探测到电子，而不是直接观测到它们。同样地，我们可以通过高速喷气式飞机留下的尾迹来探测它们，但观察这些尾迹并不等同于观测到喷气式飞机本身。但是，如何区分观察和探测总是很清楚的吗？

One such problem concerns the relation between observation and detection. Entities such as electrons are not observable in the ordinary sense, but their presence can be detected using special pieces of apparatus called particle detectors. The simplest particle detector is the cloud chamber, which consists of a closed container filled with air that has been saturated with water vapour (see Figure 5). When charged particles such as electrons pass through the chamber, they collide with neutral atoms in the air, converting them into ions; water vapour condenses around these ions causing liquid droplets to form, which can be seen with the naked eye. We can follow the path of an electron through the cloud chamber by watching the tracks of these liquid droplets. Does this mean that electrons can be observed after all? Most philosophers would say no: cloud chambers allow us to detect electrons, not observe them directly. In much the same way, high-speed jets can be detected by the vapour trails they leave behind, but watching these trails is not observing the jet. But is it always clear how to distinguish observing from detecting?

5.云室。

5. Cloud chamber.

在20世纪60年代初一篇著名的科学实在论辩护文章中，格罗弗·麦克斯韦向反实在论者提出了以下问题。考虑以下一系列事件：用肉眼观察某物，透过窗户观察某物，透过一副高度数的眼镜观察某物，透过双筒望远镜观察某物，透过低倍显微镜观察某物，透过……高倍显微镜等等。麦克斯韦认为这些事件处于一个平滑的连续体上。那么，我们如何决定哪些算作观察，哪些不算呢？生物学家可以观察吗？他们能否借助高倍显微镜直接观察到微生物？或者他们只能像物理学家在云室中探测电子那样探测到微生物的存在？如果某种事物只能借助精密的科学仪器才能被观察到，那么它究竟是可观测的还是不可观测的？仪器要达到何种精密程度，才能区分出“探测”和“观察”？麦克斯韦认为，这类问题没有原则性的答案，因此反实在论者试图将实体分为可观测和不可观测两类的做法是失败的。

In a well-known defence of scientific realism from the early 1960s, Grover Maxwell posed the following problem for the anti-realist. Consider the following sequence of events: looking at something with the naked eye, looking at something through a window, looking at something through a pair of strong glasses, looking at something through binoculars, looking at something through a low-powered microscope, looking at something through a high-powered microscope, and so on. Maxwell argued that these events lie on a smooth continuum. So how do we decide which count as observing and which not? Can a biologist observe micro-organisms with their high-powered microscope, or can they only detect their presence in the way that a physicist can detect the presence of electrons in a cloud chamber? If something can be only be seen with the help of sophisticated scientific instruments, does it count as observable or unobservable? How sophisticated can the instrumentation be, before we have a case of detecting rather than observing? There is no principled way of answering such questions, Maxwell argued, so the anti-realist’s attempt to classify entities as either observable or unobservable fails.

麦克斯韦的论点得到了科学家自身有时也会借助精密仪器“观察”粒子这一事实的支持。在哲学文献中，电子通常被视为不可观察实体的典型例子，但科学家们却常常乐于谈论使用粒子探测器“观察”电子。当然，这并不能证明哲学家们的观点是错误的，也不能证明电子实际上是可观察的，因为科学家们的这种说法或许更像是一种修辞手法。同样地，正如我们在第二章中所看到的，科学家们谈论某个理论的“实验证明”并不意味着实验真的能够证明理论的正确性。然而，如果真如反实在论者所坚持的那样，存在一个在哲学上重要的可观察/不可观察的区分，那么它与科学家们自身的表达方式如此不符，就显得十分奇怪了。

Maxwell’s argument is bolstered by the fact that scientists themselves sometimes talk about ‘observing’ particles with the help of sophisticated bits of apparatus. In the philosophical literature, electrons are usually taken as paradigm examples of unobservable entities, but scientists are often perfectly happy to talk about ‘observing’ electrons using particle detectors. Of course, this does not prove that the philosophers are wrong and that electrons are observable after all, for the scientists’ talk is probably best regarded as a façon de parler. Similarly, the fact that scientists talk about having ‘experimental proof’ of a theory does not mean that experiments can really prove theories to be true, as we saw in Chapter 2. Nonetheless, if there really is a philosophically important observable/unobservable distinction, as anti-realists maintain, it is odd that it corresponds so badly with the way scientists themselves speak.

麦克斯韦的论证有力，但并不具有决定性。当代反实在论的领军人物巴斯·范·弗拉森认为，麦克斯韦的论证仅仅表明“可观察的”是一个模糊的概念。模糊的概念指的是存在模糊不清的情况。“秃顶”就是一个例子。由于脱发程度不一，很多男性很难判断他们是否秃顶。但范·弗拉森指出，模糊的概念完全可以使用，并且可以在现实世界中区分不同的事物。没有人会仅仅因为“秃顶”是一个模糊的概念就认为秃顶和毛发浓密之间的区别是不真实的。模糊不清。当然，如果我们试图划出一条清晰的界限，那必然是武断的。但由于秃顶和不秃顶的男性之间存在着泾渭分明的例子，缺乏一条清晰的界限也就无关紧要了。范·弗拉森认为，“可观测”的概念也同样如此。有些实体可以被观测，例如椅子；有些实体则不能，例如夸克。麦克斯韦的论证强调了这样一个事实：也存在一些模糊不清的情况，我们无法确定这些实体是可以被观测到还是只能被探测到。因此，如果我们试图划出一条清晰的界限，那必然会带有一些武断的成分。但就像秃顶一样，这并不意味着可观测/不可观测的区分是不真实的。

Maxwell’s arguments are powerful but not decisive. Bas van Fraassen, a leading contemporary anti-realist, claims that Maxwell’s arguments only show ‘observable’ to be a vague term. A vague term is one that has borderline cases. ‘Bald’ is an example. Since hair loss comes in degrees, there are many men of whom it’s hard to say whether they are bald or not. But van Fraassen points out that vague terms are perfectly usable, and can mark genuine distinctions in the world. No one would argue that the distinction between bald and hirsute men is unreal simply because ‘bald’ is vague. Certainly, if we attempt to draw a sharp dividing line it will be arbitrary. But since there are clear-cut cases of men who are bald and men who are not, the lack of a sharp dividing line doesn’t matter. Precisely the same applies to ‘observable’, according to van Fraassen. There are clear-cut cases of entities that can be observed, for example chairs, and entities that cannot, for example quarks. Maxwell’s argument highlights the fact that there are also borderline cases, where we are unsure whether the entities in question can be observed or only detected. So if we try to draw a sharp dividing line, it will inevitably be somewhat arbitrary. But as with baldness, this does not show that the observable/unobservable distinction is unreal.
