这个论点有多强？范·弗拉森或许是对的，即存在边界案例，以及由此导致无法在不带任意性的情况下划定清晰的界限，并不能证明可观察/不可观察的区分是不真实的。从这个意义上讲，他对麦克斯韦的反驳是成功的。然而，证明可观察与不可观察之间存在真实区别是一回事，证明这种区别值得反实在论者赋予它的重要性则是另一回事。即使我们承认范·弗拉森的观点，即存在明显的不可观察实体，并且这足以让反实在论者继续推进，我们仍然需要论证为什么对不可观察的现实的认识是不可能的。

How strong an argument is this? Van Fraassen is probably right that the existence of borderline cases, and the consequent impossibility of drawing a sharp boundary without arbitrariness, does not show the observable/unobservable distinction to be unreal. To that extent, his argument against Maxwell succeeds. However, it is one thing to show that there is a real distinction between what is observable and what is not, and another to show that the distinction merits the significance that anti-realists accord it. Even if we grant van Fraassen his point that there are clear cases of unobservable entities, and that that is enough for the anti-realist to get on with, an argument is still needed for why knowledge of unobservable reality is impossible.

欠决定论证

The underdetermination argument

其中一种论点聚焦于科学家经验数据与其理论之间的关系。反实在论者强调，科学理论所依据的经验数据是关于可观察实体和过程的事实。举例来说，我们再次考虑气体动力学理论，该理论认为任何气体样本都由运动的分子组成。由于这些分子是不可观察的，我们显然无法通过直接观察各种气体样本来检验该理论。相反，我们需要……从理论中推导出一些可以直接检验的陈述，这些陈述必然是关于可观测实体的。正如我们所见，动力学理论表明，恒压下的气体样品在加热时会膨胀。这一陈述可以通过观察实验室中相关仪器的读数来直接检验。这个例子说明了一条普遍真理：关于可观测现象的事实为那些假设不可观测实体和过程的理论提供了最终数据。

One such argument focuses on the relation between scientists’ empirical data and their theories. Anti-realists emphasize that the empirical data to which scientific theories are responsible consist of facts about observable entities and processes. To illustrate, consider again the kinetic theory of gases, which says that any sample of gas consists of molecules in motion. Since these molecules are unobservable, we obviously cannot test the theory by directly observing various samples of gas. Rather, we need to deduce from the theory some statement that can be directly tested, which will invariably be about observable entities. As we saw, the kinetic theory implies that a sample of gas at constant pressure will expand when heated. This statement can be directly tested, by observing the readings on the relevant pieces of apparatus in a laboratory. This example illustrates a general truth: facts about observable phenomena provide the ultimate data for theories that posit unobservable entities and processes.

反实在论者进而认为，经验数据“不足以解释”科学家基于这些数据提出的理论。这意味着什么呢？这意味着原则上，这些数据可以用许多不同的、相互矛盾的理论来解释。以分子运动论为例，反实在论者会说，对经验数据的一种可能解释是，气体包含大量运动的分子，正如分子运动论所描述的那样。但他们坚持认为，还存在其他可能的解释，这些解释与分子运动论相冲突。因此，根据反实在论者的观点，假设存在不可观测实体的科学理论会被经验数据“不足以解释”——总会有许多相互竞争的理论能够同样很好地解释这些数据。

Anti-realists then argue that the empirical data ‘underdetermine’ the theories scientists put forward on their basis. What does this mean? It means that the data can in principle be explained by many different, mutually incompatible, theories. In the case of the kinetic theory, anti-realists will say that one possible explanation of the empirical data is that gases contain large numbers of molecules in motion, as the kinetic theory says. But they will insist that there are other possible explanations too, which conflict with the kinetic theory. So according to anti-realists, scientific theories which posit unobservable entities are underdetermined by the empirical data—there will always be a number of competing theories which can account for the data equally well.

不难理解，为何“不确定性决定论”支持反实在论的科学观。假设一位科学家相信某个关于不可观测实体的理论，理由是该理论能够解释大量的经验数据。然而，如果这些数据同样可以被其他相互矛盾的理论所解释，那么这位科学家的自信就显得毫无根据。他凭什么偏爱自己的理论而放弃其他理论呢？不确定性决定论自然而然地导向反实在论的结论：对于关于不可观测现实领域的理论，不可知论才是理性的态度。

It is easy to see why the underdetermination argument supports an anti-realist view of science. Suppose a scientist believes a given theory about unobservable entities, on the grounds that it can explain a large range of empirical data. However if the data can equally be accounted for by alternative theories, which are mutually incompatible, then the scientist’s confidence seems misplaced. For what reason does the scientist have to prefer their theory to one of the alternatives? Underdetermination leads naturally to the anti-realist conclusion that agnosticism is the rational attitude to take towards theories about the unobservable region of reality.

但反实在论者所坚持的那种观点是否真的能够用多种理论来解释经验数据呢？实在论者通常回应说，这种说法只在微不足道的意义上成立。原则上，对于给定的观测结果，总是存在不止一种可能的解释。但现实主义者认为，这并不意味着所有这些可能的解释都同样有效。例如，某个理论可能比其他理论更简单，或者更能与其他科学领域的理论相契合，或者假设的隐藏原因更少。现实主义者认为，一旦我们承认理论选择的标准不仅仅在于与数据的兼容性，那么解释不足的问题就迎刃而解了。

But is it true that the empirical data can always be explained by multiple theories, as anti-realists maintain? Realists typically reply that this is true only in a trivial sense. In principle, there will always be more than one possible explanation of a given set of observations. But, say the realists, it does not follow that all of these possible explanations are equally good. One of the theories might be simpler than the others, for example, or might fit better with theories from another area of science, or might postulate fewer hidden causes. Once we acknowledge that there are criteria for theory choice that go beyond mere compatibility with the data, the problem of underdetermination is defused, according to realists.

这种思路得到了科学史上真正意义上的“不充分决定论”案例相对较少这一事实的支持。如果像反实在论者所坚持的那样，经验数据总是能被许多不同的理论解释，那么我们理应看到科学家们几乎永远处于争论之中。但事实并非如此。实际上，当我们考察历史记录时，情况几乎与“不充分决定论”的论证所预期的完全相反。科学家们非但没有面临大量对其数据的替代解释，反而常常难以找到一个能够充分拟合数据的理论。这支持了实在论的观点，即“不充分决定论”仅仅是哲学家们的担忧，与实际的科学实践几乎毫无关联。

This line of thought is bolstered by the fact that there are relatively few real cases of underdetermination in the history of science. If the empirical data can always be explained by many different theories, as anti-realists maintain, surely we should expect to find scientists in near perpetual disagreement with one another? But that is not what we find. Indeed when we inspect the historical record, the situation is almost exactly the reverse of what the underdetermination argument would lead us to expect. Far from scientists being faced with a large number of alternative explanations of their data, they often have difficulty finding even one theory that fits the data adequately. This lends support to the realist view that underdetermination is merely a philosopher’s worry, with little relation to actual scientific practice.

反实在论者不太可能对这种回应感到满意。毕竟，哲学上的担忧仍然是合理的，即便它们的实际意义微乎其微。此外，认为可以用诸如简洁性之类的标准来评判相互竞争的理论，这立刻引出了一个棘手的问题：为什么更简单的理论就更有可能是正确的？我们在第二章中已经探讨过这个问题。

Anti-realists are unlikely to be impressed by this response. After all, philosophical worries are still genuine ones, even if their practical implications are few. Moreover, the suggestion that criteria such as simplicity can be used to adjudicate between competing theories immediately invites the awkward question of why simpler theories should be thought more likely to be true; we touched on this issue in Chapter 2.

反实在论者通常承认，在实践中可以通过诸如简洁性之类的标准来区分对数据的相互竞争的解释，从而消除不确定性。但他们否认这些标准是真理的可靠指标。简单的理论或许更便于操作，但它们本质上并不比复杂的理论更可能成立。因此，不完全决定论的论点依然成立：原则上，经验数据总是有多种解释，我们无从得知哪种解释是正确的，因此我们无法获得关于不可观察现实的知识。

Anti-realists typically grant that underdetermination can be eliminated in practice by using criteria such as simplicity to discriminate between competing explanations of our data. But they deny that such criteria are reliable indicators of the truth. Simpler theories may be more convenient to work with, but they are not intrinsically more probable than complex ones. So the underdetermination argument stands: in principle there are always multiple explanations of the empirical data, we have no way of knowing which is true, so knowledge of unobservable reality cannot be had.

然而，故事并未就此结束；现实主义者还有进一步的反驳。现实主义者指责反现实主义者选择性地运用“不确定性论证”。现实主义者认为，如果始终如一地运用这一论证，不仅会排除对不可观测世界的知识，还会排除对大部分可观测世界的知识。为了理解现实主义者为何如此认为，我们不妨注意到，许多可观测的事物实际上从未被观测到。例如，地球上绝大多数生物从未被人类观测到，但它们显然是可观测的。再比如，想想陨石撞击地球这样的事件。虽然从未有人亲眼目睹过此类事件，但它显然是可观测的。只不过恰好没有人恰好出现在正确的时间和地点。只有极小一部分可观测的事物最终被观测到。

However the story does not end here; there is a further realist comeback. Realists accuse anti-realists of applying the underdetermination argument selectively. If the argument is applied consistently, it rules out not only knowledge of the unobservable world, but also knowledge of much of the observable world, say the realists. To understand why realists say this, notice that many things that are observable never actually get observed. For example, the vast majority of living organisms on the planet never get observed by humans, but they are clearly observable. Or think of an event such as a large meteorite hitting the earth. No one has ever witnessed such an event, but it is clearly observable. It just so happens that no human was ever in the right place at the right time. Only a small fraction of what is observable actually gets observed.

关键在于此。反实在论者声称，不可观测的现实领域超出了科学知识的范畴。因此，他们承认我们可以了解那些可观测但未被观测到的物体和事件。然而，关于不可观测事物的理论，其数据不确定性并不亚于关于不可观测事物的理论。例如，假设一位科学家提出假设：1987年一颗陨石撞击了月球。他引用了各种观测数据来支持这一假设，例如，卫星拍摄的月球照片显示，月球上出现了一个1987年之前并不存在的大陨石坑。然而，原则上，这些数据可以用其他假设来解释——或许是火山爆发或地震造成了这个陨石坑。又或许是拍摄卫星照片的相机出了故障，实际上根本没有陨石坑。因此，这位科学家的假设同样无法完全被数据所证实。尽管这个假设是关于一个完全可观测的事件——陨石撞击月球。现实主义者认为，如果我们始终如一地运用不确定性论证，就不得不得出这样的结论：科学只能为我们提供关于实际观测到的事物的知识。

The key point is this. Anti-realists claim that the unobservable region of reality lies beyond the limits of scientific knowledge. So they allow that we can have knowledge of objects and events that are observable but unobserved. But theories about the unobserved are no less underdetermined by our data than theories about the unobservable. For example, suppose a scientist advances the hypothesis that a meteorite struck the moon in 1987. They cite various pieces of observational data to support this hypothesis, e.g. that satellite pictures of the moon show a large crater that wasn’t there before 1987. However, this data can in principle be explained by alternative hypotheses—perhaps a volcanic eruption caused the crater, or an earthquake. Or perhaps the camera that took the satellite pictures was faulty, and there is no crater at all. So the scientist’s hypothesis is underdetermined by the data, even though the hypothesis is about a perfectly observable event—a meteorite striking the moon. If we apply the underdetermination argument consistently, say realists, we are forced to conclude that science can only give us knowledge of things that have actually been observed.

许多科学哲学家并不认同这一结论。因为科学告诉我们的大部分内容都与尚未被观测到的事物有关——例如冰河时代、恐龙和大陆漂移。如果说我们不可能获得关于未观测事物的知识，那就等于说大多数被认为是科学知识的东西根本就不是真正的知识。科学实在论者认为这表明“未确定性论证”必然是错误的。既然科学显然能够为我们提供关于未观测事物的知识，即便我们关于未观测事物的理论受到数据的未确定性限制，那么未确定性本身就不是获得知识的障碍。因此，我们关于未观测事物的理论也受到未确定性限制这一事实，并不意味着科学无法为我们提供关于未观测事物的知识。

This conclusion is not one that many philosophers of science would accept. For much of what science tell us concerns things that have not been observed—think of ice ages, dinosaurs, and continental drift. To say that knowledge of the unobserved is impossible is to say that most of what passes for scientific knowledge is not really knowledge at all. Scientific realists take this to show that the underdetermination argument must be wrong. Since science clearly does give us knowledge of the unobserved, despite the fact that theories about the unobserved are underdetermined by our data, it follows that underdetermination is no barrier to knowledge. So the fact that our theories about the unobservable are also underdetermined does not mean that science cannot give us knowledge of the unobservable.

实际上，持这种观点的实在论者认为，不完全决定论问题不过是换了种说法的休谟归纳问题。不完全决定论意味着数据可以用其他理论来解释。但这实际上只是说数据并不蕴含理论：从数据到理论的推论是非演绎的。无论理论是关于不可观测的实体，还是关于可观测但不可观测的实体，都无关紧要——两种情况下逻辑相同。当然，证明不完全决定论证只是归纳问题的一种变体，并不意味着它可以被忽略。但这确实意味着，对于不可观测的实体，并没有什么特殊的困难。因此，实在论者认为，反实在论的立场最终是武断的。理解科学如何赋予我们关于原子和电子的知识所面临的任何难题，同样也适用于理解科学如何赋予我们关于普通宏观物体的知识。

In effect, realists who argue this way are saying that the underdetermination problem is simply Hume’s problem of induction in disguise. Underdetermination means that the data can be accounted for by alternative theories. But this is effectively just to say that the data do not entail the theory: the inference from data to theory is non-deductive. Whether the theory is about unobservable entities, or about observable but unobserved entities, makes no difference—the logic of the situation is the same in both cases. Of course, showing that the underdetermination argument is just a version of the problem of induction does not mean that it can be ignored. But it does mean that there is no special difficulty about unobservable entities. Therefore the anti-realist position is ultimately arbitrary, say the realists. Whatever problems there are in understanding how science can give us knowledge of atoms and electrons are equally problems for understanding how science can give us knowledge of ordinary macroscopic objects.

第五章

Chapter 5

科学变革和科学革命

Scientific change and scientific revolutions

科学思想变化迅速。几乎随便挑一个科学领域，你都可以肯定，该领域当前的主流理论与五十年前的理论截然不同，与一百年前的理论更是天壤之别。与其他智力活动领域相比，科学是一项快速变化的活动。许多有趣的哲学问题都围绕着科学变革展开。科学思想随时间推移而变化的方式是否存在某种可辨识的模式？当科学家放弃原有理论而接受新理论时，我们应该如何解释这种现象？后来的科学理论是否客观上优于早期的理论？

Scientific ideas change fast. Pick virtually any scientific discipline you like, and you can be sure that the prevalent theories in the discipline will be different from those of fifty years ago, and very different from those of 100 years ago. Compared with other areas of intellectual endeavour, science is a rapidly changing activity. A number of interesting philosophical questions centre on the issue of scientific change. Is there a discernible pattern to the way scientific ideas change over time? When scientists abandon their existing theory in favour of a new one, how should we explain this? Are later scientific theories objectively better than earlier ones?

现代对这些问题的讨论大多源于美国科学史学家和哲学家托马斯·库恩的著作。1963年，库恩出版了《科学革命的结构》一书，该书对后来的科学哲学产生了巨大影响。库恩的思想不仅影响了社会学和人类学等学术领域，也波及到更广泛的知识文化。（《卫报》将《科学革命的结构》列入20世纪最具影响力的100本书榜单。）为了理解库恩的思想为何会引起如此大的轰动，我们需要简要回顾一下库恩著作出版之前的科学哲学状况。

Most modern discussion of these questions takes off from the work of Thomas Kuhn, an American historian and philosopher of science. In 1963 Kuhn published a book called The Structure of Scientific Revolutions, which had an enormous influence on subsequent philosophy of science. The impact of Kuhn’s ideas has also been felt in academic disciplines such as sociology and anthropology, and in the intellectual culture at large. (The Guardian newspaper included The Structure of Scientific Revolutions in its list of the 100 most influential books of the 20th century.) To understand why Kuhn’s ideas caused such a stir, we need to look briefly at the state of philosophy of science prior to the publication of his book.

逻辑经验主义科学哲学

Logical empiricist philosophy of science

战后时期，逻辑经验主义是英语世界的主导哲学运动。最初的逻辑经验主义者是一群松散的哲学家、逻辑学家和科学家，他们在20世纪20年代和30年代初聚集在维也纳和柏林。（我们在第三章中提到的卡尔·亨佩尔与该团体关系密切，卡尔·波普尔也是如此。）为了逃避纳粹的迫害，大多数逻辑经验主义者移居美国，他们及其追随者对学术哲学产生了强大的影响，直到20世纪60年代中期，该运动才开始瓦解。

The dominant philosophical movement in the English-speaking world in the post-war period was logical empiricism. The original logical empiricists were a loosely knit group of philosophers, logicians, and scientists who gathered in Vienna and Berlin in the 1920s and early 1930s. (Carl Hempel, whom we met in Chapter 3, was closely associated with the group, as was Karl Popper.) Fleeing persecution by the Nazis, most of the logical empiricists emigrated to the United States, where they and their followers exerted a powerful influence on academic philosophy until about the mid-1960s, by which time the movement had begun to disintegrate.

逻辑经验主义者高度重视自然科学，也重视数学和逻辑。20世纪初，科学取得了令人振奋的进步，尤其是在物理学领域，这给他们留下了深刻的印象。他们的目标之一是使哲学本身更加“科学”，希望这能使哲学领域取得类似的进步。逻辑经验主义者对科学印象深刻的是其显而易见的客观性。他们认为，与其他领域（很多时候取决于研究者的主观意见）不同，科学问题可以完全客观地解决。诸如实验检验之类的技术使科学家能够将他们的理论与事实直接比较，从而对理论的优劣做出知情且公正的判断。因此，在逻辑经验主义者看来，科学是一种典型的理性活动，是通往真理的最可靠途径。

The logical empiricists had a high regard for the natural sciences and also for mathematics and logic. The early years of the 20th century witnessed exciting scientific advances, particularly in physics, which impressed them tremendously. One of their aims was to make philosophy itself more ‘scientific’, in the hope that this would allow similar advances to be made in philosophy. What impressed the logical empiricists about science was its apparent objectivity. Unlike in other fields, where much turned on the subjective opinion of enquirers, scientific questions could be settled in a fully objective way, they believed. Techniques such as experimental testing allowed a scientist to compare their theory directly with the facts, and thus reach an informed, unbiased decision about the theory’s merits. Science for the logical empiricists was thus a paradigmatically rational activity, the surest route to the truth that there is.

尽管逻辑经验主义者对科学极为推崇，但他们对科学思想史却鲜有关注。这主要是因为他们将所谓的“发现的背景”和“论证的背景”截然区分开来。“发现的背景”指的是实际的……科学家得出特定理论的历史过程。论证的背景指的是科学家在得出理论后试图证明其合理性的方法——包括检验理论、寻找相关证据以及将其与竞争理论进行比较。逻辑经验主义者认为，前者是一个主观的、心理过程，不受精确规则的约束；而后者则是一个客观的逻辑问题。他们认为，科学哲学家应该专注于研究后者。

Despite the high esteem in which they held science, the logical empiricists paid little attention to the history of scientific ideas. This was primarily because they drew a sharp distinction between what they called the ‘context of discovery’ and the ‘context of justification’. The context of discovery refers to the actual historical process by which a scientist arrives at a given theory. The context of justification refers to the means by which the scientist tries to justify the theory once they already have it—which includes testing the theory, searching for relevant evidence, and comparing it with rival theories. The logical empiricists believed that the former was a subjective, psychological process which wasn’t governed by precise rules, while the latter was an objective matter of logic. Philosophers of science should confine themselves to studying the latter, they argued.

一个例子可以帮助说明这个概念。1865年，德国化学家凯库勒发现苯分子具​​有六边形结构。据说，他是在梦中看到一条蛇试图咬自己的尾巴（见图6）后，才想到了六边形结构的假设。当然，凯库勒接下来必须……在接受他的假设之前，必须对其进行科学检验。这是一个极端的例子，但它表明科学假设的产生方式可能出人意料——它们并非总是经过深思熟虑、系统思考的结果。逻辑经验主义者认为，假设最初是如何产生的并不重要。重要的是假设产生后如何进行检验——正是这一点使科学成为一种理性活动。

An example can help illustrate this idea. In 1865 the German chemist Kekulé discovered that the benzene molecule has a hexagonal structure. Apparently, he hit on the hypothesis of a hexagonal structure after a dream in which he saw a snake trying to bite its own tail (see Figure 6). Of course, Kekulé then had to test his hypothesis scientifically before it could be accepted. This is an extreme example, but it shows that scientific hypotheses can be arrived at in the most unlikely of ways—they are not always the product of careful, systematic thought. The logical empiricists held that it makes no difference how a hypothesis is arrived at initially. What matters is how it is tested once it is already there—for it is this that makes science a rational activity.

6.凯库勒做了一个梦，梦中他看到一条蛇试图咬自己的尾巴，之后他提出了苯的六边形结构的假设。

6. Kekulé arrived at the hypothesis of the hexagonal structure of benzene after a dream in which he saw a snake trying to bite its own tail.

逻辑经验主义科学哲学中的另一个主题是理论与观察事实之间的区别；这与第四章讨论的可观察/不可观察的区分密切相关。逻辑经验主义者认为，相互竞争的科学理论之间的争论可以通过完全客观的方式解决——即将理论直接与各方都能接受的“中立”观察事实进行比较。究竟应该如何界定这组中立事实，是逻辑经验主义者争论的焦点，但他们坚信它的存在。如果理论与观察事实之间没有明确的区分，科学的理性和客观性就会受到损害，而他们坚信科学是理性和客观的。

Another theme in logical empiricist philosophy of science was the distinction between theories and observational facts; this is related to the observable/unobservable distinction discussed in Chapter 4. The logical empiricists believed that disputes between rival scientific theories could be solved in a fully objective way—by comparing the theories directly with the ‘neutral’ observational facts, which all parties could accept. How exactly this set of neutral facts should be characterized was a matter of debate among the logical empiricists, but they were adamant that it existed. Without a clear distinction between theories and observational facts the rationality and objectivity of science would be compromised, and they were resolute in their belief that science was rational and objective.

库恩的科学革命理论

Kuhn’s theory of scientific revolutions

库恩接受的是科学史方面的训练，他坚信哲学家可以从科学史研究中获益良多。他认为，对科学史关注不足导致逻辑经验主义者对科学事业形成了不准确且幼稚的认识。正如他的书名所示，库恩尤其关注科学革命——即科学领域发生巨大变革的时期，在这些时期，原有的科学思想被全新的思想所取代。例如，哥白尼在天文学领域的革命、爱因斯坦在物理学领域的革命以及达尔文在生物学领域的革命。每一次革命都导致了科学世界观的根本性转变——一套全新的思想体系推翻了原有的思想体系。

Kuhn was a historian of science by training, and firmly believed that philosophers had much to learn from studying the history of science. Insufficient attention to the history of science had led the logical empiricists to form an inaccurate and naive picture of the scientific enterprise, he maintained. As the title of his book indicates, Kuhn was especially interested in scientific revolutions—periods of great upheaval when existing scientific ideas are replaced with radically new ones. Examples include the Copernican revolution in astronomy, the Einsteinian revolution in physics, and the Darwinian revolution in biology. Each of these revolutions led to a fundamental change in the scientific worldview—the overthrow of an existing set of ideas by a completely different set.

当然，科学革命发生的频率相对较低——大多数时候，任何一门科学都处于非革命状态。库恩创造了“常规科学”一词，用来描述科学家们在其学科未经历革命性变革时所从事的日常活动。库恩对常规科学的阐述的核心是范式概念。范式包含两个主要组成部分：首先，是一套科学共同体所有成员都接受的基本理论假设；其次，是一套运用这些理论假设解决的“范例”或特定科学问题，这些问题出现在相关学科的教科书中。但范式不仅仅是一种理论（尽管库恩有时将这两个词互换使用）。当科学家们认同某种范式时，他们不仅在某些科学命题上达成共识，还就未来该领域的研究方向、需要解决的关键问题、解决这些问题的合适方法以及可接受的解决方案等问题达成一致。简而言之，范式是一种完整的科学视角——一系列共同的假设、信念和价值观，它将科学共同体凝聚在一起，并使正常的科学研究得以开展。

Of course, scientific revolutions happen relatively infrequently—most of the time any given science is not in a state of revolution. Kuhn coined the term ‘normal science’ to describe the ordinary day-to-day activities that scientists engage in when their discipline is not undergoing revolutionary change. Central to Kuhn’s account of normal science is the concept of a paradigm. A paradigm consists of two main components: first, a set of fundamental theoretical assumptions which all members of a scientific community accept; secondly, a set of ‘exemplars’ or particular scientific problems which have been solved by means of those theoretical assumptions, and which appear in the textbooks of the discipline in question. But a paradigm is more than just a theory (though Kuhn sometimes uses the words interchangeably). When scientists share a paradigm they do not just agree on certain scientific propositions, they agree also on how future research in their field should proceed, on which problems are the pertinent ones to tackle, on what the appropriate methods for solving those problems are, and on what an acceptable solution of the problems would look like. In short, a paradigm is an entire scientific outlook—a constellation of shared assumptions, beliefs, and values which unite a scientific community and allow normal science to take place.

常规科学究竟包含哪些内容？库恩认为，它本质上是一个解谜的过程。无论一个范式多么成功，它总会遇到一些问题——一些它难以解释的现象，或者理论预测与实验事实之间的不符。常规科学家的任务就是在尽可能少地改变范式的情况下，努力消除这些小的难题。因此，常规科学是一种保守的活动——它的实践者并不试图做出任何惊天动地的发现，而只是发展和扩展现有的范式。用库恩的话来说，“常规科学并不追求事实或理论的新发现，即使成功，也未必能发现任何新发现”。最重要的是，库恩强调，常规科学家并非试图检验范式。相反，他们毫不质疑地接受范式，并以此为基础开展研究。在既定的框架内。如果一位普通的科学家得到一个与既定范式相悖的实验结果，他们通常会认为是自己的实验技术出了问题，而不是范式本身错了。

What exactly does normal science involve? According to Kuhn it is primarily a matter of puzzle-solving. However successful a paradigm is, it will always encounter certain problems—phenomena which it cannot easily accommodate, or mismatches between the theory’s predictions and the experimental facts. The job of the normal scientist is to try to eliminate these minor puzzles while making as few changes as possible to the paradigm. So normal science is a conservative activity—its practitioners are not trying to make any earth-shattering discoveries, but rather just to develop and extend the existing paradigm. In Kuhn’s words, ‘normal science does not aim at novelties of fact or theory, and when successful finds none’. Above all, Kuhn stressed that normal scientists are not trying to test the paradigm. On the contrary, they accept the paradigm unquestioningly, and conduct their research within the limits it sets. If a normal scientist gets an experimental result which conflicts with the paradigm, they will usually assume that their experimental technique is faulty, not that the paradigm is wrong.

通常，一个常规科学时期会持续数十年，有时甚至数百年。在此期间，科学家们逐步完善范式——对其进行微调、补充细节并扩展其应用范围。但随着时间的推移，异常现象会被发现——无论科学家们如何努力，这些现象都无法与现有范式相符。当异常现象很少时，它们往往被忽略。但随着异常现象的积累，一种日益增长的危机感笼罩着科学界。人们对现有范式的信心开始动摇，常规科学的进程也随之停滞。这标志着库恩所说的“革命性科学”时期的开始。在这样的时期，基本的科学思想处于开放状态。各种替代旧范式的方案被提出，最终形成新的范式。通常需要一代人的时间，科学界的所有成员才能接受新的范式——这标志着一场科学革命的完成。因此，科学革命的本质是从旧的范式向新的范式转变。

Typically a period of normal science lasts many decades, sometimes even centuries. During this time scientists gradually articulate the paradigm—fine-tuning it, filling in details, and extending its range of application. But over time anomalies are discovered—phenomena which simply cannot be reconciled with the paradigm, however hard scientists try. When anomalies are few they tend to just get ignored. But as anomalies accumulate, a burgeoning sense of crisis envelops the scientific community. Confidence in the existing paradigm breaks down, and the process of normal science grinds to a halt. This marks the beginning of a period of ‘revolutionary science’ as Kuhn calls it. During such periods, fundamental scientific ideas are up for grabs. A variety of alternatives to the old paradigm are proposed, and eventually a new paradigm becomes established. A generation is usually required before all members of the scientific community are won over to the new paradigm—an event which marks the completion of a scientific revolution. The essence of a scientific revolution is thus the shift from an old paradigm to a new one.

库恩将科学史描述为漫长的常规科学时期与偶尔发生的科学革命交织在一起，这一观点引起了许多学者的共鸣。科学史上的许多例子都与库恩的描述非常吻合。例如，从托勒密天文学到哥白尼天文学的过渡，或者从牛顿物理学到爱因斯坦物理学的过渡，都体现了库恩所描述的许多特征。托勒密天文学家确实共享着一个范式，即地球静止于宇宙中心的理论，这构成了他们研究的不容置疑的背景。18、19世纪的牛顿物理学家也是如此，他们的范式建立在牛顿的力学理论之上。引力。在这两种情况下，库恩关于旧范式如何被新范式取代的描述都相当准确。当然，也有一些科学革命并不完全符合库恩的模型——例如20世纪五六十年代生物学的分子革命。但尽管如此，大多数人仍然认同库恩对科学史的描述蕴含着许多有价值的见解。

Kuhn’s characterization of the history of science as long periods of normal science punctuated by occasional scientific revolutions struck a chord with many scholars. A number of examples from the history of science fit Kuhn’s description quite well. In the transition from Ptolemaic to Copernican astronomy, for example, or from Newtonian to Einsteinian physics, many of the features that Kuhn describes are present. Ptolemaic astronomers did indeed share a paradigm, based around the theory that the earth is stationary at the centre of the universe, which formed the unquestioned back-drop to their investigations. The same is true of Newtonian physicists in the 18th and 19th centuries, whose paradigm was based around Newton’s theory of mechanics and gravitation. And in both cases, Kuhn’s account of how an old paradigm gets replaced by a new one applies fairly accurately. There are also scientific revolutions which do not fit the Kuhnian model so neatly—for example the molecular revolution in biology in the 1950s and 1960s. But nonetheless, most people agree that Kuhn’s description of the history of science contains much of value.

库恩的思想为何会引发如此轩然大波？因为除了他对科学史的描述性论述之外，库恩还提出了一些颇具争议的哲学论点。通常我们认为，科学家用新理论取代旧理论是基于证据的。但库恩认为，采纳新的范式需要科学家具备某种信念。他承认科学家可能出于正当理由放弃旧范式而选择新范式，但他坚持认为，仅凭理由永远无法理性地促成范式转变。库恩写道：“从一个范式到另一个范式的忠诚转移是一种无法强迫的皈依体验。”在解释为什么新的范式能够迅速被科学界接受时，库恩强调了科学家之间的同侪压力。如果某个范式拥有强有力的拥护者，它就更有可能获得广泛的认可。

Why did Kuhn’s ideas cause such a storm? Because in addition to his descriptive claims about the history of science, Kuhn advanced some controversial philosophical theses. Ordinarily we assume that when scientists trade their existing theory for a new one, they do so on the basis of evidence. But Kuhn argued that adopting a new paradigm involves a certain act of faith on the part of the scientist. He allowed that a scientist could have good reasons for abandoning an old paradigm for a new one, but he insisted that reasons alone could never rationally compel a paradigm shift. ‘The transfer of allegiance from paradigm to paradigm’, Kuhn wrote, ‘is a conversion experience which cannot be forced.’ And in explaining why a new paradigm rapidly gains acceptance in the scientific community, Kuhn emphasized the peer pressure of scientists on one another. If a given paradigm has very forceful advocates, it is more likely to win widespread acceptance.

库恩的许多批评者对这些论断感到震惊。因为如果范式转变真如库恩所说的那样运作，那么科学究竟如何能被视为一种理性活动就很难说了。科学家难道不应该基于证据和理性来建立信念，而不是基于信仰和同侪压力吗？面对两种相互竞争的范式，科学家难道不应该对它们进行客观比较，以确定哪一种范式拥有更多证据支持吗？经历一次“转变体验”，或者让自己被最有影响力的同行科学家说服，这显然不是一种理性的行为方式。一位批评者写道，按照库恩的说法，科学中的理论选择“完全取决于群体心理学”。

Many of Kuhn’s critics were appalled by these claims. For if paradigm shifts work the way Kuhn says, it is hard to see how science can be regarded as a rational activity at all. Surely scientists are meant to base their beliefs on evidence and reason, not on faith and peer pressure? Faced with two competing paradigms, surely the scientist should make an objective comparison of them to determine which has more evidence in its favour? Undergoing a ‘conversion experience’, or allowing oneself to be persuaded by the most forceful of one’s fellow scientists, hardly seems like a rational way to behave. One critic wrote that on Kuhn’s account, theory choice in science was ‘a matter for mob psychology’.

库恩也对科学发展的总体方向提出了一些颇具争议的观点。一种广为接受的观点认为，科学以线性方式朝着真理发展，旧的错误观念被更新的正确观念所取代。因此，后来的理论客观上优于早期的理论，科学知识也随着时间的推移而积累。这种线性累积的科学观在普通民众和科学家中都很流行，但库恩认为它既不符合历史事实，又在哲学上过于幼稚。

Kuhn also made some controversial claims about the overall direction of scientific change. According to a widely held view, science progresses towards the truth in a linear fashion, as older incorrect ideas get replaced by newer, correct ones. Later theories are thus objectively better than earlier ones, so scientific knowledge accumulates over time. This linear, cumulative conception of science is popular among laypeople and scientists alike, but Kuhn argued that it is both historically inaccurate and philosophically naive.

例如，他指出爱因斯坦的相对论在某些方面更接近亚里士多德的物理学而非牛顿物理学——因此，力学的历史并非简单的从错误到正确的线性发展。此外，库恩质疑客观真理的概念是否真的有意义。他认为，认为存在一套独立于任何特定范式的关于世界的固定事实的观点，其逻辑性值得怀疑。库恩提出了一个激进的替代方案：关于世界的事实是范式相关的，因此会随着范式的改变而改变。如果这一观点是正确的，那么询问某个理论是否与“真实存在的事实”相符，以及它是否客观正确，就毫无意义。这导致库恩拥护一种激进的反实在论科学观。

For example, he noted that Einstein’s theory of relativity is in some respects more similar to Aristotelian than Newtonian physics—so the history of mechanics is not simply a linear progression from wrong to right. Moreover, Kuhn questioned whether the concept of objective truth actually makes sense at all. The idea that there is a fixed set of facts about the world, independent of any particular paradigm, was of dubious coherence, he believed. Kuhn suggested a radical alternative: the facts about the world are paradigm-relative, and thus change when paradigms change. If this suggestion is right, then it makes no sense to ask whether a given theory corresponds to the facts ‘as they really are’, nor therefore to ask whether it is objectively true. This led Kuhn to espouse a radical form of anti-realism about science.

数据的不可通约性和理论负载性

Incommensurability and the theory-ladenness of data

库恩对这些论断提出了两个主要的哲学论证。首先，他认为相互竞争的范式通常是彼此“不可通约的”。为了理解这一观点，我们需要回顾一下，在库恩看来，科学家的范式决定了他们的整个世界观。因此，当科学革命中一个现有的范式被一个新的范式所取代时，科学家们就必须放弃他们用来理解世界的整个概念框架。事实上，库恩甚至以一种略带比喻的方式声称，在范式转变前后，科学家们“生活在不同的世界里”。不可通约性是指两种范式可能差异巨大，以至于无法进行任何直接比较——它们之间不存在可以相互翻译的共同语言。库恩认为，因此，不同范式的支持者“无法就彼此的观点进行充分的沟通”。

Kuhn had two main philosophical arguments for these claims. First, he argued that competing paradigms are typically ‘incommensurable’ with one another. To understand this idea, recall that for Kuhn a scientist’s paradigm determines their entire worldview. So when an existing paradigm is replaced by a new one in a scientific revolution, scientists have to abandon the whole conceptual framework which they use to make sense of the world. Indeed Kuhn even claims, somewhat metaphorically, that before and after a paradigm shift scientists ‘live in different worlds’. Incommensurability is the idea that two paradigms may be so different as to render impossible any straightforward comparison of them with each other—there is no common language into which both can be translated. As a result, the proponents of different paradigms ‘fail to make complete contact with each other’s viewpoints’, Kuhn claimed.

这是一个有趣但略显模糊的观点。不可通约性理论源于库恩的信念：科学概念的意义来源于它们所处的理论。例如，要理解牛顿的质量概念，我们需要理解整个牛顿理论——概念无法脱离其所嵌入的理论来解释。库恩非常重视这一观点，有时也被称为“整体论”。他认为，“质量”一词对牛顿和爱因斯坦而言实际上意义不同，因为他们各自所处的理论截然不同。这意味着牛顿和爱因斯坦实际上是在说不同的语言，这显然使比较他们的理论变得复杂。如果一位牛顿派物理学家和一位爱因斯坦派物理学家试图进行理性讨论，他们最终只会各说各话。

This is an interesting if somewhat vague idea. The doctrine of incommensurability stems from Kuhn’s belief that scientific concepts derive their meaning from the theory in which they play a role. So to understand Newton’s concept of mass, for example, we need to understand the whole of Newtonian theory—concepts cannot be explained independently of the theories in which they are embedded. This idea, which is sometimes called ‘holism’, was taken very seriously by Kuhn. He argued that the term ‘mass’ actually meant something different for Newton and Einstein, since the theories in which each embedded the term were so different. This implies that Newton and Einstein were in effect speaking different languages, which obviously complicates the attempt to compare their theories. If a Newtonian and an Einsteinian physicist tried to have a rational discussion, they would end up talking past each other.

库恩运用不可通约性论题，既反驳了范式转变完全“客观”的观点，也强化了他关于科学史的非累积性图景。传统的科学哲学认为，在相互竞争的理论之间做出选择并无太大困难——只需根据现有证据对它们进行客观比较即可。但这显然预设了一种能够表达两种理论的共同语言。如果库恩的观点——即新旧范式的支持者实际上是在各说各话——是正确的，那么任何如此简单的范式选择解释都是错误的。不可通约性同样也对传统的线性科学史图景构成挑战。如果新旧范式是不可通约的，那么认为科学史是线性的就站不住脚了。将革命视为用“正确”的观念取代“错误”的观念。因为称一种观念正确而称另一种观念错误，意味着存在一个共同的评价框架，而这恰恰是库恩所否认的。不可通约性意味着科学变革远非通往真理的直接进程，在某种意义上是无方向的：后来的范式并不比早期的范式更好，只是不同而已。

Kuhn used the incommensurability thesis both to rebut the view that paradigm shifts are fully ‘objective’, and to bolster his non-cumulative picture of the history of science. Traditional philosophy of science saw no huge difficulty in choosing between competing theories—one simply makes an objective comparison of them in the light of the available evidence. But this clearly presumes that there is a common language in which both theories can be expressed. If Kuhn is right that proponents of old and new paradigms are quite literally talking past each other, no such simplistic account of paradigm choice can be correct. Incommensurability is equally problematic for the traditional linear picture of scientific history. If old and new paradigms are incommensurable, then it cannot be correct to think of scientific revolutions as the replacement of ‘wrong’ ideas by ‘right’ ones. For to call one idea right and another wrong implies the existence of a common framework for evaluating them, which is precisely what Kuhn denies. Incommensurability implies that scientific change, far from being a straightforward progression towards the truth, is in a sense directionless: later paradigms are not better than earlier ones, just different.

库恩的不可通约性论题并未说服多少哲学家。部分原因在于，库恩还声称新旧范式互不相容。这一说法看似合理，因为如果新旧范式并不相容，也就无需在二者之间做出选择。而且在许多情况下，这种不相容性显而易见——托勒密关于行星绕地球运转的论断显然与哥白尼关于行星绕太阳运转的论断相矛盾。但正如库恩的批评者很快指出的那样，如果两个事物不可通约，那么它们就不可能互不相容。为了理解这一点，不妨考虑一下“物体的质量取决于其速度”这一命题。爱因斯坦的理论认为这一命题为真，而牛顿的理论则认为为假。但如果不可通约性理论是正确的，那么牛顿和爱因斯坦之间实际上并不存在分歧，因为这一命题对他们二人而言意义不同。只有当同一命题在两种理论中具有相同的含义时，二者之间才存在真正的冲突。既然所有人都（包括库恩）都认同爱因斯坦和牛顿的理论确实存在冲突，那么我们就有充分的理由对不可通约性论题抱持怀疑态度。

Not many philosophers were convinced by Kuhn’s incommensurability thesis. Part of the problem was that Kuhn also claimed old and new paradigms to be incompatible. This claim is plausible, for if old and new paradigms were not incompatible there would be no need to choose between them. And in many cases the incompatibility is anyway obvious—the Ptolemaic claim that the planets revolve around the earth is obviously incompatible with the Copernican claim that they revolve around the sun. But as Kuhn’s critics were quick to point out, if two things are incommensurable then they cannot be incompatible. To see why not, consider the proposition that an object’s mass depends on its velocity. Einstein’s theory says this proposition is true while Newton’s says it is false. But if the doctrine of incommensurability is right, then there is no actual disagreement between Newton and Einstein here, for the proposition means something different for each. Only if the proposition has the same meaning in both theories is there a genuine conflict between the two. Since everybody (including Kuhn) agrees that Einstein’s and Newton’s theories do conflict, this is strong reason to regard the incommensurability thesis with suspicion.

针对这一反对意见，库恩对其不可通约性论题做出了一定的修正。他认为，不同范式之间可以实现部分转换，因此新旧范式的支持者可以在一定程度上进行沟通：他们并非总是完全各说各话。但库恩仍然坚持认为，完全客观性至关重要。在不同范式之间做出选择是不可能的。因为除了缺乏共同语言导致的不可通约性之外，还存在他所谓的“标准不可通约性”。这意味着不同范式的支持者可能对一个好的范式应该具备哪些特征、应该能够解决哪些问题以及这些问题的可接受解决方案应该是什么样子等问题存在分歧。因此，即使他们能够进行有效的沟通，也无法就哪个范式更优越达成一致。用库恩的话来说，“每个范式都会被证明能够满足它自己设定的标准，但同时也会在某些方面达不到其对手设定的标准”。

In response to this objection, Kuhn moderated his incommensurability thesis somewhat. He argued that partial translation between paradigms could be achieved, so the proponents of old and new paradigms could communicate to some extent: they would not always be talking past each other entirely. But Kuhn continued to maintain that fully objective choice between paradigms was impossible. For in addition to the incommensurability deriving from the lack of a common language, there is also what he called ‘incommensurability of standards’. This is the idea that proponents of different paradigms may disagree about what features a good paradigm should have, what problems it should be able to solve, and what an acceptable solution to those problems would look like. So even if they can communicate effectively, they will not be able to reach agreement about whose paradigm is superior. In Kuhn’s words, ‘each paradigm will be shown to satisfy the criteria that it dictates for itself and to fall short of a few of those dictated by its opponent’.

库恩的第二个哲学论证基于一个被称为“数据理论负载性”的概念。为了理解这个概念，假设你是一位科学家，试图在两个相互冲突的理论中做出选择。显而易见的做法是寻找能够决定二者孰优孰劣的数据，或者进行一项能够解决问题的“关键实验”。但这只有在存在与理论完全独立（即无论科学家相信哪个理论，都可以接受这些数据）的数据时才有可能。正如我们所见，逻辑经验主义者相信存在这种理论中立的数据，它可以为相互竞争的理论提供一个客观的评判标准。但库恩认为，理论中立的理想是一种错觉——数据总是不可避免地受到理论假设的影响。他认为，不可能找到一组所有科学家无论其理论倾向如何都会接受的“纯粹”数据。

Kuhn’s second philosophical argument was based on an idea known as the ‘theory-ladenness’ of data. To grasp this idea, suppose you are a scientist trying to choose between two conflicting theories. The obvious thing to do is to look for a piece of data which will decide between them, or to perform a ‘crucial experiment’ that will settle the matter. But this will only be possible if there exist data which are suitably independent of the theories, in the sense that a scientist could accept the data whichever of the two theories they believed. As we have seen, the logical empiricists believed in the existence of such theory-neutral data, which could provide an objective court of appeal between competing theories. But Kuhn argued that the ideal of theory-neutrality is an illusion—data are invariably contaminated by theoretical assumptions. It is impossible to isolate a set of ‘pure’ data which all scientists would accept irrespective of their theoretical persuasion, he argued.

数据的理论负载性对库恩产生了两个重要后果。首先，这意味着相互竞争的范式之间的争论不能仅仅诉诸“数据”或“事实”来解决，因为科学家对数据或事实的定义取决于他们接受哪种范式。因此，在两种范式之间做出完全客观的选择是不可能的：不存在一个中立的视角来评估每种范式的主张。其次，客观真理的概念本身也受到了质疑。一个理论要成为客观真理，就必须与事实相符，但如果事实本身也受到我们理论的影响，那么这种相符性就毫无意义。正因如此，库恩才得出了这样一种激进的观点：真理本身是相对于某种范式而言的。

The theory-ladenness of data had two important consequences for Kuhn. First, it meant that a dispute between competing paradigms could not be resolved by simply appealing to ‘the data’ or ‘the facts’, for what a scientist counts as data, or facts, will depend on which paradigm they accept. Perfectly objective choice between two paradigms is therefore impossible: there is no neutral vantage-point from which to assess the claims of each. Secondly, the very idea of objective truth is called into question. To be objectively true, a theory must correspond to the facts, but the idea of such a correspondence makes little sense if the facts themselves are infected by our theories. This is why Kuhn was led to the radical view that truth itself is relative to a paradigm.

库恩为何认为所有数据都带有理论色彩？他的著作对此并未完全阐明，但至少可以辨别出两条论证思路。第一条思路是，感知深受背景信念的影响——我们所见的部分取决于我们的信念。因此，一位训练有素的科学家在实验室观察一台精密仪器时，所见与普通人所见会有所不同，因为科学家显然对仪器拥有许多普通人所不具备的信念。一些心理学实验似乎表明，感知确实会受到背景信念的影响——尽管对这些实验的正确解读仍存在争议。第二条思路是，科学家的实验和观察报告通常使用高度理论化的语言。例如，一位科学家可能会这样报告实验结果：“电流正在流过铜棒”。但这种数据报告显然包含大量理论。如果一位科学家不持有关于电流的标准信念，他就不会接受这种说法，因此它显然并非理论中立的。

Why did Kuhn think that all data are theory-laden? His writings are not totally clear on this point, but at least two lines of argument are discernible. The first is the idea that perception is heavily conditioned by background beliefs—what we see depends in part on what we believe. So a trained scientist looking at a sophisticated piece of apparatus in a laboratory will see something different from what a layperson sees, for the scientist obviously has many beliefs about the apparatus that the layperson lacks. There are a number of psychological experiments which apparently show that perception is sensitive in this way to background belief—though the correct interpretation of these experiments is a contentious matter. Secondly, scientists’ experimental and observational reports are often couched in highly theoretical language. For example, a scientist might report the outcome of an experiment by saying ‘an electric current is flowing through the copper rod’. But this data report is obviously laden with a large amount of theory. It would not be accepted by a scientist who did not hold standard beliefs about electric currents, so it is clearly not theory-neutral.

哲学家们对这些论点的优劣看法不一。一方面，许多人同意库恩的观点，即纯粹的理论中立性是无法实现的。逻辑经验主义者所设想的完全不带任何理论预设的数据陈述类型，遭到了大多数当代哲学家的反对——这在很大程度上是因为至今无人能够阐明这类陈述究竟是什么样子。但这并不意味着范式转变的客观性就此完全丧失。假设一位托勒密派天文学家和一位哥白尼派天文学家正在辩论谁的理论更优越。为了使他们的辩论更有意义，他们需要一些能够达成共识的天文数据。但是，为什么……这会是个问题吗？他们肯定能就地球和月亮在连续几个夜晚的相对位置，或者太阳升起的时间达成一致吧？显然，如果哥白尼派坚持用一种预设日心说正确的方式来描述数据，托勒密派肯定会反对。但哥白尼派完全没有理由这样做。像“5月14日，太阳早上7点10分升起”这样的陈述，无论科学家信奉地心说还是日心说，都能达成共识。这类陈述具有足够的理论中立性，足以被两种理论的支持者所接受，而这才是关键所在。

Philosophers are divided over the merits of these arguments. On the one hand, many agree with Kuhn that pure theory-neutrality is unattainable. The logical empiricist ideal of a class of data statements totally free of theoretical commitment is rejected by most contemporary philosophers—not least because no one has succeeded in saying what such statements would look like. But this need not compromise the objectivity of paradigm shifts altogether. Suppose that a Ptolemaic and a Copernican astronomer are engaged in a debate about whose theory is superior. In order for them to debate meaningfully, there needs to be some astronomical data they can agree on. But why should this be a problem? Surely they can agree about the relative position of the earth and the moon on successive nights, for example, or the time at which the sun rises? Obviously, if the Copernican insists on describing the data in a way that presumes the truth of the heliocentric theory, the Ptolemaist will object. But there is no reason why the Copernican should do that. Statements like ‘on May 14th the sun rose at 7.10 am’ can be agreed on by a scientist whether they believe the geocentric or the heliocentric theory. Such statements are sufficiently theory-neutral to be acceptable to proponents of both paradigms, which is what matters.

那么，库恩对客观真理的否定又该如何解释呢？很少有哲学家效仿库恩的做法。部分原因在于，与许多否定客观真理概念的人一样，库恩未能提出一个切实可行的替代方案。真理是范式相对的这种激进观点最终难以理解。因为与所有相对主义理论一样，它面临着一个关键问题。试想一下：真理是范式相对的这一论断本身是否客观正确？如果相对主义的支持者回答“是”，那么他们就承认了客观真理的概念是合理的，从而自相矛盾。如果他们回答“否”，那么他们就无法与持不同意见者辩论，后者认为真理并非范式相对的。并非所有哲学家都认为这个论点对相对主义来说是致命的，但这确实表明，放弃客观真理的概念说起来容易做起来难。库恩确实对科学史只是通往真理的线性发展这一传统观点提出了一些有说服力的反对意见，但他提出的相对主义替代方案并不容易被接受。

What about Kuhn’s rejection of objective truth? Few philosophers have followed Kuhn’s lead here. Part of the problem is that, like many who reject the concept of objective truth, Kuhn failed to articulate a viable alternative. The radical view that truth is paradigm-relative is ultimately hard to make sense of. For like all relativist doctrines, it faces a critical problem. Consider the question: is the claim that truth is paradigm-relative itself objectively true or not? If the proponent of relativism answers ‘yes’, then they have admitted that the concept of objective truth does make sense and thus contradicted themselves. If they answer ‘no’, then they have no grounds on which to argue with someone who disagrees and says that, in their opinion, truth is not paradigm-relative. Not all philosophers regard this argument as completely fatal to relativism, but it does suggest that abandoning the concept of objective truth is easier said than done. Kuhn certainly raised some telling objections to the traditional view that the history of science is simply a linear progression to the truth, but the relativist alternative he offered in its place is not easy to accept.

库恩与科学的理性

Kuhn and the rationality of science

《科学革命的结构》一书的写作风格激进。库恩给人的印象是，他想要取代传统的科学理论。关于理论的哲学思想在科学领域会发生根本性的转变。库恩的范式转变、不可通约性以及数据蕴含理论等理论理论似乎与逻辑经验主义将科学视为理性、客观和累积性的观点完全背道而驰。库恩的读者有理由认为，他是在说科学在很大程度上是一种非理性活动，其特点是在正常时期教条地坚持某种范式，而在革命时期则会发生突然的“转变”。

The Structure of Scientific Revolutions is written in a radical tone. Kuhn gives the impression of wanting to replace standard philosophical ideas about theory change in science with a radically different conception. His doctrines of paradigm shifts, incommensurability, and the theory-ladenness of data seem wholly at odds with the logical empiricist view of science as rational, objective, and cumulative. With some justification, Kuhn’s readers took him to be saying that science is a largely non-rational activity, characterized by dogmatic adherence to a paradigm in normal periods, and sudden ‘conversion experiences’ in revolutionary periods.

但库恩本人并不认同这种对他的著作的解读。在1970年出版的《结构》第二版的后记以及后来的著作中，库恩的语气明显缓和了许多，与他之前似乎赞同的那些更为激进的观点划清了界限。他认为，他并非试图质疑科学的理性，而是为了提供一个更现实、更符合历史的科学发展图景。逻辑经验主义者忽视了科学史，导致他们对科学运作方式的解释过于简单化，而库恩的目标正是纠正这种错误。他并非试图证明科学是非理性的，而是要更好地阐释科学理性究竟包含哪些要素。

But Kuhn himself was unhappy with this interpretation of his work. In a Postscript to the second edition of Structure published in 1970, and in subsequent writings, Kuhn moderated his tone considerably, distancing himself from the more radical views that he had seemed to endorse. He was not trying to cast doubt on the rationality of science, he argued, but rather to offer a more realistic, historically accurate picture of how science actually develops. By neglecting the history of science, the logical empiricists had been led to a simplistic account of how science works, and Kuhn’s aim was to provide a corrective. He was not trying to show that science was irrational, but rather to provide a better account of what scientific rationality involves.

一些评论家认为库恩的后记是一种180度大转弯——与其说是对其最初立场的澄清，不如说是对其最初立场的退缩。这种评价是否公正，我们在此不做探讨。但后记确实揭示了一个重要问题。为了反驳他将科学描绘成非理性的指责，库恩提出了著名的论断：科学中不存在“选择理论的算法”。这是什么意思呢？算法是一套规则，它使我们能够计算出特定问题的答案。例如，乘法算法是一套规则，当应用于任意两个数时，可以告诉我们它们的乘积。因此，理论选择的算法是一套规则，当应用于两个相互竞争的理论时，可以告诉我们应该选择哪一个。许多传统的科学哲学……逻辑经验主义者或明示或暗示地承认这种算法的存在。他们的论述常常仿佛在说，给定一组数据和两种相互竞争的理论，就可以运用“科学方法原理”来确定哪种理论更优。这种观点隐含在他们心中，他们认为发现是心理学问题，而论证则是逻辑问题。

Some commentators regard Kuhn’s Postscript as an about-turn—a retreat from his original position rather than a clarification of it. Whether this is a fair assessment is not a question we will consider here. But the Postscript did bring to light one important issue. In rebutting the charge that he had portrayed science as non-rational, Kuhn made the famous claim that there is ‘no algorithm’ for theory choice in science. What does this mean? An algorithm is a set of rules which allows us to compute the answer to a particular question. For example, an algorithm for multiplication is a set of rules which when applied to any two numbers, tells us their product. So an algorithm for theory choice is a set of rules which, when applied to two competing theories, would tell us which to choose. Much traditional philosophy of science was committed, implicitly or explicitly, to the existence of such an algorithm. The logical empiricists often wrote as if, given a set of data and two competing theories, the ‘principles of scientific method’ could be used to determine which theory was superior. This idea was implicit in their belief that although discovery was a matter of psychology, justification was a matter of logic.

库恩坚持认为科学中不存在理论选择算法，这或许是正确的。的确，至今无人成功构建出这样的算法。许多哲学家和科学家都曾就理论的选择提出过一些看似合理的建议——例如简洁性、适用范围广、与数据吻合度高等等。但正如库恩所清楚的那样，这些建议远不足以构成真正的算法。首先，理论选择往往存在权衡：理论A可能比理论B更简洁，但理论B可能更符合数据。因此，在相互竞争的理论之间做出选择时，通常需要运用主观判断或科学常识。从这个角度来看，库恩关于采纳新范式需要某种程度的信念的观点似乎并不那么激进，同样，他强调范式倡导者的说服力在决定其能否赢得科学界认可方面的重要性，也并非那么离经叛道。

Kuhn’s insistence that there is no algorithm for theory-choice in science is probably correct. Certainly no one has ever succeeded in producing such an algorithm. Lots of philosophers and scientists have made plausible suggestions about what to look for in theories—simplicity, broadness of scope, close fit with the data, and so on. But these suggestions fall short of providing a true algorithm, as Kuhn knew well. For one thing, there may be trade-offs: theory A may be simpler than theory B, but B may fit the data more closely. So an element of subjective judgement, or scientific common sense, will often be needed to decide between competing theories. Seen in this light, Kuhn’s suggestion that the adoption of a new paradigm involves a certain act of faith does not seem quite so radical, and likewise his emphasis on the persuasiveness of a paradigm’s advocates in determining its chance of winning over the scientific community.

“无算法”的观点支持了这样一种看法：库恩对范式转变的论述并非是对科学理性的攻击。因为我们可以将库恩的理解解读为对某种理性观念的否定。逻辑经验主义者实际上认为，理论选择必须遵循某种算法，否则科学变革就会被视为非理性的。这种观点并非异想天开：许多理性行为的范式转变案例确实涉及规则或算法。例如，如果你想判断某种商品在英国还是在日本更便宜，你会应用英镑兑日元的算法；任何其他试图解决这个问题的方法都是非理性的。同样，如果一位科学家试图在两种相互竞争的理论之间做出选择，人们很容易认为唯一理性的方法是应用理论选择算法。因此，如果……既然似乎并不存在这样的算法，我们就面临两种选择。要么我们可以得出结论：科学变革是非理性的；要么我们可以得出结论：理性运作的概念要求过高。库恩在其后期的著作中赞同后一种选择。他所阐述的道理并非范式转变是非理性的，而是我们需要一种更为宽松、务实的理性概念来理解它们。

The ‘no algorithm’ idea lends support to the view that Kuhn’s account of paradigm shifts is not an assault on the rationality of science. For we can read Kuhn instead as rejecting a certain conception of rationality. The logical empiricists believed, in effect, that there must be an algorithm for theory-choice on pain of scientific change being irrational. This is not a crazy view: many paradigm cases of rational action do involve rules or algorithms. For example, if you want to decide whether a good is cheaper in England or Japan, you apply an algorithm for converting pounds into yen; any other way of trying to decide the matter is irrational. Similarly, if a scientist is trying to decide between two competing theories, it is tempting to think that the only rational way to proceed is to apply an algorithm for theory-choice. So if it turns out that there is no such algorithm, as seems likely, we have two options. Either we can conclude that scientific change is irrational or that the conception of rationality at work is too demanding. In his later writings Kuhn endorses the latter option. The moral of his story is not that paradigm shifts are irrational, but rather that a more relaxed, pragmatic concept of rationality is required to make sense of them.

库恩的遗产

Kuhn’s legacy

尽管库恩的思想颇具争议，但它彻底改变了科学哲学。部分原因是库恩质疑了许多传统上被视为理所当然的假设，迫使哲学家们正视它们；部分原因是他关注了一系列传统科学哲学所忽略的问题。在库恩之后，哲学家可以忽视科学史的观点以及发现与论证之间泾渭分明的二元论都显得越来越站不住脚。当代科学哲学家比库恩之前的先辈们更加关注科学的历史发展。即使是那些对库恩较为激进的观点持保留态度的人也会承认，在这些方面，他的影响是积极的。

Despite their controversial nature, Kuhn’s ideas transformed philosophy of science. In part this is because Kuhn called into question many assumptions that had traditionally been taken for granted, forcing philosophers to confront them, and in part because he drew attention to a range of issues that traditional philosophy of science had simply ignored. After Kuhn, the idea that philosophers could afford to ignore the history of science appeared increasingly untenable, as did the idea of a sharp dichotomy between the contexts of discovery and justification. Contemporary philosophers of science pay much greater attention to the historical development of science than did their pre-Kuhnian ancestors. Even those unsympathetic to Kuhn’s more radical ideas would accept that in these respects his influence has been positive.

库恩著作的另一项重要影响在于，它将人们的注意力集中到科学发生的社会背景上，而这正是传统科学哲学所忽略的。在库恩看来，科学本质上是一种社会活动：一个由共同范式维系的科学共同体的存在，是正常科学实践的先决条件。库恩还非常关注学校和大学的科学教学方式、年轻科学家如何融入科学共同体、科学成果如何发表以及其他类似的“社会学”问题。不出所料，库恩的思想对科学社会学家产生了深远的影响。尤其值得一提的是……在科学社会学领域被称为“强纲领”的运动，于 20 世纪 70 年代和 80 年代在英国兴起，很大程度上要归功于库恩。

Another important impact of Kuhn’s work was to focus attention on the social context in which science takes place, something that traditional philosophy of science ignored. Science for Kuhn is an intrinsically social activity: the existence of a scientific community, bound together by allegiance to a shared paradigm, is a prerequisite for the practice of normal science. Kuhn also paid considerable attention to how science is taught in schools and universities, how young scientists are initiated into the scientific community, how scientific results are published, and other such ‘sociological’ matters. Not surprisingly, Kuhn’s ideas have been influential among sociologists of science. In particular, a movement known as the ‘strong programme’ in the sociology of science, which emerged in Britain in the 1970s and 1980s, owes much to Kuhn.

强纲领的核心理念是，科学应被视为其所处社会环境的产物。强纲领社会学家对这一理念进行了字面解读：他们认为科学家的信念在很大程度上是由社会因素决定的。例如，为了解释科学家为何相信某个理论，他们会引用科学家的社会和文化背景。他们坚持认为，科学家自身相信该理论的理由永远不足以解释其原因。强纲领借鉴了库恩的诸多观点，包括数据的理论负载性、科学本质上是一种社会活动的观点，以及不存在客观的理论选择算法。但强纲领社会学家比库恩更为激进，也更为不谨慎。他们公开否定真理和理性的概念，认为这些概念在意识形态上存在问题，并对传统的科学哲学抱有极大的怀疑。这导致了科学哲学家和社会学家之间持续存在的某种紧张关系。

The strong programme was based around the idea that science should be viewed as a product of the society in which it is practised. Strong programme sociologists took this idea literally: they held that scientists’ beliefs were in large part socially determined. So to explain why a scientist believes a given theory, for example, they would cite aspects of the scientist’s social and cultural background. The scientist’s own reasons for believing the theory were never explanation enough, they maintained. The strong programme borrowed a number of themes from Kuhn, including the theory-ladenness of data, the view of science as an essentially social activity, and the idea that there is no objective algorithm for theory-choice. But strong programme sociologists were more radical than Kuhn, and less cautious. They openly rejected the notions of truth and rationality, which they regarded as ideologically suspect, and viewed traditional philosophy of science with great suspicion. This led to a certain amount of tension between philosophers and sociologists of science, which continues to this day.

更广泛地说，库恩的著作对人文和社会科学领域社会建构主义的兴起产生了影响。社会建构主义认为，某些现象，例如种族类别，是“社会建构”，而非具有独立于意识的客观存在。鉴于库恩强调科学的社会背景，并否定科学理论“与客观事实相符”的观点，我们很容易理解为什么有人会认为科学是一种“社会建构”。然而，这里存在某种讽刺意味。因为那些支持科学是“社会建构”观点的人通常持有反科学态度，他们常常反对现代社会赋予科学的权威。但库恩本人却是一位坚定的科学拥护者。与逻辑经验主义者一样，他认为现代社会是科学的基石。科学是一项令人叹为观止的智力成就。他提出的范式转变、常规科学与革命性科学、不可通约性以及理论负载性等理论，并非意在削弱或批判科学事业，而是为了帮助我们更好地理解它。

Further afield, Kuhn’s work has played a role in the rise of social constructionism in the humanities and social sciences. Social constructionism is the idea that certain phenomena, e.g. racial categories, are ‘social constructs’, as opposed to having an objective mind-independent existence. Given Kuhn’s emphasis on the social context of science, and his rejection of the idea that scientific theories ‘correspond to the objective facts’, it is easy to see why he could be read as saying that science is a ‘social construct’. However there is a certain irony here. For proponents of the idea that science is a ‘social construct’ have typically had an anti-scientific attitude, often objecting to the authority accorded to science in modern society. But Kuhn himself was strongly pro-science. Like the logical empiricists, he regarded modern science as a hugely impressive intellectual achievement. His doctrines of paradigm shifts, normal and revolutionary science, incommensurability, and theory-ladenness were not intended to undermine or criticize the scientific enterprise, but rather to help us understand it better.

第六章

Chapter 6

物理学、生物学和心理学中的哲学问题

Philosophical problems in physics, biology, and psychology

我们目前研究的问题——推理、解释、实在论和科学变革——都属于所谓的“科学哲学”范畴。这些问题关注的是科学研究的本质，而非具体到化学或地质学等学科。然而，也存在一些有趣的哲学问题，它们特指某些特定科学——这些问题属于所谓的“特殊科学哲学”范畴。这些问题通常部分依赖于哲学思考，部分依赖于经验事实，这正是它们引人入胜之处。本章我们将探讨三个这样的问题，分别来自物理学、生物学和心理学。

The issues we have studied so far—inference, explanation, realism, and scientific change—belong to what is called ‘general philosophy of science’. These issues concern the nature of scientific investigation in general, rather than pertaining specifically to chemistry, say, or geology. However, there are also interesting philosophical questions that are specific to particular sciences—they belong to what is called ‘philosophy of the special sciences’. These questions usually depend partly on philosophical considerations and partly on empirical facts, which is what makes them so interesting. In this chapter we examine three such questions, one each from physics, biology, and psychology.

莱布尼茨与牛顿关于绝对空间的争论

Leibniz versus Newton on absolute space

我们首先要探讨的是戈特弗里德·莱布尼茨（1646-1716）和艾萨克·牛顿（1642-1727）这两位17世纪杰出的科学思想家之间关于空间和时间本质的辩论。在《自然哲学原理》中，牛顿捍卫了一种所谓的“绝对主义”空间观。根据这种观点，空间具有凌驾于物体间空间关系之上的“绝对”存在。牛顿将空间视为一个三维容器，上帝在创世之初将物质宇宙置于其中。这意味着空间先于任何物质对象而存在，就像一个容器，例如一个麦片盒。在放入任何麦片之前，空间就已经存在了。根据牛顿的说法，空间与普通容器（例如麦片盒）之间的唯一区别在于，后者具有有限的尺寸，而空间则向各个方向无限延伸。

Our first topic is a debate between Gottfried Leibniz (1646–1716) and Isaac Newton (1642–1727), two of the outstanding scientific intellects of the 17th century, concerning the nature of space and time. In his Principles of Natural Philosophy, Newton defended what is called an ‘absolutist’ conception of space. According to this view, space has an ‘absolute’ existence over and above the spatial relations between objects. Newton thought of space as a three-dimensional container into which God placed the material universe at creation. This implies that space existed before there were any material objects, just as a container like a cereal box exists before any pieces of cereal are put inside. The only difference between space and ordinary containers like cereal boxes, according to Newton, is that the latter have finite dimensions whereas space extends infinitely in every direction.

莱布尼茨强烈反对绝对主义的空间观，以及牛顿哲学中的许多其他观点。他认为，空间仅仅是物质对象之间所有空间关系的总和。例如，“上方”、“下方”、“左侧”和“右侧”都是空间关系——它们是物质对象彼此之间的联系。这种“关系主义”的空间观意味着，在任何物质对象出现之前，空间并不存在。莱布尼茨认为，空间是在上帝创造物质宇宙时才出现的；它并非预先存在，等待被物质对象填充。因此，将空间视为容器，甚至将其视为任何形式的实体，都是不恰当的。我们可以用一个类比来理解莱布尼茨的观点。例如，一份法律合同是由双方（例如房屋的买卖双方）之间的关系构成的。如果其中一方死亡，那么合同就终止了。因此，如果说合同独立于买卖双方的关系而存在，那就太荒谬了——合同本身就是这种关系。同样，空间也仅仅是物体之间空间关系的体现。

Leibniz strongly disagreed with the absolutist view of space, and with much else in Newton’s philosophy. He argued that space consists simply of the totality of spatial relations between material objects. Example of spatial relations are ‘above’, ‘below’, ‘to the left of’, and ‘to the right of’—they are relations that material objects bear to each other. This ‘relationist’ conception of space implies that before there were any material objects, space did not exist. Leibniz argued that space came into existence when God created the material universe; it did not exist beforehand, waiting to be filled up with material objects. So space is not usefully thought of as a container, nor indeed as an entity of any sort. Leibniz’s view can be understood in terms of an analogy. A legal contract consists of a relationship between two parties—the buyer and seller of a house, for example. If one of the parties dies, then the contract ceases to exist. So it would be crazy to say that the contract has an existence independently of the relationship between buyer and seller—the contract just is that relationship. Similarly, space is nothing over and above the spatial relations between objects.

牛顿引入绝对空间概念的主要目的是为了区分相对运动和绝对运动。相对运动是指一个物体相对于另一个物体的运动。就相对运动而言，询问一个物体是否“真正”在运动是没有意义的——我们只能问它相对于其他物体是否在运动。举例来说，想象两个慢跑者沿着一条笔直的道路并排奔跑。相对于路边的旁观者，他们都在运动——他们正逐渐远离。但相对于彼此而言，这两个慢跑者并没有运动——只要他们继续朝着同一个方向慢跑，他们的相对位置就保持不变。速度相同。因此，一个物体相对于一个物体可能处于相对运动状态，但相对于另一个物体则可能处于静止状态。

Newton’s main reason for introducing the concept of absolute space was to distinguish relative from absolute motion. Relative motion is the movement of one object with respect to another. So far as relative motion is concerned, it makes no sense to ask whether an object is ‘really’ moving or not—we can only ask whether it is moving with respect to something else. To illustrate, imagine two joggers running in tandem along a straight road. Relative to a bystander on the road side, both are in motion—they are getting further away by the moment. But relative to each other, the joggers are not in motion—their relative positions remain exactly the same, so long as they keep jogging in the same direction at the same speed. So an object may be in relative motion with respect to one thing but be stationary with respect to another.

牛顿认为，除了相对运动之外，还存在绝对运动。常识也支持这一观点。想象一下两个相对运动的物体——比如一架滑翔机和一个地球上的观察者。相对运动是对称的：正如滑翔机相对于地球上的观察者运动一样，观察者相对于滑翔机也在运动。但直觉上，我们肯定会问：究竟是观察者还是滑翔机在“真正”运动？如果是这样，我们就需要绝对运动的概念了。

Newton believed that as well as relative motion, there is also absolute motion. Common sense supports this view. Imagine two objects in relative motion—say a hang-glider and an observer on the earth. Now relative motion is symmetric: just as the hang-glider is in motion relative to the observer on the earth, so the observer is in motion relative to the hang-glider. But intuitively, it surely makes sense to ask whether the observer or the hang-glider is ‘really’ the one moving? If so, then we need the concept of absolute motion.

但究竟什么是绝对运动呢？根据牛顿的说法，它是物体相对于绝对空间的运动。牛顿认为，在任何时刻，每个物体在绝对空间中都有一个特定的位置。如果一个物体在绝对空间中的位置随时间发生变化，那么它就是在做绝对运动；否则，它就是在做绝对运动。因此，我们需要将空间视为一个独立于物质对象之间关系的实体，才能区分相对运动和绝对运动。请注意，牛顿的论证基于一个重要的假设，即所有运动都必须相对于某个事物。相对运动是相对于其他物质对象的运动；绝对运动是相对于绝对空间本身的运动。因此，从某种意义上说，即使是绝对运动对牛顿而言也是“相对的”。实际上，牛顿假设运动状态，无论是绝对运动还是相对运动，都不能是物体本身的“客观事实”；它只能是物体与其他事物之间关系的客观事实。这个“其他事物”可以是另一个物质对象，也可以是绝对空间本身。

But what exactly is absolute motion? According to Newton, it is the motion of an object with respect to absolute space. Newton thought that at any time, every object has a particular location in absolute space. If an object changes its location in absolute space over time then it is in absolute motion; otherwise, it is at absolute rest. So we need to think of space as an entity, over and above the relations between material objects, in order to distinguish relative from absolute motion. Notice that Newton’s reasoning rests on an important assumption, namely that all motion has got to be relative to something. Relative motion is motion relative to other material objects; absolute motion is motion relative to absolute space itself. So in a sense, even absolute motion is ‘relative’ for Newton. In effect, Newton is assuming that being in motion, whether absolute or relative, cannot be a ‘brute fact’ about an object; it can only be a fact about the object’s relations to something else. That something else can either be another material object, or it can be absolute space.

莱布尼茨承认相对运动和绝对运动之间存在区别，但他否认后者应该被解释为相对于绝对空间的运动。因为他认为绝对空间的概念是不连贯的。他为此观点提出了许多论证，其中许多都与神学有关。从哲学角度来看，莱布尼茨最有趣的论点是，绝对空间与他所谓的“不可辨识事物同一性原则”（PII）相冲突。由于莱布尼茨认为这一原则毋庸置疑，因此他否定了绝对空间的概念。

Leibniz accepted that there was a difference between relative and absolute motion, but denied that the latter should be explained as motion with respect to absolute space. For he regarded the concept of absolute space as incoherent. He had a number of arguments for this view, many of which were theological. From a philosophical viewpoint, Leibniz’s most interesting argument was that absolute space conflicts with what he called the principle of the identity of indiscernibles (PII). Since Leibniz regarded this principle as indubitably true, he rejected the concept of absolute space.

同一性原理（PII）认为，如果两个物体无法区分，那么它们就是同一的，也就是说，它们实际上是同一个物体。称两个物体无法区分，意味着它们之间没有任何区别——它们拥有完全相同的属性。因此，如果同一性原理为真，那么任何两个真正不同的物体必然在某些属性上有所不同——否则它们就应该是一个物体，而不是两个。同一性原理在直觉上相当有说服力。当然，要找到两个属性完全相同的不同物体的例子并不容易——即使是两个批量生产的工厂商品，通常也会在无数方面存在差异。同一性原理是否普遍成立是一个复杂的问题，哲学家们至今仍在争论；答案部分取决于“属性”的定义，部分取决于量子物理学中的一些难题。但就目前而言，我们关注的是莱布尼茨如何运用这一原理。

PII says that if two objects are indiscernible then they are identical, i.e. they are really one and the same object. To call two objects indiscernible is to say that no difference at all can be found between them—they have exactly the same attributes. So if PII is true, then any two genuinely distinct objects must differ in some attribute—otherwise they would be one, not two. PII is intuitively quite compelling. It is certainly not easy to find an example of two distinct objects which share all their attributes—even two mass-produced factory goods will normally differ in innumerable ways. Whether PII is true in general is a complex question that philosophers still debate; the answer depends in part on exactly what counts as an ‘attribute’, and in part on difficult issues in quantum physics. But for the moment our concern is the use to which Leibniz puts the principle.

莱布尼茨运用两个思想实验揭示了牛顿绝对空间理论与PII之间的冲突。首先，莱布尼茨让我们想象两个不同的宇宙，它们都包含完全相同的物体。在宇宙一中，每个物体都占据绝对空间中的一个特定位置。在宇宙二中，每个物体都被移动到了绝对空间中的另一个位置，例如向东移动两公里。我们根本无法区分这两个宇宙。因为正如牛顿自己承认的那样，我们无法直接观测物体在绝对空间中的位置。我们所能观测的只是物体彼此之间的相对位置，而这两个宇宙中的相对位置是相同的。任何观测或实验都无法揭示我们究竟生活在宇宙一还是宇宙二中。

Leibniz uses two thought experiments to reveal a conflict between Newton’s theory of absolute space and PII. Firstly, Leibniz asks us to imagine two different universes, both containing exactly the same objects. In universe one, each object occupies a particular location in absolute space. In universe two, each object has been shifted to a different location in absolute space, two kilometres to the east (for example). There would be no way of telling these two universes apart. For we cannot observe the position of an object in absolute space, as Newton himself admitted. All we can observe are the positions of objects relative to each other, and these are the same in both universes. No observations or experiments could ever reveal whether we lived in universe one or two.

莱布尼茨的第二个思想实验与之类似。回想一下，对于牛顿来说，有些物体在绝对空间中运动，而其他物体则处于静止状态。这意味着在每个时刻，每个物体都具有确定的绝对速度。（速度是指物体在给定方向上的速率，因此物体的绝对速度是指它在绝对空间中沿特定方向运动的速率。）现在想象两个不同的宇宙，它们都包含完全相同的物体。在宇宙一中，每个物体都具有特定的绝对速度。在宇宙二中，每个物体的绝对速度都被提高了一个固定值，例如沿特定方向提高了300公里/小时。同样，我们永远无法区分这两个宇宙。因为我们无法观察物体相对于绝对空间的运动速度，正如牛顿所承认的那样，而只能观察物体彼此之间的相对运动速度——而这两个宇宙中的相对速度是相同的。

Leibniz’s second thought experiment is similar. Recall that for Newton, some objects are moving through absolute space while others are at rest. This means that at each moment, every object has a definite absolute velocity. (Velocity is speed in a given direction, so an object’s absolute velocity is the speed at which it moves through absolute space in a specified direction.) Now imagine two different universes, both containing exactly the same objects. In universe one, each object has a particular absolute velocity. In universe two, the absolute velocity of each object has been boosted by a fixed amount, say 300 kilometres per hour in a specified direction. Again, we could never tell these two universes apart. For we cannot observe how fast an object is moving with respect to absolute space, as Newton admitted, but only observe how fast objects are moving relative to each other—and these are the same in both universes.

在这些思想实验中，莱布尼茨描述了两个宇宙，而牛顿自己也承认我们永远无法区分这两个宇宙——它们完全无法区分。但根据PII（完全不可区分性假设），这意味着这两个宇宙实际上是同一个宇宙。因此，如果PII为真，那么牛顿的理论就产生了一个错误的推论：它暗示存在两个事物，而实际上只有一个。因此，莱布尼茨认为，牛顿的理论是错误的。

In each of these thought experiments, Leibniz describes two universes which by Newton’s own admission we could never tell apart—they are perfectly indiscernible. But by PII, this means that the two universes are actually one. So if PII is true, then Newton’s theory has a false consequence: it implies that there are two things when there is only one. Therefore Newton’s theory is false, Leibniz argues.

实际上，莱布尼茨认为绝对空间是一个空洞的概念，因为它在观测上没有任何意义。如果物体在绝对空间中的位置以及它们相对于绝对空间的速度都无法被探测到，那么我们又为何要相信绝对空间的存在呢？莱布尼茨援引了一个相当合理的原则：只有当不可观测实体的存在能够产生我们可以观测到的影响时，我们才应该在科学中假设它们的存在。

In effect, Leibniz is arguing that absolute space is an empty notion because it makes no observational difference. If neither the location of objects in absolute space nor their velocity with respect to absolute space can ever be detected, why believe in absolute space at all? Leibniz is appealing to the quite reasonable principle that we should only postulate unobservable entities in science if their existence would make a difference that we can detect observationally.

但牛顿认为他可以证明绝对空间确实会对观测产生影响。这就是他著名的“旋转水桶”论证的要点。他让我们想象一个装满水的水桶，用一根穿过桶底小孔的绳子悬挂着（见图7）。最初，水相对于水桶是静止的。绳子被缠绕数圈后松开。随着绳子展开，水桶开始旋转。起初，桶里的水保持静止，水面平坦；此时水桶相对于水旋转。但片刻之后，水桶的运动传递给了水，水开始与水桶同步旋转；此时，水桶和水再次相对静止。经验表明，此时水面两侧会向上弯曲。

But Newton thought he could show that absolute space did have observational effects. This is the point of his famous ‘rotating bucket’ argument. He asks us to imagine a bucket full of water, suspended on a rope threaded through a hole in its base (see Figure 7). Initially the water is at rest relative to the bucket. The rope is then twisted around a number of times and released. As it uncoils, the bucket starts rotating. At first the water in the bucket stays still, its surface flat; the bucket is then rotating relative to the water. But after a few moments the bucket imparts its motion to the water, and the water begins to rotate in tandem with the bucket; the bucket and water are then at rest relative to each other again. Experience shows that the surface of the water then curves upwards at the sides.

7.牛顿的“旋转水桶”实验。阶段（i）水桶和水静止；阶段（ii）水桶相对于水旋转；阶段（iii）水桶和水同步旋转。

7. Newton’s ‘rotating bucket’ experiment. Stage (i) bucket and water are at rest; stage (ii) bucket rotates relative to water; stage (iii) bucket and water rotate in tandem.

牛顿问道：是什么导致水面上升？显然，这与水的旋转有关。但旋转是一种运动，而对牛顿来说，物体的运动总是相对于其他事物而言的。因此，我们必须追问：水是相对于什么旋转的？显然不是相对于水桶，因为水桶和水是同步旋转的，因此它们处于相对静止状态。牛顿认为，水是相对于绝对空间旋转的，正是这种旋转导致水面向上弯曲。所以，绝对空间确实会对观测结果产生影响。

What is causing the surface of the water to rise, Newton asks? Clearly it is something to do with the water’s rotation. But rotation is a type of motion, and for Newton an object’s motion is always relative to something else. So we must ask: relative to what is the water rotating? Not relative to the bucket, obviously, for the bucket and water are rotating in tandem and are hence at relative rest. Newton argues that the water is rotating relative to absolute space, and that this is causing its surface to curve upwards. So absolute space does in fact have observational effects.

你或许认为牛顿的论证存在明显的漏洞。诚然，水相对于水桶没有旋转，但为什么就此得出结论说它一定相对于绝对空间在旋转呢？水相对于实验者、地球表面以及恒星都在旋转，那么这些因素中的任何一个都可能导致水面上升吗？然而，牛顿对此有一个简单的回应。想象一个宇宙，其中除了旋转的水桶之外什么都没有。在这样的宇宙中，我们无法通过水相对于其他物体的旋转来解释水面的弯曲，因为那里没有其他物体，而且水相对于水桶仍然是静止的。水唯一可能相对于其旋转的物体就是绝对空间。因此，我们必须相信绝对空间的存在，否则就无法解释水面为何会弯曲。

You may think there is an obvious gap in Newton’s argument. Granted the water is not rotating relative to the bucket, but why conclude that it must be rotating relative to absolute space? The water is rotating relative to the person doing the experiment, and relative to the earth’s surface, and relative to the fixed stars, so surely any of these might be causing its surface to rise? However Newton had a simple response to this move. Imagine a universe containing nothing except the rotating bucket. In such a universe, we cannot explain the water’s curved surface by appealing to the water’s rotation relative to other objects, for there are none, and as before the water is at rest relative to the bucket. Absolute space is the only thing left for the water to be rotating relative to. So we must believe in absolute space on pain of being unable to explain why the water’s surface curves.

实际上，牛顿的意思是，虽然物体相对于绝对空间的位置和速度永远无法被直接探测，但它相对于绝对空间的加速度却是可以探测的。因为当一个物体旋转时，即使旋转速率恒定，根据定义它也是加速的。这是因为在物理学中，加速度被定义为速度的变化率，而速度是指物体在给定方向上的快慢。由于旋转物体的运动方向不断变化，它们的速度并非恒定不变，因此它们就是在加速运动。水面的曲面就是所谓的“惯性效应”的一个例子——惯性效应是由加速运动产生的效应。另一个例子是飞机起飞时被推向座椅靠背的感觉。牛顿认为，惯性效应的唯一可能解释是，经历这些效应的物体相对于绝对空间的加速度。因为在一个只包含加速物体的宇宙中，绝对空间是唯一能够解释加速度的参照物。

In effect, Newton is saying that although an object’s position and velocity with respect to absolute space can never be detected, its acceleration with respect to absolute space is detectable. For when an object rotates then it is by definition accelerating, even if the rate of rotation is constant. This is because in physics, acceleration is defined as the rate of change of velocity, and velocity is speed in a given direction. Since rotating objects are constantly changing their direction of motion, their velocity is not constant, hence they are accelerating. The water’s curved surface is just one example of what are called ‘inertial effects’—effects produced by accelerated motion. Another example is the feeling of being pushed to the back of your seat when an aeroplane takes off. The only possible explanation of inertial effects, Newton believed, is the acceleration of the object experiencing those effects with respect to absolute space. For in a universe containing only the accelerating object, absolute space is the only thing that the acceleration could be relative to.

牛顿的论证很有力，但并非结论性的。因为，如果旋转水桶实验是在一个没有任何其他物质的宇宙中进行的，牛顿又如何知道水面会向上弯曲呢？牛顿只是假设，我们在现实世界中观察到的惯性效应，在一个没有任何物质的世界中仍然会保持不变。

Newton’s argument is powerful but not conclusive. For how does Newton know that the water’s surface would curve upwards, if the rotating bucket experiment were done in a universe containing no other material objects? Newton simply assumes that the inertial effects we find in this world would remain the same in a world bereft of any other matter.

这显然是一个相当大的假设，许多人质疑牛顿是否有资格做出这样的假设。因此，牛顿的论证并不能证明绝对空间的存在。相反，它向莱布尼茨理论的捍卫者提出了挑战，要求其对惯性效应提供另一种解释。

This is obviously quite a substantial assumption, and many people have questioned Newton’s entitlement to it. So Newton’s argument does not prove the existence of absolute space. Rather, it lays down a challenge to the defender of Leibniz to provide an alternative explanation of inertial effects.

莱布尼茨还面临着如何在不引入绝对空间的情况下解释绝对运动和相对运动区别的挑战。针对这个问题，莱布尼茨写道，当物体运动的直接原因是物体自身时，该物体就处于真运动或绝对运动状态。回想一下滑翔机和地球上的观察者，它们都相对于对方运动。为了确定谁“真正”在运动，莱布尼茨认为我们需要判断运动的直接原因（即相对运动）是在滑翔机上还是在观察者身上。这种区分绝对运动和相对运动的方法完全避免了提及绝对空间，但并不十分清晰。莱布尼茨从未真正解释过“运动的直接原因”在物体内部究竟意味着什么。但他或许意在反驳牛顿的假设，即物体的运动，无论是相对运动还是绝对运动，都只能反映物体与其他事物之间的关系。

Leibniz also faces the challenge of explaining the difference between absolute and relative motion without invoking absolute space. On this problem, Leibniz wrote that a body is in true or absolute motion ‘when the immediate cause of the change is in the body itself’. Recall the case of the hang-glider and the observer on earth, both in motion relative to the other. To determine who is ‘really’ moving, Leibniz would say that we need to decide whether the immediate cause of the change (i.e. the relative motion) is in the hang-glider or the observer. This suggestion for how to distinguish absolute from relative motion avoids all reference to absolute space, but it is not very clear. Leibniz never properly explains what it means for the ‘immediate cause of the change’ to be in an object. But it may be that he intended to reject Newton’s assumption that an object’s motion, whether relative or absolute, can only be a fact about the object’s relations to something else.

绝对空间与相对空间之争最引人入胜之处在于它始终挥之不去。牛顿的空间理论与他的物理学密不可分，而莱布尼茨的观点则是对牛顿理论的直接回应。因此，人们或许会认为，自17世纪以来物理学的进步应该已经解决了这个问题。然而事实并非如此。尽管人们一度普遍认为爱因斯坦的相对论已经使莱布尼茨的观点胜出，但近年来这种观点受到了越来越多的质疑。在牛顿与莱布尼茨最初的论战300多年后，这场争论仍在继续。

One of the intriguing things about the absolute/relational controversy is that it refuses to go away. Newton’s account of space was intimately bound up with his physics, and Leibniz’s views were a direct reaction to Newton’s. So one might think that advances in physics since the 17th century would have resolved the issue. But this has not happened. Although it was once widely held that Einstein’s theory of relativity had decided the issue in favour of Leibniz, this view has increasingly come under attack in recent years. More than 300 years after the original Newton/Leibniz exchange, the debate continues.

什么是生物物种？

What are biological species?

科学家常常希望将他们研究的对象归类为不同的种类或类型。地质学家将岩石分为火成岩、根据形成方式的不同，元素可分为沉积岩或变质岩。化学家根据元素的物理和化学性质，将其分为金属、类金属和非金属。分类的主要功能是传递信息。如果化学家告诉你某种物质是金属，这就能让你对它的性质有大致的了解。分类引发了一些有趣的哲学问题。这些问题主要源于这样一个事实：一组给定的物体原则上可以用多种不同的方式进行分类。那么，我们应该如何选择呢？是否存在一种“正确”的分类方法？或者说，所有的分类方案最终都是任意的？在生物分类学的背景下，这些问题显得尤为重要，而生物分类学正是我们本文的关注点。

Scientists often wish to classify the objects they are studying into general kinds or types. Geologists classify rocks as igneous, sedimentary, or metamorphic, depending on how they were formed. Chemists classify elements as metals, metalloids, or non-metals, depending on their physical and chemical attributes. The main function of classification is to convey information. If a chemist tells you that something is a metal, this tells you a lot about its likely behaviour. Classification raises some interesting philosophical issues. Mostly, these stem from the fact that a given set of objects can in principle be classified in many different ways. So how should we choose between them? Is there a ‘correct’ way to classify, or are all classification schemes ultimately arbitrary? These questions take on a particular urgency in the context of biological classification or taxonomy, which will be our concern here.

生物分类的基本单位是物种。在传统分类学中，每个生物首先被归入一个物种，物种名称由拉丁文两部分组成，称为二项式。因此，你属于智人（Homo sapiens），你的宠物猫属于猫（Felis catus），你食品储藏室里的老鼠属于小家鼠（Mus musculus）。然后，物种按照层级顺序排列到“更高级别的分类单元”——属、科、目、纲、门和界。因此，智人（ Homo sapiens）属于人属（Homo），人属又属于人科（Hominid）、灵长目（Primate）、哺乳纲（Mammalia）、脊索动物门（Chordate）和动物界（Animal）。这种分类系统被称为林奈系统，以其发明者——18世纪瑞典博物学家卡尔·林奈（Carl Linnaeus，1707-1778）的名字命名，至今仍被广泛使用。

The basic unit of biological classification is the species. In traditional taxonomy each organism is first assigned to a species, denoted by a Latin name with two parts called a binomial. Thus you belong to Homo sapiens, your pet cat to Felis catus, and the mouse in your larder to Mus musculus. Species are then arranged into ‘higher taxa’—genus, family, order, class, phylum, and kingdom—in a hierarchical fashion. Thus Homo sapiens is in the Homo genus, which is in the Hominid family, the Primate order, the Mammalian class, the Chordate phylum, and the Animal kingdom. This system of classification is called the Linnean system, named after the 18th-century Swedish naturalist Carl Linnaeus (1707–78) who invented it, and is still widely used today.

本文将重点讨论分类学家任务的第一阶段，即如何将生物体归类到物种。这远比看起来复杂，主要是因为生物学家对于物种的真正定义以及物种鉴定的标准尚未达成共识。事实上，现代生物学中充斥着各种相互竞争的物种定义，或者说“物种概念”。这种缺乏共识的情况有时被称为“物种问题”。

Our focus here will be on the first stage of the taxonomist’s task, namely how to assign organisms to species. This is less straightforward than it may seem, primarily because biologists do not agree on what a species actually is, nor therefore on what criteria should be used for identifying species. Indeed competing definitions of a biological species, or ‘species concepts’ as these definitions are known, abound in modern biology. This lack of consensus is sometimes called ‘the species problem’.

你或许会惊讶地发现，物种问题确实存在。从普通人的角度来看，将生物归类为物种似乎并没有什么问题。毕竟，即使是粗略的观察也能清楚地看出，生物体并非千篇一律。有些生物体型庞大，有些则非常微小；有些会移动，有些则不会；有些能活数年，有些则只能存活几个小时。同样显而易见的是，这种多样性并非连续的，而是呈聚集分布的。生物体似乎可以归入若干离散的类型或种类，其中许多类型甚至连小孩子都能识别。一个三岁的孩子可以自信地判断公园里的两只动物都是狗，即使它们的品种不同；而生物学家也会证实孩子的判断是正确的——这些动物确实属于同一物种，即家犬（Canis familiaris）。因此，人们自然会认为生物体之间存在客观的界限，而生物学家的职责就是发现这些界限。在这种观点看来，物种的边界存在于世界之中，等待着人们去发现，而不是由生物学家强加于世界的。大多数非生物学家似乎都毫不质疑地接受这种观点。

You may be surprised to hear that there is a species problem. From a layperson’s perspective, there seems nothing very problematic about assigning organisms to species. After all, it is clear from even casual observation that living organisms are not all alike.
